introSummary: The right IB tutor in Gurgaon has taught the exact International Baccalaureate (IB) stage and subject your child is in, marks work against IB criteria rather than chapter-end answers, and can offer home tuition or online lessons at a time that survives school timings and evening traffic. A child in the Primary Years Programme (PYP) usually needs a patient generalist. Middle Years Programme (MYP) students need someone fluent in criterion-based tasks, while Diploma Programme (DP) students need a subject specialist who knows Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) demands, the Internal Assessment (IA) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK). This guide covers how the stages differ, the subjects that cause most trouble, how home, online and hybrid lessons compare across Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana, and how IB Gram matches tutors.

contentBlocks.heading: How Do You Find and Trial an IB Tutor in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Start with a precise request. Tell IB Gram the programme, subjects and levels, the school calendar, your sector and the slots your child can keep. IB Gram then shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and who match those needs, a demo or trial session can be arranged, and you decide only after seeing how the tutor works with your child.

Precision decides the quality of the shortlist. A message saying 'need IB tutors in Gurgaon for my son' could describe a Grade 3 child working through units of inquiry or a DP2 student weeks away from the May session. Compare it with this one: DP1, Maths AA at HL, weak on proof, IA topic not yet chosen, free after 5.30 pm on Tuesdays and Thursdays, Sector 57. The second message rules out most tutors before anyone picks up the phone. That is the point.

The demo is where the real decision gets made. Give the tutor something real to work on: a unit test your child found hard, a criterion comment nobody explained, a past question left blank. Watch whether the tutor asks your child to talk through their thinking before correcting it. Afterwards, ask your child on their own whether they would sit through another hour with this person. Teenagers are blunt about this, and they are usually right.

Choose the mode next (home, online or hybrid, compared further down) and agree a review point at four weeks before lessons begin. Decide too whether the tutor reports to you or to the student, since many DP students want to own that relationship. If the fit is wrong at the demo or at the review, ask IB Gram for a different match and say precisely what did not work. 'Rushed through HL content without checking understanding' leads to a far better second shortlist than 'not great'.
items: 1. Send IB Gram a query or book a free consultation.
2. Share programme, subjects, levels, school calendar, sector and weekly slots.
3. Get a shortlist of tutors with verified profiles who match, subject to availability.
4. Run a demo or trial session on a real piece of marked work.
5. Choose home, online or hybrid lessons and set a four-week review.
6. At the review, continue or ask for a different match.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: What Each Stage Asks of a Tutor
contentBlocks.body:
Read this as a table in prose. The PYP runs from ages 3 to 12 and has no external examinations. Learning is organised around six transdisciplinary themes, from Who we are to Sharing the planet, through units of inquiry, alongside the ten attributes of the IB learner profile, and students complete the PYP exhibition in the final year. An IB PYP tutor in Gurgaon is rarely there to push content ahead; the useful work is reading, number sense and the confidence to ask questions.

The MYP covers MYP 1 to 5, roughly ages 11 to 16, across eight subject groups. Every subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored 0-8, and the criterion total out of 32 converts to a final 1-7 grade through IB grade boundaries. So an IB MYP tutor in Gurgaon needs a different skill from a content coach: teaching to the criterion, not the chapter. The Community Project comes in MYP 3 or 4 and the Personal Project in MYP 5. MYP eAssessment in MYP 5, with on-screen examinations and ePortfolios, is optional, and each school decides whether to offer it.

The DP is a two-year course, DP1 and DP2, of six subjects from six groups. Three or four are taken at HL, with 240 recommended teaching hours each, and the rest at SL, with 150. Each subject is graded 1-7, TOK and the Extended Essay (EE) together add up to 3 more points, and Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) must also be completed. An IB DP tutor in Gurugram is usually hired per subject, and the HL and SL gap is wide enough to ask which level the tutor has taught recently.

Many families first look for help at the seams between stages. A child moving from PYP into MYP 1 has to get used to criteria. An MYP 5 student juggles the Personal Project and DP subject choices. And a DP1 student from another board finds a strong Class 10 mark does not carry over.
items: PYP, ages 3-12: no external examinations; the exhibition comes in the final year.
MYP: four criteria per subject, scored 0-8 each, out of 32 in total.
MYP 5: Personal Project, and eAssessment only if the school offers it.
DP: three or four HL subjects at 240 hours, the rest SL at 150.

contentBlocks.heading: Which IB Subjects Do Gurgaon Students Most Often Need Help With?
contentBlocks.body:
Among Gurgaon DP students, most requests are for Maths AA or AI at HL, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Economics and English A. The reasons differ: HL Maths moves fast, the sciences pair dense content with practical work, Economics marks down vague evaluation, and English A expects written analysis that many keen readers have never been taught to produce.

Maths needs a paragraph of its own. An IB Maths tutor in Gurgaon usually meets two kinds of HL student in DP1. One chose HL because a university course seemed to require it, and is discovering that 240 recommended teaching hours is a great deal of mathematics. The other is capable but was trained to reach answers by routine, and drops marks whenever a question asks them to show, justify or interpret. AA and AI are different courses, so a tutor who is strong in one is not automatically right for the other. Ask.

An IB Physics tutor in Gurgaon often finds the difficulty sits in the mathematics inside the physics: rearranging equations, reading graphs, handling units. Chemistry and Biology help tends to be requested partway through DP1, when new content and practical work build up in the same weeks. Economics students frequently understand the theory yet write answers that describe where they should evaluate, and the tutor's job is to make them commit to a judgement and support it. English A catches out students who read widely, because it rewards a written argument about how a text works rather than evidence of having enjoyed it.

In the MYP, requests usually concern mathematics or the sciences, but the underlying issue is the same across groups: correct work that does not show what the criterion asks for. For a DP student, one subject is normally the right place to start, and a second is worth adding only once the first is clearly working.
items: Maths AA or AI at HL: pace, proof and justification, not just answers.
Physics: rearranging, graphs and units often cost more marks than concepts.
Chemistry and Biology: new content and practical work peak together in DP1.
Economics: from describing theory to a supported, committed evaluation.
English A: turning close reading into structured written argument.

contentBlocks.heading: School Calendars That Shape IB Tutoring in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
An IB tutor in Gurgaon who ignores your child's school calendar wastes sessions, so get the calendar first. Internal dates vary, and the calendar at Pathways World School need not match the one at Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, The Shri Ram School, Aravali or Heritage Xperiential Learning School. Ask your child's coordinator for the year's assessment dates and pass them to the tutor. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

For DP families, the fixed points are the exam sessions. May is the session most Gurgaon IB schools use, with May results released in early July, and a November session also exists. Everything else is set internally: draft dates for IA work, the TOK exhibition and essay, the Extended Essay and school mocks. Picture a student taking Chemistry and Biology at HL who finds two IA drafts and a TOK deadline landing in the same fortnight. A tutor who had seen that calendar months earlier would have spread the load.

MYP 5 has its own squeeze. The Personal Project runs alongside ordinary criterion-assessed tasks, and where the school offers MYP eAssessment, on-screen examinations and ePortfolios add another layer. In the final PYP year, the exhibition is not an examination, and the most useful help at home is organisation, not extra content.

Exam preparation is a subject in itself, and it belongs to the months before the May session: mocks, past papers, markschemes and timed practice. Here it is enough to say that a tutor hired in DP1 should already be building the habits that make that run-in calmer, such as answering exactly what the command term asks. Families who start in DP2 can still get real help. They simply have fewer weeks to spread it over.
items: DP exams: May is the session most Gurgaon IB schools use; results arrive in early July.
IA, TOK and Extended Essay draft dates come from the school; check each.
Share mock dates early so lessons shift from new content to review in time.
PYP final year: the exhibition needs organisation at home, not extra worksheets.

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or Hybrid: What Suits an IB Student in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Home lessons suit younger children and students who need someone beside them to stay on task. Online lessons give the widest choice of subject specialists and no travel. Hybrid pairs a weekly home session with online follow-up. For most DP students across Gurgaon, the real choice is specialist fit against face-to-face accountability.

Put plainly, an IB home tutor in Gurgaon gives you accountability and handwritten work checked on the spot, but limits you to tutors who can reach your sector at your slot. An IB online tutor in Gurugram can be the right specialist regardless of where they live, but the student has to manage their own attention through a screen. Hybrid recovers most of both, at the cost of more coordination. None of the three is better in general. Each is better for a particular child.

Stage and address decide it together. A PYP child in DLF Phase 3 or Sector 45 is usually better off at home, because young children tend to drift in front of a screen. An MYP 4 student in Sector 49 on the Sohna Road corridor might start at home and move online once the routine is set. A DP2 student in Sector 108 on Dwarka Expressway, or in Sector 84 in New Gurgaon, who needs an HL Chemistry specialist is better served by a strong online tutor than by a weaker home tutor chosen for distance.

Online lessons deserve a fair hearing, because parents often rule them out too early. Discussion-heavy TOK work, feedback on a shared IA draft and most DP Maths lose little when a session is well run. What online cannot replace is presence. For a student who drifts, hides a phone under the desk or needs someone to watch them write a timed answer, a home lesson on Golf Course Road or in Palam Vihar is worth the extra planning.
items: Home: best for PYP children and students needing in-person accountability; limited by travel.
Online: widest choice of DP specialists and no traffic; needs a student who self-manages.
Hybrid: weekly home lesson plus online follow-up; flexible, but needs more coordination.
Mode can change later, subject to tutor availability.

contentBlocks.heading: Verified Profiles, and the Checks Only a Parent Can Make
contentBlocks.body:
Every tutor on an IB Gram shortlist has a verified profile. Treat that as a filter, not a verdict. A profile, however carefully checked, cannot show you how a tutor explains an unfamiliar idea to a nervous sixteen-year-old, or whether they notice that a quiet MYP 2 child has stopped following. Only the demo, and your own questions, can show you that.

Ask any IB tutor in Gurgaon direct questions, and expect direct answers. Which IB programmes, subjects and levels has the tutor taught in the last two years? How do they use criteria and markschemes when they correct work? What would the first few sessions look like, based on your child's latest marked test? For IA, TOK and Extended Essay drafts, where do they draw the line between questioning and feedback, which is legitimate, and rewriting, which is not? A tutor who hesitates on that last question is not the right person for DP coursework.

Parents often ask for the best IB tutor in Gurgaon. There is no such person in general, only the best fit for one student at one moment. A tutor with long DP experience may be wrong for an anxious MYP 3 child who needs patience more than depth, while a younger tutor who took Maths AA at HL recently can sometimes explain it more clearly to a DP1 student a few weeks behind. Ask the tutor what they would do if your child's marks had not moved after a month. A thoughtful answer is a better sign than a confident promise.

For home lessons, settle the basics before day one. Agree that lessons happen in a shared room rather than a bedroom, and that an adult is at home when the student is young. None of this signals distrust. Experienced tutors expect it, and a tutor who objects has told you something useful.
items: Ask which IB programme, subject and level the tutor has taught most recently.
Confirm the tutor guides IA, TOK and EE drafts without writing any part.
Hold home lessons in a shared room, with an adult at home for young children.
Agree how, and how often, the tutor will report progress to you.

contentBlocks.heading: What Does an IB Tutor Do That a CBSE or ICSE Tutor Usually Cannot?
contentBlocks.body:
An IB tutor teaches to the way IB work is judged: against criteria and command terms rather than a single expected answer, with internally assessed work such as the TOK exhibition counting towards the grade. A strong CBSE or ICSE tutor may know the content thoroughly and still coach answers that score poorly under IB marking.

Criterion-based marking is the first difference. Because MYP work is scored criterion by criterion, an accurate answer that never attempts what a criterion rewards earns little under it. Picture a student who joins in MYP 4 from a board school, hands in full, correct paragraphs and gets a disappointing score, because nothing shows the reasoning the task asked for. An experienced IB tutor reads the criteria before the question, and trains the student to do the same.

Command terms are the second. Describe, explain, discuss and evaluate ask for different things, and a student taught to write down everything they know answers none of them precisely. Then comes the work that is not an exam at all. A good IB tutor can comment on an IA draft without writing a word of it, and knows how TOK is assessed: an internally assessed exhibition built on three objects and one of 35 IA prompts, capped at 950 words and worth a third of the TOK grade, plus an externally assessed essay of up to 1,600 words on one of six prescribed titles, worth the other two thirds. An E in either TOK or the EE is a failing condition.

Coaching centres raise a related question. A batch designed for CBSE, JEE or NEET moves through a common syllabus at one pace, which rarely suits a room where each student has a different mix of HL and SL subjects. For most subject help, one-to-one IB tuition in Gurgaon, or an IB private tutor in Gurugram working from your child's own marked work, is the simpler place to begin.
items: Criterion-based marking: read what each criterion rewards before starting the task.
Command terms: explain, discuss and evaluate each demand a different kind of answer.
TOK exhibition: three objects tied to one of 35 IA prompts, up to 950 words.
TOK essay: one of six prescribed titles, up to 1,600 words, externally assessed.

contentBlocks.heading: What Progress Should You Expect After Four Weeks?
contentBlocks.body:
After four weeks you should see changed habits, not necessarily a new grade: your child can explain what recent lessons fixed, marked work repeats the same errors less often, and the tutor can name specific gaps with a plan for each. Grades tend to follow later, once the next assessed task comes round.

Make the four-week review concrete. Sit down with the tutor and your child, and ask for evidence rather than impressions: one topic before and after, an answer rewritten to match its command term, an IA plan that has actually moved. A DP1 student in Maths AI at SL, for instance, should by now be setting out working so that a marker can follow it, even if the unit test mark has not shifted. An MYP 3 student should be able to point to the criterion a piece of work was aimed at.

Some limits are better heard early. No tutor can guarantee a grade, a 7 or a diploma score, and anyone who does is selling something. A student who starts a few months before the May session can gain real ground in one or two papers but cannot rebuild two years of foundations. And not every student needs a tutor. A DP student who is organised, asks teachers questions and is scoring where they want may be better served by protected study time than by another weekly session.

If week four shows nothing, find out why before changing anything. Missed sessions, homework that never gets done and a tutor who spends the hour re-teaching the school lesson are different problems with different fixes. A month also shows whether your child dreads the session or looks forward to it, which matters more than parents expect. Where attendance and effort are fine and the problem is the fit, ask IB Gram for a different match and pass on what you learned.
items: Your child can explain, in their own words, what recent sessions fixed.
The same error type shows up less often in newly marked school work.
The tutor names specific gaps and a written plan, not general encouragement.
Good attendance but no change: discuss the fit, then request a different match.

contentBlocks.heading: Getting Started With an IB Tutor in Gurgaon: What to Prepare
contentBlocks.body:
Before you send a query, gather a few things. Collect the latest school report, any criterion or markscheme feedback, and the subject list with HL or SL marked, plus the internal assessment calendar if the coordinator has shared one. For a DP student, add which subjects have an IA under way and how far each draft has got. Then write down your sector or society and the slots your child can really keep once school buses, activities and homework are counted, not the slots that look free on paper.

The first session with a new IB tutor in Gurgaon is mostly diagnosis. A good tutor looks at a recent marked paper or task, asks your child to talk through a couple of answers, and works out whether marks are being lost on content, method or the way answers are written. Expect a short plan at the end: which topics come first, what homework will look like and when you will next review progress. For a PYP child the first session is gentler, often reading together or working a number problem aloud while the tutor watches how they think. Keep your own notes from that session, since they become the baseline for the four-week review.

Fees are usually the first question, and the honest answer is that they depend on the programme stage, subject and level, the tutor's experience, session length and whether lessons are at home or online. Ask about the fee for each option on your shortlist before you commit to regular lessons, so you compare real arrangements instead of guessing. How those factors add up across DP1 and DP2 is a conversation of its own.

If your child is about to start DP1 or MYP 1, the weeks before term are the easiest time to run a demo, because nothing is overdue yet.
items: Latest school report plus any criterion or markscheme feedback from teachers.
Subject list with HL or SL marked, and each IA's current draft status.
Your sector or society, gate process and the weekly slots your child can keep.
One recent marked test or task for the tutor to diagnose at the demo.

faqs.question: Does my child need an IB tutor, or can a CBSE or ICSE tutor manage?
faqs.answer: For MYP and DP work, a tutor with genuine IB experience is usually the better choice, because IB marking rewards different things from board exams. A CBSE or ICSE tutor can be excellent on content, and for a PYP child's reading or times tables that may be enough. The trouble starts when work is judged against criteria and command terms: a tutor unfamiliar with those can make a student more accurate and no better on the report.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the IA, TOK and Extended Essay without doing the work?
faqs.answer: Yes, and any tutor who offers to write part of it should be turned down. Legitimate help means asking questions that sharpen a research focus, explaining what a criterion rewards and pointing out where an argument is thin. The words, data and decisions must be the student's own. That protects integrity and the result, since an E in TOK or the Extended Essay is a failing condition. Ask the tutor, before lessons begin, how they give feedback on a draft.

faqs.question: It has been a month and nothing has improved. Is it the tutor or my child?
faqs.answer: It can be either, so check attendance, homework and the tutor's plan before deciding. If sessions were missed or homework skipped, the tutor has had little to work with, and that is a family conversation first. If your child turned up and did the work but the tutor cannot name specific gaps or show changed habits in marked work, the fit is the likelier problem. Then ask IB Gram for a different match and explain what was missing.

faqs.question: The tutor is not working out. Can we switch without starting over?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can ask IB Gram for a different match whenever the fit is wrong, and what you learned from the first tutor shortens the second search. Be specific: pace, explanation style, punctuality, too much lecturing or too little practice. Share notes and marked work from the sessions so far, so the next tutor does not repeat the diagnosis. A demo with the new tutor can be arranged first, subject to availability. Nobody needs to feel awkward asking.

faqs.question: We live in Sector 84. Will a home tutor come on weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: Possibly, depending on the subject, the level and which suitable tutors are free at your slot. In New Gurgaon sectors such as 84, and on Dwarka Expressway in sectors such as 106, evening traffic can stretch what looks like a short trip, so weekday home lessons need realistic timing. For an HL specialist, one workable pattern is a weekend home lesson with an online session midweek; another is going fully online. Tell IB Gram your society and slots at the start.

faqs.question: Can one home tutor teach two siblings at different IB stages?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but it is rarely the best arrangement once one child reaches the DP. The tutor who suits a PYP child's reading and number work is seldom the person you want for HL Physics. Where both children are in the MYP and need the same subject, one tutor can work well, and back-to-back home lessons in a society such as Ireo Skyon or Malibu Towne save a second visit. Otherwise, match each need separately.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram work with my child's school or teachers?
faqs.answer: No, IB Gram is independent of every school, and the tutor works only from what your family chooses to share. That usually means task sheets, criteria, marked work, teacher comments and the internal calendar. If a teacher suggests, say, that a student practise longer written answers, pass it on and the tutor can build it into the plan. Questions about deadlines, subject changes or assessment rules belong with your child's coordinator, because only the school can answer them accurately.

faqs.question: Can a tutor guarantee a 7 or a particular diploma score?
faqs.answer: No tutor can guarantee a grade, a 7 or a diploma score, and a promise of one is a reason to look elsewhere. The final result depends on exam performance, internally assessed work and two years of the student's own effort, none of which a tutor fully controls. What a good tutor can offer is a clear diagnosis, a plan and honest feedback on whether it is working. Judge them on that, starting at the four-week review.

faqs.question: We are moving to Gurugram from an IB school abroad. Can a tutor help with the switch?
faqs.answer: Yes, and help is most useful in the first term, while the student adjusts to a new school's calendar and teachers. The programme stays the IB, but internal deadlines, topic order and teacher expectations can all differ. A tutor can compare what was covered before with what the new class is doing, and close gaps before they surface in marked work. If you are still choosing between, say, DLF Phase 4 and Sector 67, tell IB Gram early so lessons fit the move.

faqs.question: What if my teenager does not want a tutor?
faqs.answer: Involve them in the choice, because a DP student who had no say in picking a tutor rarely engages with one. Let your child read the shortlist, take part in the demo and tell you afterwards whether it helped. Start with the subject they worry about most, not the one you worry about most. If a tutor feels like a sign of failure, framing it as help with one IA can change that. After a fair trial, a firm no is worth respecting for a while.

The tutor who suits a PYP child's reading and number work is seldom the person you want for HL Physics. Where both children are in the MYP and need the same subject, one tutor can work well, and back-to-back home lessons in a society such as Ireo Skyon or Malibu Towne save a second visit. Otherwise, match each need separately.

mainEntity.name: Does IB Gram work with my child's school or teachers?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, IB Gram is independent of every school, and the tutor works only from what your family chooses to share. That usually means task sheets, criteria, marked work, teacher comments and the internal calendar. If a teacher suggests, say, that a student practise longer written answers, pass it on and the tutor can build it into the plan. Questions about deadlines, subject changes or assessment rules belong with your child's coordinator, because only the school can answer them accurately.

mainEntity.name: Can a tutor guarantee a 7 or a particular diploma score?

acceptedAnswer.text: No tutor can guarantee a grade, a 7 or a diploma score, and a promise of one is a reason to look elsewhere. The final result depends on exam performance, internally assessed work and two years of the student's own effort, none of which a tutor fully controls. What a good tutor can offer is a clear diagnosis, a plan and honest feedback on whether it is working. Judge them on that, starting at the four-week review.

mainEntity.name: We are moving to Gurugram from an IB school abroad. Can a tutor help with the switch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and help is most useful in the first term, while the student adjusts to a new school's calendar and teachers. The programme stays the IB, but internal deadlines, topic order and teacher expectations can all differ. A tutor can compare what was covered before with what the new class is doing, and close gaps before they surface in marked work. If you are still choosing between, say, DLF Phase 4 and Sector 67, tell IB Gram early so lessons fit the move.

mainEntity.name: What if my teenager does not want a tutor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Involve them in the choice, because a DP student who had no say in picking a tutor rarely engages with one. Let your child read the shortlist, take part in the demo and tell you afterwards whether it helped. Start with the subject they worry about most, not the one you worry about most. If a tutor feels like a sign of failure, framing it as help with one IA can change that. After a fair trial, a firm no is worth respecting for a while.

finalCta: Send a query or book a free consultation with the programme, subjects, levels, school calendar, your sector and preferred slots. IB Gram asks any follow-up questions, then shortlists tutors with verified profiles who match, subject to availability. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit, lessons run at home, online or hybrid, and you can ask for a different match if the fit is wrong.

heroSubtitle: A sector-by-sector guide for International Baccalaureate (IB) families: which parts of Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana a home tutor can realistically reach on weekday evenings, how society gate rules and parking affect the slot, and when an online specialist is a smarter choice than the closest available tutor.
introSummary: If you typed "IB tutor near me Gurgaon", you are probably looking for home tuition: a tutor with a verified profile who teaches your child at home, in your own sector or society. Whether a nearby home tutor is realistic depends on your corridor, your child's programme stage and your evening slot, and a tutor two sectors away can still be the wrong person for Diploma Programme (DP) Higher Level (HL) Physics. IB Gram asks where you live, which school calendar you follow, the subject and level, and when your child is free, then shortlists tutors who can reach your home or, failing that, teach online or hybrid, subject to tutor availability. This page covers all ten Gurgaon corridors, from DLF Phase 5 and Sohna Road to New Gurgaon and Dwarka Expressway, and explains how gate entry, weekday traffic and a mid-year move change the plan.

contentBlocks.heading: How is a nearby IB tutor matched to your sector in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
A nearby request is matched in a fixed order. IB Gram notes your sector or society and the slot you want, filters for tutors who teach the right subject at the right International Baccalaureate stage, keeps only those whose travel to you at that hour is sensible, and then offers a shortlist with a demo or trial session before you commit. Subject fit comes first. Distance decides between tutors who already fit.

The radius is not a circle drawn on a map. A tutor based near Sector 49 can often reach Nirvana Country or Malibu Towne for an early-evening slot, yet the same tutor heading to DLF Phase 2 once the offices around Cyber City empty out may spend the lesson's first quarter in traffic. So the radius changes with the hour. Weekend mornings stretch it. Weekday evenings shrink it, sometimes to a few neighbouring sectors.

Take a family in Central Park Resorts on Sohna Road whose daughter is in DP1 and needs HL Mathematics twice a week. The search starts with tutors who can reach Sector 48 and Sector 50 on weekday evenings. If two strong Maths tutors already work along that stretch, the shortlist stays local. If the only HL specialist free on those evenings lives in Palam Vihar, IB Gram says so plainly and suggests that tutor online, or at home on a Saturday, instead of pretending a weekday home slot across the city will hold through the monsoon and the winter smog.

What you share at the start matters more than any filter. Give the exact tower or block, whether a visitor can park inside, which evenings clash with sport or music, and whether a hybrid week of one home session and one online session would suit your child. A shortlist built on a vague address such as "near Golf Course Road" tends to fall apart by the second week, when the tutor discovers the gate is on the far side of the society.
items: 1. You share your sector or society, school calendar, subject, level and the slots your child can keep.
2. IB Gram sets a realistic travel radius for that time of day, not a fixed distance.
3. Tutors inside that radius are filtered by subject, programme stage and level, for example DP HL.
4. If nobody suitable remains nearby, the search widens across Gurgaon or moves to online specialists.
5. A demo or trial session is arranged, and you can ask for a different match if the fit is wrong.

contentBlocks.heading: How the IB stage changes how far you should look
contentBlocks.body:
The younger the child, the more distance matters. The higher the level, the more subject expertise matters. That trade-off shapes every nearby search across the three International Baccalaureate programmes: the Primary Years Programme (PYP), the Middle Years Programme (MYP) and the Diploma Programme. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

For a PYP child, a tutor from the same society or the next sector is often the right call. Young learners tire after a school day, a parent usually wants to be within earshot, and a short, calm session at the dining table beats a longer one that starts late because the tutor was held up near Hero Honda Chowk. Broad strength in reading, numeracy and patient questioning matters more at this age than a narrow specialism, so a nearby tutor is rarely a compromise.

The MYP runs for five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, roughly ages 11 to 16, across eight subject groups. Every subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each scored 0 to 8, and the total out of 32 converts to a final 1 to 7 grade through IB grade boundaries. In the early MYP years a capable local tutor can often support two related subjects. By MYP 5, with the Personal Project due and, where the school offers it, optional eAssessment through on-screen examinations and ePortfolios, families start weighing specialist knowledge against a short commute. The Community Project, in MYP 3 or 4, rarely needs a specialist at all.

The DP is where the radius widens. It is a two-year course, DP1 and DP2, of six subjects from six groups, with three or four taken at HL (240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours). Each subject is graded 1 to 7, and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) with the Extended Essay (EE) adds up to 3 more points, for a maximum of 45. A tutor who handles SL Economics comfortably may not be ready for HL, and the right HL tutor may live across the city.
items: PYP: favour a tutor from your own society or the next sector over a distant specialist.
Early MYP years: a nearby all-rounder can often support two related subject groups.
MYP 5: the Personal Project, and eAssessment where offered, can justify searching beyond your sector.
DP HL: subject expertise outranks distance, so accept online lessons if the specialist lives far away.
DP SL: a competent nearby tutor is often enough, depending on the student's goals and timetable.

contentBlocks.heading: Which IB subjects are easy to find nearby, and which are not?
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics and English tutors tend to be the easiest to find close to home across most Gurgaon corridors, subject to availability. HL science and HL Economics specialists are thinner on the ground, so families in outer sectors often have to accept a longer trip, a weekend slot or online lessons to get the right person for those subjects.

Mathematics shows the gap most clearly. An MYP student working through criterion-based tasks needs a tutor who asks good questions and lets the student reason aloud, which many local tutors do well. A DP student at HL needs someone who can work through long, multi-step problems at speed and show exactly where method marks slip away. That second tutor is scarcer. If the options closest to you on Golf Course Extension Road are confident at SL but hesitant at HL, a specialist teaching online from DLF Phase 3 is a better use of the same Tuesday evening.

IB Sciences sit in the middle. Theory and data questions travel well on a shared screen. Whatever practical and Internal Assessment (IA) work the school runs happens in its own labs, though, so a home tutor's advantage is smaller than parents expect. For a DP student taking HL Chemistry and HL Biology together, depth in both subjects matters far more than whether the tutor lives in Sector 57 or Sector 104.

IB Economics and IB English reward a tutor who marks written work closely. Many families prefer that at home, with handwritten answers corrected beside the student, and in central pockets such as Sushant Lok 1 or DLF Phase 4 it is usually practical. In New Gurgaon or along Dwarka Expressway, where fewer specialists may be close by, a hybrid rhythm works better: answers submitted midweek and marked online, then one home session at the weekend if a tutor's route allows it. TOK and EE mentoring is discussion-led and seldom needs a home visit.
items: Mathematics HL: prioritise proven HL experience over distance; online suits step-by-step problem-solving well.
Sciences: practical work happens in school labs, so a home visit adds less than expected.
Economics: diagrams and written answers benefit from close marking, at home or on screen.
English: essay feedback beside the student is easiest when the tutor lives in your corridor.
TOK and EE mentoring: discussion-based and usually fine online from anywhere in Gurugram.

Golf Course Road, taking in DLF Phase 5, DLF Phase 1, Sector 42, Sector 43, Sector 53, Sector 54, Ardee City and Wazirabad, is compact, and one tutor can often teach two families here on the same evening. Golf Course Extension Road is longer than it looks: Sector 56, Sector 58, Sector 59, Sector 60, Sector 62, Sector 65, Sushant Lok 3, Ghata and Gwal Pahari do not all share an easy route, so an IB tutor Golf Course Extension Road families can rely on is usually someone already working that stretch.

Sohna Road runs past Sector 47, Sector 48, Sector 49 and Sector 50 towards Vatika Chowk and Badshahpur, with Nirvana Country, South City 2, Rosewood City and Uppal Southend alongside. Home classes work, but the approach to Vatika Chowk can slow badly in the evening, so an IB tutor Sohna Road families keep for a full year tends to live on the corridor. The DLF Phases 2 to 4, MG Road and Cyber City belt, including Sikanderpur, Chakkarpur, Sector 24, Sector 27 and Sector 28, is central, but office traffic shapes everything; earlier slots survive better.

Sushant Lok, South City 1 and Millennium City Centre covers Sushant Lok 1, Sushant Lok 2, South City 1, Sector 29, Sector 40, Sector 45, Sector 46 and Greenwood City. It is the most central belt, and home lessons are practical from several directions. The Southern Peripheral Road (SPR), with Sector 66, Sector 67, Sector 68, Sector 69, Sector 72, Ansal Esencia and Bhondsi, suits tutors already based in the south of the city.

New Gurgaon (Sector 82, Sector 83, Sector 85, Sector 89, Sector 90, Kherki Daula and Pataudi Road) and Dwarka Expressway (Sector 102, Sector 103, Sector 108, Sector 109, Sector 110 and Sector 113) are newer and spread out, so online or hybrid often wins for DP. Sohna Road: book slots that start before the evening build-up around Vatika Chowk where possible.
DLF Phases 2 to 4: office traffic near Cyber City and MG Road favours earlier or weekend slots.
New Gurgaon and Dwarka Expressway: expect hybrid or online lessons for most DP HL subjects.
Old Gurgaon and Palam Vihar: a local home tutor is often practical for PYP and early MYP.

contentBlocks.heading: School buses, activities and the evening slot in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
The logo strip on this page shows schools Gurgaon families often mention: Pathways World School, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, The Shri Ram School, Aravali and Heritage Xperiential Learning School. Which programmes each one offers is a question for the school itself. For a nearby tutor, what matters is simpler and harder to plan around: when your child actually walks in the door, and how much energy is left.

The school bus decides the real start time. A student dropped at the gate of Ireo Grand Arch or M3M Golf Estate after a long route needs food and a short break before any serious work, so a lesson booked for the minute the bus arrives rarely goes well. Activities squeeze it further. Two evenings a week lost to football or debate leave three usable slots, and on a corridor such as Golf Course Extension Road the tutor's own route may rule out one of those. Ireo Skyon families face the same arithmetic.

The DP calendar brings pressure in waves. Most Gurgaon IB schools use the May examination session, with results released in early July, though a November session also runs and your coordinator will confirm which applies. In the weeks before internal deadlines and mocks, students want more sessions, not fewer. A home tutor who could just about reach Orchid Petals or Vipul Greens on a quiet October evening may not manage an extra weekday in a busy term. Plan that capacity early, either as a second slot online or as a weekend home session.

Younger children face a different squeeze. A PYP or MYP student in Vatika City or The Close may finish school earlier but carry more clubs, and school holidays rarely line up neatly with a tutor's other students. Families who fix a steady weekday slot in the first month of term, and protect it, tend to lose fewer lessons to reshuffling than families who book week by week.

But a slot that looks free on paper is not the same as a slot your child can use.
items: Add the bus drop-off time and a short break before fixing a home lesson start.
Mark mock and internal deadline weeks early so the tutor can hold extra evenings.
Ask the school coordinator which exam session applies; most Gurgaon IB schools use May.
Keep one weekend slot in reserve for weeks when traffic or activities wreck the plan.
Confirm programme details with your school directly, not with a tutor or a website.

contentBlocks.heading: Nearby generalist, farther specialist or online specialist: which is right?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring with a nearby generalist is usually the right choice for PYP and most MYP work, because the tutor is likelier to arrive on time and a young child settles faster in familiar surroundings. For DP HL subjects, choose the specialist. Have that specialist teach at home if the route and slot genuinely hold, and online or hybrid if they do not, rather than settling for a closer tutor who is unsure of the material.

Home tutoring means the tutor travels to your house or society and teaches at your own table. A parent can stay within earshot, and handwritten work is marked beside the student. Its weak point is travel, which on weekday evenings depends heavily on the corridor. Online tutoring, live on a shared screen, removes the commute and widens the choice of specialists, but it asks more concentration of the student and gives up some of the face-to-face attention a younger child needs. Hybrid, commonly one home session and one online session a week, keeps some in-person contact and costs a little extra planning.

Consider a DP2 student in Sobha City on Dwarka Expressway taking HL Economics. A nearby generalist from Sector 106 can reach Godrej Summit, Sobha City or ATS Kocoon easily and would handle SL revision well. A farther specialist lives in Sector 45 and can only come on Sundays. An online specialist can teach on two weekday evenings with written answers marked in between. For this student the online specialist is the strongest option, and the Sunday home visit is a bonus only if the family wants handwritten timed work checked in person. Picking the generalist because the drive is short would save travel and cost marks.

The same logic applies in New Gurgaon, where families in Vatika India Next or Godrej Air around Sector 84 and Sector 86 may have no HL specialist within an easy evening's reach, and on the Southern Peripheral Road, where Tata Primanti and Sector 70 homes suit tutors already based in the south. A local generalist is never a bad choice for a younger child. It becomes a poor one when a student needs HL depth the tutor cannot supply.
items: Nearby generalist home tutor: reliable timing and low travel risk; best for PYP, early MYP and SL support.
Farther specialist at home: strongest subject fit, but weekday evening trips across Gurgaon often fail.
Online specialist: subject depth without travel; needs a quiet room and a focused student.
Hybrid: online on weekdays, home at weekends when roads are usually lighter.
Home lessons are hardest to sustain between distant corridors, such as New Gurgaon and Golf Course Road.

contentBlocks.heading: Checking a tutor who will walk into your home
contentBlocks.body:
Every tutor IB Gram shortlists has a verified profile, and that is where the platform's check ends and yours begins. Someone who comes into your home week after week deserves your own scrutiny: meet them during the demo, ask what they have taught at your child's exact level, and agree which adult will be at home during lessons.

Gated societies add a layer families often forget. In DLF The Magnolias, DLF The Aralias, DLF The Crest or DLF The Belaire, as in most large societies across the city, visitors are generally registered at the gate, and many societies expect a regular visitor to be pre-approved through the security desk or a resident app. Do this before the demo. A tutor who spends the first visit waiting at the barrier while a guard rings your intercom starts on the wrong foot, and a lesson that begins late usually ends late too.

Parking is a scheduling factor, not a detail. In DLF Park Place, DLF Beverly Park or DLF Regency Park, and on the plotted streets of DLF Phase 2 and Heritage City, a visitor's car may not be allowed inside or may struggle for space outside. Ask how the tutor travels. If they drive, tell them exactly where to park; if they come by cab or two-wheeler, name the gate nearest your tower. Families in DLF Hamilton Court, DLF Richmond Park, Ambience Caitriona or an independent floor in Sector 27 can ask their management whether a regular visitor can be given a fixed entry pass.

Your checks should continue past the first week. Sit within earshot for the demo. Notice what the tutor asks your child before teaching anything. After three or four sessions, ask your child whether explanations feel clearer than before, and read one piece of marked work yourself. If the fit is wrong, you can ask IB Gram for a different match, and asking early costs far less than waiting until mocks.
items: Pre-register the tutor at your society gate or resident app before the demo session.
Confirm where a visitor's car or two-wheeler can park, or where a cab should drop.
Ask which IB levels the tutor has taught recently, for example DP HL or MYP 5.
Agree which adult is at home during lessons, especially for PYP and early MYP children.
Read one piece of marked work yourself after the first few sessions.

contentBlocks.heading: Is the nearest IB tutor in Gurgaon the right one for HL?
contentBlocks.body:
Not always. For PYP, MYP and most SL subjects the nearest capable tutor is often the right one, but for DP HL subjects subject fit should outrank distance. If the best HL match lives across the city, online lessons with that specialist usually serve a student better than weekly home visits from a closer tutor who is less sure of HL material.

A near-me match is best defined as the closest tutor who meets every non-negotiable requirement: the right subject, the right programme stage and level, and a slot your child can keep. Distance is the tie-breaker, not the first filter. Families who reverse that order, asking for anyone within a few sectors and checking the subject afterwards, often end up changing tutors halfway through DP1. A search for "IB tutor near me Gurgaon" should really be read as a search for the right tutor, as close as possible.

HL is where the difference shows. With 240 recommended teaching hours against 150 at SL, an HL course carries more content and harder questions, and a tutor who teaches SL well can find the extra depth uncomfortable. A nearby IB tutor for DP Mathematics at SL may be exactly right for a student in South City 2 or Rosewood City. The same student taking HL Physics may need someone else. A search for IB tutor South City or IB tutor Sushant Lok can return several local names, most of them fine at SL, while a smaller share may be comfortable at HL. That is the moment to look across Gurgaon.

Accept online when the specialist is clearly stronger at the level, a home trip would land in weekday evening traffic, and your child can concentrate on a screen for a full lesson. A student in Sector 83 searching IB tutor New Gurgaon for HL Chemistry is the classic case. So is a family whose search for IB tutor Dwarka Expressway turns up SL-ready tutors nearby but an HL specialist based in DLF Phase 1 or Sector 54. If your child genuinely cannot work online, say so, and the match looks for a weekend home slot with the specialist instead.
items: Define a near-me match as the closest tutor who meets subject, level and slot requirements.
For PYP and early MYP, distance and punctuality usually matter more than narrow specialism.
For DP HL, a stronger specialist online generally beats a weaker tutor at home.
Choose a weekend home slot with a distant specialist only if online truly fails your child.
Review the choice after mocks or a school assessment, not after a single lesson.

contentBlocks.heading: What progress with a nearby tutor should look like
contentBlocks.body:
In the first month, progress with a nearby tutor shows up as routine before it shows up as marks. Lessons start on time, the work the tutor sets gets done, and your child can explain one topic more clearly than before. Marks follow later, usually after a school assessment or two, and no tutor can guarantee a grade.

Watch the logistics as closely as the learning. A home tutor who cancels one weekday evening in three because of traffic out of Sector 29 or a late finish near MG Road is not a nearby tutor in any useful sense. Keep a simple record for four weeks. If more than the odd lesson is lost, move one session online or ask IB Gram for a different match before the pattern hardens into habit.

For MYP students, look at criterion feedback on school tasks, where each of the four criteria is scored 0 to 8, rather than only at the final 1 to 7 grade, because one criterion often improves before the others. For DP students, look at teacher comments on practice work and at how the student handles questions they previously avoided. If nothing has shifted after a full term with a consistent tutor, the cause is usually fit or effort rather than distance, and changing the tutor or the plan is the honest next step.

Some limits are real. Starting HL support in the last weeks before May exams narrows what any tutor can do, near or far. Some students do not need a tutor at all: a PYP child who reads well and enjoys school may only need a calmer homework routine. And no tutor living close to your society can make up for a student who is not engaging with the work. An IB tutor near me in Gurgaon is worth having only when the teaching itself is right.
items: First four weeks: lessons start on time and the tutor's set work actually gets done.
After a school assessment or two: fewer repeated mistakes and clearer written explanations.
MYP: watch individual criterion scores, each out of 8, alongside the final grade.
Lessons lost to traffic more than occasionally: move one online or request a new match.
No tutor, however close to home, can guarantee a grade or a particular score.

contentBlocks.heading: Starting with a Gurgaon home tutor, or restarting after a move
contentBlocks.body:
A request that simply says "home IB tutor in my sector Gurgaon" is a good start but not quite enough. Send a query or book a free consultation with these details ready: your exact sector or society, the school calendar and exam session your child follows, each subject with its level, the weekday and weekend slots that are genuinely free, and whether home, online or hybrid lessons would suit. That is enough for IB Gram to build a first shortlist, subject to tutor availability.

Keep recent school work within reach, such as a marked MYP task with criterion scores, a DP practice answer or a teacher's comments, and note any deadlines coming up this term. Give the gate the tutor's name. If a demo or trial session happens at home, set aside a table in a quiet room and have the relevant unit notes from school ready.

The first session is diagnostic. The tutor typically asks your child to explain a recent topic, works through a few questions together and looks at where marks were lost in school work. By the end you should hear a plain view of what needs attention first and a suggested frequency. If the approach or the rapport feels wrong, say so; you can ask for a different match.

Families move across the city more often than they plan to, from a rental in Palam Vihar to Sector 65, or from DLF Phase 4 to a new tower in Sector 89. When that happens mid-year, do not stop lessons abruptly. Tell IB Gram the new address and the moving date, ask the current tutor whether the new route still works, and if it does not, continue online with the same tutor until a natural break in term. A new nearby match can start then, without disrupting the run-up to internal deadlines or May exams.
items: Have your exact society, tower and gate process ready before you send the query.
Share a recent marked task so the first session starts from real evidence.
List every slot your child can truly keep, including at least one weekend option.
Moving mid-year: continue online with the same tutor until a natural break in term.
Ask for a different match if the first tutor's approach does not suit your child.

faqs.question: Can I find an IB home tutor near me in Gurgaon for every subject?
faqs.answer: Not for every subject, because nearby availability depends on the subject, the level and your corridor. Families looking for IB tutors near me in Gurgaon usually find Mathematics and English support for PYP, MYP and SL students fairly close to home, subject to availability. HL sciences and HL Economics are thinner in every part of the city, so the right tutor may live several corridors away. When that happens, the shortlist sets out the choice plainly: online lessons with the specialist, a weekend home slot when roads are lighter, or a hybrid week combining both. Which one suits depends on your child's age, the subject and the slots you can keep.

faqs.question: How far will a home tutor travel to my sector on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: There is no fixed distance, because the same trip can be easy in the late afternoon and unworkable an hour later. Many home tutors keep weekday evening lessons within their own corridor or the next one, so a tutor who already teaches along Sohna Road is far likelier to take a Sector 49 family than one in Sector 104. Weekday slots tend to break down when a lesson means crossing the city, say between Golf Course Road and Dwarka Expressway, or between Palam Vihar and the Southern Peripheral Road. Give IB Gram the exact start time you need, because a tutor can judge that route at that hour far better than a map can.

faqs.question: Should I accept online lessons if no DP HL specialist lives near me?
faqs.answer: Yes, in most cases, as long as your child can concentrate on a screen for a full lesson. At HL, the tutor's command of the course matters more than the length of the drive, and a strong specialist teaching online from another corner of Gurgaon usually serves a student better than a closer tutor who is unsure of the material. Ask for the demo to run online so you see the real format. If your child drifts, ask whether the specialist could manage one home visit at the weekend, with the other weekly lesson online. A tutor who knows HL inside out but cannot hold your child's attention is not the right match either.

faqs.question: What does my society gate need to know about a regular tutor?
faqs.answer: Share the tutor's name, mobile number, lesson days and usual arrival time with security before the first session, and ask whether a regular visitor can be pre-approved. Processes vary. One society may want a resident app entry for every visit, while another issues a pass to regular visitors or simply rings the flat each time. Ask as well where a visiting car or two-wheeler may park and which gate is closest to your tower, then send those directions to the tutor the day before. A lesson that starts ten minutes late every week becomes, over a whole term, a noticeably shorter course.

faqs.question: We are moving from Palam Vihar to Golf Course Extension Road mid-year. What happens to lessons?
faqs.answer: Lessons can usually carry on without a gap if you plan the switch a few weeks before the move. Start by asking your current tutor whether the new route works at your usual time; a weekend slot may survive even when a weekday one will not. If neither works, move the same tutor online for the rest of the term so your child keeps continuity through internal deadlines. Meanwhile, send IB Gram your new sector and moving date. A tutor who can reach Sector 62 or Sector 65 can then be shortlisted, subject to availability, and given a demo before the handover rather than in the middle of mock season.

faqs.question: It has been a month with a nearby tutor and nothing has improved. Should we switch?
faqs.answer: A month is enough to judge the teaching, though often too early to judge school marks. Look for signs that do not depend on a test: whether your child can explain a recent topic more clearly than before, and whether the tutor sets work, checks it and can describe a plan for the term. If those signs are missing, ask IB Gram for a different match rather than keeping the tutor only because the commute is short. The better replacement may live farther away or teach online. introSummary: An IB online tutor in Gurgaon teaches your child live and one-to-one over a video call with a shared digital whiteboard, so, unlike home tutoring, nobody has to cross the city in evening traffic. It works best for Diploma Programme (DP) Maths, Physics, Chemistry, Economics, English A and Theory of Knowledge (TOK), and reasonably well for the Middle Years Programme (MYP). For the Primary Years Programme (PYP), keep sessions short or choose home lessons.
