heroTitle: Choosing the right IB coaching format in Gurgaon
heroSubtitle: Compare coaching-centre batches, small groups and one-to-one lessons for the International Baccalaureate (IB) Middle Years Programme (MYP) and Diploma Programme (DP): which format suits Maths, Physics, Economics and Theory of Knowledge (TOK), which tasks must never be group-coached, and how verified tutors work at home or online.
introSummary: IB coaching in Gurgaon comes in three formats, and for most Diploma Programme students the place to start is one-to-one home tuition, with a verified tutor who comes to your sector or society. A coaching-centre batch gives structure and a fixed timetable, but its single pace suits entrance exams better than IB work, where marks depend on command terms and assessment criteria. A small group of two to four same-level students can suit Theory of Knowledge discussion or Economics case practice. One-to-one home classes fit Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) differences, Internal Assessment (IA) feedback and a student's own school calendar, at a higher cost and without peers to argue with. This page compares the three, lists what must never be group-coached, and shows how IB Gram matches Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana families with tutors whose profiles are verified.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram shortlists coaching options in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
A parent asking for IB coaching is usually asking two things at once: who should teach this child, and in what format. IB Gram treats the format as part of the match rather than an afterthought. Before any tutor is suggested, the conversation pins down the programme, each subject and level, the school's internal deadlines, the sector or society where lessons would happen, and which evenings are genuinely free once school timings, buses and activities are counted.

The reason is practical. A DP2 student taking Physics HL and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches (AA) SL, with an IA draft due soon, needs a different arrangement from an MYP 5 student who wants steady weekly help in sciences. The first may need one-to-one home tuition aimed at one component and one deadline. The second might do perfectly well sharing sessions with a classmate at the same level. Treating both as another seat in a batch wastes the family's money and the student's evenings.

The numbered steps in this section describe what happens after you send a query or book a free consultation. None of it is a promise of a particular tutor or time slot, since both depend on level, subject and schedule, and a suitable specialist for a less common HL combination can take longer to find than one for SL Maths.

One point about groups. If two or three families want to share sessions, mention it in the query and the shortlist can allow for it, subject to tutor availability. Sharing makes sense only when the students are at the same level, on the same subject route and working to similar school timelines. Mixed-level rooms are a common reason IB coaching in Gurgaon disappoints, and the next section explains why. If you are unsure which format to ask for, start there. The first conversation can be about format before it is about any tutor.
items: 1. You send a query or book a free consultation, naming the programme, subjects and HL or SL.
2. IB Gram asks about syllabus, school calendar, internal deadlines, your sector or society, and free evenings.
3. You say whether one-to-one, a small group of same-level peers, or either could work.
4. IB Gram shortlists tutors with verified profiles that match subject, level, format and location.
5. A demo or trial session is arranged before the family commits to regular coaching.
6. If the fit is wrong, you ask for a different match instead of persisting for months.

contentBlocks.heading: Why does batch coaching built for CBSE, JEE or NEET suit IB poorly?
contentBlocks.body:
Batch coaching built for CBSE, JEE or NEET suits IB poorly because it moves a large room through one syllabus, towards one style of paper, at one speed. IB students rarely share any of those. They sit different levels, write different internal assessments, and earn marks for explaining and evaluating, which a fast objective-question drill does not train.

Look at what a Diploma Programme student actually carries. The DP is a two-year course, DP1 and DP2, of six subjects from six groups. Three or four are taken at HL, with 240 recommended teaching hours each, and the rest at SL, with 150 hours. Each subject is graded 1 to 7. TOK and the Extended Essay (EE) combine for up to 3 more points, so the maximum is 45, and 24 points is the minimum for the diploma, subject to the IB's failing conditions. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) must also be completed. Ten students in one room can hold ten different combinations.

Now put HL and SL students in one Physics or Maths batch. Pitch the lesson at SL and the HL student never reaches the depth their papers will demand. Pitch it at HL and the SL student sits through content that will never be examined at their level, and starts to feel behind when they are not. Split the difference and the batch slows both of them. Neither gets enough practice at their own level, and that practice is what moves an IB grade over a term. A centre that runs one 'IB Chemistry batch' for both levels is showing you how little it has planned.

The Middle Years Programme has its own mismatch. MYP 4 and 5 work is judged against criteria, so a student who can reproduce a method but cannot justify a choice or evaluate a result loses marks that extra speed never recovers. Command terms such as explain, discuss and evaluate set specific expectations in both programmes. Students arriving from CBSE schooling often need to unlearn the habit of writing the shortest correct line, and a batch built for board-exam volume tends to reinforce it.
items: HL and SL students in one batch means one level is always taught at the wrong depth.
Each DP subject is graded 1-7, and TOK with the EE adds up to 3 points.
The diploma needs at least 24 points, subject to the IB's failing conditions, plus completed CAS.
Speed drills train short answers; IB command terms reward explanation and evaluation.
Ask any IB coaching centre in Gurgaon whether Physics and Maths batches are split by level.

contentBlocks.heading: What Maths, Physics, Economics and TOK coaching should involve
contentBlocks.body:
IB Maths coaching in Gurgaon has to begin with the course, not the chapter. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation (AI) are separate DP courses, each offered at HL and SL, so one 'IB Maths' label can hide four different routes. A group that mixes AA and AI students is two classes sharing a whiteboard. Past questions from the wrong course teach the wrong emphasis, however clearly they are explained.

IB Physics coaching, and Chemistry coaching with it, is often sold as problem practice. Numerical fluency matters. But students also have to interpret data and explain what is happening in precise words, and the internal assessment is individual work. The usual gap is not the formula. It is a correct idea written loosely, which only closes when someone reads that student's own answers closely.

Most requests for IB Economics coaching in Gurugram come from students who understand the ideas but lose marks on structure. The course has four units: Introduction to economics, Microeconomics, Macroeconomics and The global economy. Paper 1 is extended response, Paper 2 is data response, and Paper 3, a policy paper, is HL only. Data-response practice suits a small group, because students learn from how peers read the same extract, while Paper 3 practice belongs with HL students alone. The IA is a portfolio of three commentaries, each up to 800 words, on published news articles, each drawing on a different syllabus unit and a different one of the nine key concepts.

IB TOK coaching is the strongest case for discussion. The course covers the core theme, knowledge and the knower, two of five optional themes and five areas of knowledge, and arguments improve when students test them on each other. Some work, though, must never be coached in a group. IA drafts, Economics commentaries, the TOK exhibition and essay, and EE drafts are each student's own assessed work. Workshopping one draft in front of classmates, or giving everyone a common template, invites look-alike submissions and academic integrity trouble. Draft feedback belongs in one-to-one time, as questions and comments, within the school's rules.
items: Maths AA and AI are separate courses and should never share a batch.
Economics Paper 3, the policy paper, is sat by HL students only.
Each Economics commentary is up to 800 words on a published news article.
IA, EE and TOK drafts get individual feedback only, never group workshopping.
Physics and Chemistry coaching should mark written explanations, not just numerical answers.

contentBlocks.heading: Where in Gurgaon home tuition and small coaching groups are practical
contentBlocks.body:
Families on Golf Course Road, across DLF Phase 5, DLF Phase 1, Sector 42, Sector 43, Sector 53, Sector 54, Ardee City and Wazirabad, often want IB coaching on Golf Course Road itself so the student is not crossing the city after school. In societies such as DLF The Magnolias, DLF The Aralias, DLF Park Place, DLF The Crest and DLF The Belaire, home tuition needs gate entry arranged in advance. A small group is easiest when the students live in the same society, since one living room saves everyone a drive.

The Sushant Lok, South City 1 and Millennium City Centre corridor takes in Sushant Lok 1, Sushant Lok 2, South City 1, Sector 29, Sector 40, Sector 45, Sector 46 and Greenwood City. Parents looking for IB coaching in Gurgaon from these sectors often have several formats within reach, so the choice is about fit rather than distance. Being near a centre is convenient. It does not fix a room that mixes HL and SL students.

The Sohna Road corridor covers Sector 47, Sector 48, Sector 49, Sector 50, Nirvana Country, South City 2, Rosewood City, Uppal Southend, Vatika Chowk and Badshahpur. In societies such as Central Park Resorts, Orchid Petals, Vatika City, Malibu Towne, Vipul Greens and The Close, it is sometimes possible to find two same-level students in one complex, which makes a home group simple. Evening traffic on Sohna Road can stretch a short trip, though, so a tutor finishing near Vatika Chowk may only reach Badshahpur for a later slot. Hybrid coaching often solves that.

DLF Phases 2 to 4, MG Road and Cyber City form the fourth pattern: DLF Phase 2, DLF Phase 3, DLF Phase 4, MG Road, Cyber City, Sikanderpur, Chakkarpur, Sector 24, Sector 27 and Sector 28. Evening traffic around Cyber City and MG Road can stretch even a short trip at the hour school finishes, so weekday home slots are harder to fix. Families in DLF Beverly Park, Heritage City, DLF Hamilton Court, DLF Regency Park, DLF Richmond Park and Ambience Caitriona may find online one-to-one coaching simpler on school nights, with home sessions kept for weekends.
items: Golf Course Road societies: arrange gate entry before the first home session.
Small groups work best when students live in the same society or complex.
Sohna Road families can mix weekend home lessons with weekday online sessions.
Around Cyber City and MG Road, weekday evening home slots can be hard to fix.
Sushant Lok and South City 1 families usually have more than one format within reach.

contentBlocks.heading: How school deadlines in Gurgaon should shape a coaching term
contentBlocks.body:
Families at international schools across Gurgaon, including Pathways World School, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, The Shri Ram School, Aravali and Heritage Xperiential Learning School, work to internal calendars that a coaching plan has to respect. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Nothing on this page describes a particular school's policy or deadlines.

Only a few dates come from the IB itself. DP exam sessions run in May, the session most Gurgaon IB schools use, and in November, and May results are released in early July. The rest is set by each school: IA draft dates, EE milestones, the TOK exhibition, mock examinations and the point when predicted grades are sent. These vary between schools and even between years, so ask the DP coordinator for the calendar instead of trusting a coaching centre's assumptions.

A structured coaching term is planned backwards from those dates. The opening two or three weeks are diagnostic: recent tests, teacher comments and one timed task show where marks are going. The middle weeks teach content in the school's order, slightly ahead where possible. As an internal draft deadline approaches, new content pauses so the student has time to write their own IA, and the tutor's job narrows to checking understanding and answering questions. Before mocks, the plan turns to timed past-paper work and markscheme language.

A batch centre cannot plan like this for each student, because one timetable serves the whole room. Two students in the same Chemistry batch may face IA deadlines weeks apart at different schools, and the batch pauses for neither. That is the strongest practical argument for one-to-one, or for a small group drawn from one school, in DP1 and DP2. In MYP 4 and 5 the calendar is lighter, and a fixed weekly group matters less.
items: May and November are the DP exam sessions; May results arrive in early July.
Ask the DP coordinator for internal IA, EE and TOK exhibition dates.
Pause new content before internal draft deadlines so students write their own IA.
Batch timetables cannot shift for one student's deadline; one-to-one plans can.
Same-school small groups share a calendar, which makes planning around deadlines easier.

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid: which suits IB coaching in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
For most DP students here, one-to-one home tuition is the format to start with: a verified tutor at the family's own table, close enough to read the student's handwriting and notice when attention slips. Online sessions are the better call when the best-matched specialist lives across the city or DP2 weeks are crowded. Hybrid sits between the two. A small group can work in any of these modes, provided the students genuinely match.

Here is the trade-off stated plainly. Home tuition lets the tutor see the student's notebooks, handwriting and concentration, suits timed written practice, and allows a group of neighbours to meet in one flat. But it depends on travel, gate entry and evening traffic, and it narrows the choice to home tutors who can reach your sector. Online coaching widens the choice to a specialist anywhere in the city, removes travel and makes it easy to annotate a marked past paper on screen, but it asks more self-discipline of the student and makes group discussion a little stiffer. Hybrid coaching combines the two, usually online sessions on school nights and home classes at weekends, at the price of more scheduling.

Format and mode interact. A batch at a centre is always in person and always on the centre's timetable. A small group of two to four students can meet at one family's home in a society such as Central Park Resorts or DLF Park Place, or join the same online session from different sectors. One-to-one coaching is the most flexible in both modes, and that flexibility matters most in the weeks around internal deadlines.

Sometimes home tuition is the worse choice. A DP2 student in DLF Phase 3 whose best-matched Economics tutor lives near Badshahpur will probably gain more from a punctual online session than from a home lesson that starts late after the drive. And sometimes online is worse: a restless MYP 4 student who drifts on screen, or three friends who spend the call chatting. You can choose the mode subject by subject. Nothing requires Maths and TOK to be taught the same way.
items: Home tuition: best for handwriting, attention and neighbour groups; limited by travel and traffic.
Online: widest tutor choice and no travel; needs a student who stays focused on screen.
Hybrid: online on school nights, home classes at weekends; more scheduling, fewer compromises.
Centre batches: in person only, on a fixed timetable that ignores school deadlines.
Mode can differ by subject, for example Maths online and Economics at home.

contentBlocks.heading: How should you judge an IB coaching offer in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Judge an IB coaching offer by how precisely it handles level, assessment and academic integrity, not by its timetable or its banner. Ask whether HL and SL are taught separately, whether AA and AI students are separated, how draft feedback is handled, who actually teaches, and what a trial looks like. Vague answers to those questions tell you most of what you need.

Use the numbered checklist in this section on any option, IB Gram included. It works for a large centre, a tutor another parent recommends, or a small group being set up in your society. The best IB coaching in Gurgaon for your child is simply the option that passes these checks for their subjects and levels. A hoarding that says 'best' tells you nothing about that.

On IB Gram's side, tutors are shortlisted from profiles that have been verified and matched against the subject, programme, level and schedule you describe. Treat that as a starting point, not a replacement for your own judgement. In the demo or trial session, notice whether the tutor asks for the student's recent marked work and school calendar before teaching, uses IB command terms naturally, and can explain the gap between what the student knows and what the markscheme rewards. Ask, too, which IB subjects and levels the tutor has taught most recently, and whether they have taught small groups before if that is the plan.

Then ask directly about drafts. A tutor or centre that offers to fix an IA, write model commentaries for students to adapt, or supply a finished TOK exhibition is putting your child's diploma at risk, and that answer alone should rule them out. Legitimate help looks different. It means teaching the concepts, explaining the criteria, asking questions that make the student think harder, and leaving every word of the submission to the student. If you are unsure what the school permits from outside tutors, the DP coordinator can tell you before the first session.
items: 1. Are HL and SL students, and Maths AA and AI students, taught separately?
2. How many students share a session, and are they all at the same level?
3. Are IA, EE and TOK drafts reviewed only one-to-one, with nothing written for the student?
4. Does the plan follow your school's internal deadlines or only the centre's timetable?
5. Is a demo or trial session offered before you commit to a full term?
6. What happens, and how quickly, if the fit is wrong after a few weeks?

contentBlocks.heading: Batch, small group or one-to-one: which IB coaching format fits?
contentBlocks.body:
One-to-one, usually as home tuition, fits most DP students with mixed HL and SL loads or close IA deadlines. A small group of two to four same-level students fits TOK discussion, Economics case practice and steady MYP support. A large batch fits only when every student shares the course, the level and the school's pace. Budget and the value of peers decide the rest.

A coaching-centre batch is a fixed class, often large, taught to a common syllabus on the centre's timetable. Its strengths are real: it usually costs less per hour than individual lessons, it gives structure to students who need routine, and peers set a working pace. Its weaknesses for IB are just as real. HL and SL students end up in one room, draft deadlines differ by school, and one teacher cannot read every student's written answers with care. A batch earns its place for MYP students who need a weekly rhythm, or for one narrow skill a whole group lacks in the same way.

IB small group classes in Gurgaon work when the group is chosen, not assembled. Two to four students at the same level, ideally from the same school so their calendars line up, can share TOK sessions where they test knowledge questions on each other, or Economics sessions where each explains a data extract and the others challenge the diagram. Picture three DP1 friends in Nirvana Country taking Economics HL together on Saturday mornings. It works for a term. Then one of them falls behind on Paper 3 calculations and needs separate time, and the group has to allow for that without dragging the other two back. Every group needs an agreed exit plan.

One to one IB coaching is the most precise format and the most expensive. Every minute goes to one student's gaps, one school's deadlines and one set of levels, and draft feedback can happen safely. Its limits deserve plain words. It costs more per hour than any group. It offers no peer discussion, so a TOK student may rehearse arguments with a single listener. And a student who leans on a tutor for every step can lose the independence DP2 demands. Many families combine formats rather than picking one.
items: Large batch: structure and lower hourly cost; mixed levels and fixed pace limit IB depth.
Small group of two to four: real peer discussion, but only with matched level and school.
One-to-one: exact fit and safe draft feedback; highest hourly cost and no peers.
Combine formats: one-to-one for a pressured HL subject, a small group for TOK.
Never share a session for IA, EE or TOK draft feedback, whatever the format.

contentBlocks.heading: What realistic progress looks like after a term of coaching
contentBlocks.body:
Progress in IB DP coaching in Gurgaon rarely shows up first as a jump in the school report. In the first three or four weeks, look for signs in the work itself: fuller explanations, the command term actually answered, working laid out so a marker can follow it, and fewer repeated errors on the same kind of question. Internal test grades usually lag behind those changes by a cycle or two.

By the end of a first term, a fair expectation is that the student can name where marks are being lost in each coached subject and has a plan for each. In Economics that might be diagrams drawn without labels. In Maths AI it might be a correct answer never interpreted in context. In TOK it is often describing an example instead of addressing the knowledge question. If nobody can say what has changed after six to eight weeks, talk to the tutor, and if that conversation goes nowhere, ask IB Gram for a different match.

No tutor can guarantee a grade, and no format makes up for a student who does not practise between sessions. Starting late narrows what is possible. A student who begins coaching in the spring of DP2 can still sharpen technique, but content gaps from DP1 in an HL subject will not all close in that time. One-to-one is not automatically better, either. A sociable student may make steadier progress in a well-matched small group than alone with a tutor.

So sometimes the right answer is less coaching, not more. A student coping well in MYP 4, with useful feedback from teachers, may not need regular sessions at all, or may need only a short block before a demanding unit. DP students also carry CAS alongside TOK and the EE, and an extra evening of coaching every week costs sleep and free time. Weigh that as seriously as the fees.
items: Weeks 3-4: clearer explanations and fewer repeated errors in the student's own work.
End of term one: the student can say where marks are lost in each subject.
No visible change after six to eight weeks: review with the tutor, then rematch.
Late starts in DP2 sharpen technique but rarely close every DP1 content gap.
A well-matched small group can suit a sociable student better than one-to-one.

contentBlocks.heading: Starting IB coaching in Gurugram: what to have ready
contentBlocks.body:
Before the first conversation, gather the student's subject list with HL and SL marked, the Maths course (AA or AI), the latest school report and a couple of marked tests. If the DP coordinator has shared the internal deadline calendar, bring that as well. Note the evenings that are genuinely free, your sector or society, and whether home, online or hybrid is realistic. If another family wants to share sessions, have their child's subjects and levels ready too, since a small group only works when levels match.

Then send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, and discusses the format as well as shortlisting tutors with verified profiles. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit. Availability depends on subject, level and schedule, so a family in Wazirabad asking for weekday HL Physics at home might be offered online sessions on school nights with a home lesson at the weekend.

The first session should be diagnostic, not a lecture. A good tutor looks at recent marked work, asks the student to attempt a short question or explain a recent topic aloud, checks the upcoming internal deadlines, and agrees what the next four weeks will focus on. For a small group, that first session also sets the ground rules: how discussion runs, what each student prepares, and the fact that nobody's IA, EE or TOK draft is ever shared with the group.

After two or three sessions, speak to your child privately about whether the explanations make sense and whether the format feels right. If something is off, say so early. Changing a tutor, or moving from a group to one-to-one, is far easier in October of DP1 than in March of DP2, when every week before May is already spoken for.
items: Subject list with HL and SL marked, plus the Maths course: AA or AI.
Latest school report, two marked tests and any teacher comments on recent work.
Internal deadline calendar for IA, EE, TOK and mocks, from the DP coordinator.
Your sector or society, free evenings, and whether home, online or hybrid suits.
Subjects and levels of any classmate who might join a small group.

faqs.question: Is a coaching centre good enough for the IB Diploma Programme?
faqs.answer: A centre can be good enough, but only if it separates HL from SL, keeps Maths AA and AI apart, and keeps draft work out of the classroom. Some centres run IB batches alongside CBSE or entrance-exam classes and teach them the same way: fast coverage, objective drills and a fixed timetable. That can help a disciplined MYP student who needs routine. For a DP student looking at IB coaching in Gurgaon, ask how many students share the room, whether their levels match, and whether the plan changes around your school's IA and mock dates. If the answers are vague, one-to-one or a matched small group is usually safer.

faqs.question: Will a home tutor come to our sector on weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: Often yes, but it depends on the tutor's other lessons, your sector and the evening you need. A home tutor already teaching nearby may manage a regular slot soon after school, while one travelling from across Gurgaon might only offer a later start or a weekend session. Evening traffic on Sohna Road or around Cyber City can stretch a short trip, so say in your query which evenings are free and how late the student can still concentrate. If the best-matched IB specialist cannot reach you on school nights, a hybrid plan with online sessions midweek and home tuition at the weekend may be the practical answer, subject to tutor availability.

faqs.question: Is a small group of classmates better than one-to-one IB coaching?
faqs.answer: A small group is better for some subjects and worse for others. Two to four students at the same level, ideally from one school, suit TOK, where discussion sharpens knowledge questions, and Economics data-response practice, where students learn from how others read an extract. A group is weaker for an HL subject in which one student is far behind the rest, and it is never the place for IA, EE or TOK draft feedback. Plenty of families use both: a small group for TOK at the weekend and one-to-one for Maths AA HL during the week.

faqs.question: Why shouldn't a coaching group work on IA or Extended Essay drafts together?
faqs.answer: Each draft must be the student's own work, and group workshopping puts that at risk. When a class sees one student's draft, or everyone receives the same model structure, submissions start to resemble each other, and academic integrity concerns can follow for every student involved. The safe pattern is one-to-one. The tutor explains the criteria, asks questions and comments on the thinking, and the student writes every word. Before any draft feedback begins, check the school's rules on outside help with the DP coordinator, and share those rules with the tutor so everyone works within them.

faqs.question: Does online coaching work for a student in DLF Phase 4 or Sector 54?
faqs.answer: Yes, online coaching works well for most DP students, provided the student stays focused on screen and the tutor knows the IB course. It removes the evening drive through Cyber City or Golf Course Road traffic and widens the choice to any suitable tutor in Gurgaon, which matters for less common HL combinations. It suits Maths practice, Economics data work and TOK discussion. Younger MYP students who drift on screen, or families who want handwriting checked beside the student, may prefer home lessons at weekends combined with online sessions on school nights.

faqs.question: Can small-group home tuition run in our Sohna Road society?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the students are at the same level and one family can host regularly. A home tuition group in a society such as Vipul Greens, Malibu Towne or Central Park Resorts saves everyone travel, and gate entry has to be arranged for the tutor alone. The host flat needs a table with room for every student's books, and a parent should ideally be at home while lessons run. Evening traffic on Sohna Road can stretch a short trip, so a weekend morning is often easier to fix than a school night, subject to tutor availability. Agree early what happens if one student falls behind, changes level or misses a session.

faqs.question: How does the cost of one-to-one coaching compare with a batch?
faqs.answer: One-to-one costs more per hour than a batch or a small group, because the whole session goes to one student. What that buys is exact level fit, a plan built around your school's deadlines and safe draft feedback. A small group shares the cost across families and keeps much of that precision if levels match. A batch usually costs least per hour and gives the least individual attention. This page gives no prices, because fees depend on subject, level, tutor and format, and IB Gram's fees page explains those factors in detail.

faqs.question: What if the coaching is not working after a month?
faqs.answer: Raise it with the tutor first, and if nothing changes within a couple of weeks, ask IB Gram for a different match. Before deciding, look at the student's work rather than one test score. Are explanations fuller, are repeated errors fading, and does the student know what the next internal deadline needs? Sometimes the problem is the format rather than the tutor. A student lost in a small group may need a few one-to-one sessions to close a specific gap, and a student who is bored alone with a tutor may do better with a matched peer.

faqs.question: Can TOK be coached in a small group?
faqs.answer: Yes, TOK is one of the few IB courses where a small matched group genuinely helps, and IB Gram can look for a tutor willing to teach one, subject to availability. The course covers the core theme of knowledge and the knower, two of five optional themes and five areas of knowledge, and all of it improves with argument. But the exhibition, which uses three objects linked to one of 35 IA prompts in up to 950 words, and the essay on one of six prescribed titles, in up to 1,600 words, must stay each student's own work. Groups discuss ideas; drafts are reviewed individually.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start coaching in DP2?
faqs.answer: It is not too late, but what coaching can achieve narrows as the May session approaches. A student who starts early in DP2 still has time to rebuild a weak HL topic and plan around the remaining internal deadlines. A student who starts after mocks will mostly gain exam technique, timed practice and sharper command-term answers, while some DP1 content gaps will remain. In that late window, one-to-one is usually the more efficient format, because there is no time to wait for a batch to reach the topics the student actually needs.

faqs.question: Will my child's school object to outside IB coaching?
faqs.answer: That depends on the school and on the kind of help, so confirm with the DP coordinator. Teaching concepts, practising past questions and explaining assessment criteria are ordinary tutoring. Writing, rewriting or heavily editing an IA, EE or TOK piece is not acceptable anywhere, whatever the format or the fee. IB Gram is independent and cannot speak for any school's policy in Gurgaon or elsewhere. The sensible step is to ask the coordinator what outside support is permitted, then share that answer with the tutor at the first session so the coaching plan stays inside the rules.

introSummary: For many families, IB classes in Gurgaon mean home tuition: a verified tutor teaching the student at home, in the family's own sector or society, on a timetable planned backwards from the International Baccalaureate (IB) school calendar, not squeezed into whatever evening is free. A Primary Years Programme (PYP) child might need one short class a week, a Middle Years Programme (MYP) student two, and a Diploma Programme (DP) student carrying three Higher Level (HL) subjects something closer to a schedule of its own. This page sets out weekly patterns by stage, a month-by-month DP2 plan, uses for the summer between DP1 and DP2, revision before mocks and May, and fitting an evening class around a school bus and corridor traffic. IB Gram shortlists tutors who match that timetable, at home, online or hybrid, and a trial class can be arranged before you commit.

contentBlocks.heading: How do IB classes in Gurgaon get set up through IB Gram?
contentBlocks.body:
You send a query or book a free consultation, IB Gram asks about the timetable the classes have to fit, and you get a shortlist of tutors whose verified profiles match the programme, subjects, level, location and the slots you can actually keep. A trial class can then be arranged before anything is fixed. The schedule gets settled at the start, not discovered in week three.

A request for IB classes in Gurgaon is really a request for a timetable: a set of weekly slots with a tutor, planned against the school calendar and changed on purpose as tests, holidays and exams approach. That is why the questions are specific. Which board, syllabus and stage, whether PYP, MYP 3 or DP1? Which subjects, and at Higher Level or Standard Level (SL)? What does this term hold: unit tests, Internal Assessment (IA) draft deadlines, and the mock window for a DP2 student? When does the student get home, and which evenings already belong to football, music or another commitment?

A short example shows the difference. Aanya is in DP1, lives in Sector 57, takes Maths and Economics at HL, gets off the school bus in the late afternoon and swims on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Her request is not simply for an Economics tutor. It is two weekday Economics classes on Monday and Wednesday, one longer weekend class for Maths, an online option on swimming days when a doubt cannot wait, and a plan that steps up once her school publishes mock dates in DP2. Matching against that request produces a very different shortlist.

A PYP conversation is shorter: one or two slots, an adult at home, and a clear reason for the class. A DP2 conversation is longer, because the plan should change as mocks and May get closer. And if the first match does not suit the student, or the slots stop working after the school changes its timetable, you can ask for a different match.
items: 1. Send a query or book a free consultation with the stage and subjects.
2. Share the school calendar, bus timing, activities and the evenings that are free.
3. Receive a shortlist of verified tutors matching level, location and schedule.
4. Take a trial class in the planned slot, at home or online.
5. Fix the weekly pattern, or ask for a different match if the fit is wrong.

contentBlocks.heading: How often should IB weekly classes run in PYP, MYP and DP?
contentBlocks.body:
As a starting range, a PYP child often manages well with one or two classes a week of 45 to 60 minutes, an MYP student with two classes of about an hour, and a DP student with one class a week for each subject that needs support, lasting 60 to 90 minutes. These are ranges with reasons, not prescriptions, and the reasons matter more than the numbers.

IB PYP classes in Gurgaon should be short and frequent. The Primary Years Programme covers ages 3-12, learning runs through units of inquiry under six transdisciplinary themes, and there are no external examinations, so nothing is gained by long sessions. An eight-year-old has limited attention left after a school day. A class that follows the current unit, say an inquiry under 'Sharing the planet', keeps the work connected to school. In the final year, the PYP exhibition can justify a second slot for a few weeks before the pattern drops back.

IB MYP classes work best as a weekly pair. The Middle Years Programme runs from MYP 1 to MYP 5, roughly ages 11-16, across eight subject groups, and every subject is assessed against criteria A-D, each scored 0-8. Tasks arrive in cycles, so one weekly class handles the concept and the second handles the task in progress. The Community Project in MYP 3 or 4, and the Personal Project in MYP 5, can take over one slot for a month. Where the school offers MYP eAssessment, MYP 5 is the year to add a third class, not earlier.

The Diploma Programme is two years of six subjects, three or four at HL with 240 recommended teaching hours each and the rest at SL with 150. That gap is why an HL subject often needs its own weekly class while an SL subject may manage with a fortnightly one. DP1 is for building a steady routine. DP2 adds revision on top, and a student who arrives in DP2 without a routine usually finds the week crowded fast.
items: PYP: one or two classes of 45-60 minutes, following the current unit of inquiry
MYP 1-3: two classes a week, one on concepts, one on the criterion task due
MYP 4-5: two or three classes, with project and eAssessment weeks planned early
DP1: one class per HL subject that needs support, 60-90 minutes each
DP2: the same base, plus revision classes added before school mocks and May

contentBlocks.heading: What a weekly class covers in Maths, Sciences, English and Economics
contentBlocks.body:
A weekly class earns its slot when it does what a school lesson has no time for: slowing down on the step the student missed, and practising answers at the depth the markscheme expects. How the hour is split depends on the subject.

IB Maths classes in Gurgaon are mostly working time. A DP student taking Maths at HL might spend the first quarter of the class on the school problem set that went wrong, the middle on one topic taken from definition to exam-style question, and the end on a timed question checked against a markscheme. In MYP Mathematics, the same hour is organised around the criteria the next school task will be marked against, with the criterion feedback from the last task deciding where the time goes.

Sciences classes split between understanding and writing. A student can know exactly why a reaction speeds up and still lose marks because the question said explain and the answer only described. Command terms such as define, describe, explain, evaluate, discuss and to what extent set the depth each answer needs, and a useful class trains that habit on two or three questions every week. English classes lean the other way, with more reading and extended writing: a draft comes in, gets discussed, and is rewritten before the next class.

Economics sits between the two, with exact definitions, clear diagrams and evaluation that has to reach a judgement. Past papers, markschemes and subject reports, which come through the school or the IB's official channels, show how marks are awarded, so a DP2 class uses them every week while a DP1 class uses them at the end of each unit. In MYP subjects, the four criterion scores out of 8 add to a total out of 32, which converts to a 1-7 grade through IB grade boundaries. That makes a class aimed at the weakest criterion a better use of the hour than general revision.
items: Maths: review the problem set, teach one topic, finish with a timed question
Sciences: concept first, then two or three answers written to the command term
English: reading and a written draft, rewritten after feedback before the next class
Economics: exact definitions, a clear diagram and a written judgement every week
MYP subjects: weight class time towards the weakest of criteria A-D

contentBlocks.heading: Timing IB tuition classes in Gurgaon, corridor by corridor
contentBlocks.body:
IB classes in Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana succeed or fail on the slot, and the right slot depends on the corridor. On Golf Course Extension Road, covering Sector 56, Sector 57, Sector 58, Sector 59, Sector 60, Sector 62 and Sector 65, Sushant Lok 3, Ghata and Gwal Pahari, a class that starts soon after the school bus drop-off is often easier to hold than one at 6:30 pm, when evening traffic on the road can stretch a short trip. Societies such as M3M Golf Estate, Ireo Grand Arch and Ireo Skyon add gate entry, so register a home tutor before the first class or the opening minutes go on visitor formalities.

Along the Southern Peripheral Road (SPR), in Sector 66, Sector 67, Sector 68, Sector 69, Sector 70 and Sector 72, Ansal Esencia, Bhondsi and societies like Tata Primanti, a steady pattern is two weekday classes plus one longer weekend class. Weekend mornings suit the long DP class that needs a full past-paper question, and a short online class works for midweek doubts when a home visit would not be worth the drive.

In Old Gurgaon and Palam Vihar, meaning Palam Vihar itself, Civil Lines, Sadar Bazar, Jacobpura, Rajendra Park, Ashok Vihar, Sector 4, Sector 14, Sector 15, Sector 22 and Sector 23, the older roads and market traffic near Sadar Bazar make early-evening home slots less predictable. If the school run is long, the student also gets home later. A 7 pm online class on weekdays with a home class on Sunday is often the realistic answer.

New Gurgaon, meaning Sector 82, Sector 83, Sector 84, Sector 85, Sector 86, Sector 89 and Sector 90, Kherki Daula and the Pataudi Road side, with societies such as Vatika India Next and Godrej Air, has newer roads but longer gaps between clusters. Home classes hold up when they sit on the same evenings every week. If the week keeps shifting, hybrid is the practical call, and IB classes in Gurgaon's newer sectors often settle into online midweek and at home at the weekend.
items: Golf Course Extension Road: register the tutor at the society gate before the first class
SPR: two weekday classes and one longer weekend class is often the steadiest pattern
Old Gurgaon and Palam Vihar: later weekday classes online, weekend classes at home
New Gurgaon: fix home classes to the same evenings or move midweek classes online
Every corridor: test the planned slot during the trial class on a normal school day

contentBlocks.heading: Gurgaon school timings, buses and activities: where home classes fit
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, including Pathways World School, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, The Shri Ram School, Aravali and Heritage Xperiential Learning School, or with the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. What follows describes the calendar pressures families at international schools in Gurgaon face in general, not the rules of any one school.

The school day sets the first limit. A student who leaves on an early bus and returns in the late afternoon has perhaps one good hour of focus left after food and a rest, and a class stacked straight after a sports practice rarely gets that hour. So look at the whole week before choosing slots: bus return times, after-school activities, Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) commitments for DP students, and the evenings when school homework is heaviest. With home tuition, time the tutor's arrival for when the student is home and has eaten, not for when the bus is due.

The term sets the second. Unit tests, project deadlines and, in DP, IA drafts, Extended Essay (EE) meetings and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) work all arrive on dates the school sets, and they tend to cluster. Each school sets its own DP2 mock examination dates, usually several months before May, and most Gurgaon IB schools enter students for the May session, with results released in early July. Ask the coordinator for these dates at the start of the year so classes change pace before the busy weeks, not during them.

Holidays are the most useful window of all. IB holiday classes in summer and in the winter break can close gaps that weekly classes cannot, because the student is rested and school homework is not competing for the evening. A sensible winter catch-up for an MYP student is two or three focused classes a week on the unit that went badly, not a daily cram. For a DP2 student, check where the winter break falls against the school's mock dates before booking family travel, because that decides what the holiday classes should do.
items: Collect bus return times and activity days before fixing any weekly class slot
Ask the coordinator early for unit test, IA draft and mock examination dates
Leave one weekday evening free of classes during heavy project weeks
Use winter holiday classes to repair one weak unit, not to re-teach a term
Check DP2 mock dates before booking any winter family travel

contentBlocks.heading: IB home classes in Gurugram, online or hybrid: which timetable holds up?
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition holds up best when the slot can stay fixed: a home tutor comes to your sector or society on the same days each week, and the student works at a proper desk with notebooks and school work to hand. Online classes are the alternative when traffic or a late bus squeezes weekday evenings, or when activity schedules keep changing. Hybrid, with a home class at the weekend and a shorter online class midweek, suits many MYP and DP students with busy weeks.

Home, online and hybrid classes each give something up. Home tutoring lets the tutor see the handwriting, the notebook and the child's attention, which matters most for PYP and younger MYP students, and a DP student can write a full past-paper answer while the tutor reads it line by line. The price is travel and rigid slots, since a late bus or a gate delay eats into the class. IB online classes in Gurgaon remove travel, so a class can start at 7:15 pm without anyone driving through evening traffic; the price is that a tired student can drift behind a screen, and a young child needs an adult nearby. Hybrid keeps one home class for depth and uses online for the second, shorter class, and it is often the easiest pattern to sustain across a full term.

Take Kabir, in MYP 4 near Sector 69 on the SPR, with cricket practice three evenings a week. A Saturday morning home class for Mathematics and a 40-minute online class on Wednesday night for Sciences give him two contact points without dropping practice. When his project deadline arrives, the Wednesday class moves to Monday for two weeks. That shuffle is simple online and awkward at home.

Home classes are the worse choice when the tutor would have to cross the city at rush hour for a 5:30 pm slot. Online is the worse choice for a nine-year-old, or for a DP student who keeps the camera off and the page blank. Neither choice is permanent. Modes can change between term time and holidays, and home classes often become easier in the summer break, when there is no school bus to wait for.
items: Home tuition: suits PYP and younger MYP students who need an adult's eye on the page
Online: suits late weekday slots when evening traffic makes travel unreasonable
Hybrid: weekend home class for depth, shorter online class midweek for doubts
Moving an online class for a project week is easier than moving a home slot

contentBlocks.heading: Checks to make before a tutor's class goes on the calendar
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram shortlists tutors only when their profiles are verified and match what you shared: board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule. That filter matters, but it does not replace your own judgement about whether a particular tutor will hold a weekly timetable well. A few checks are worth making yourself before any slot is fixed.

Stage experience comes first. A tutor who is strong in DP Maths at HL may not be the right person for an MYP 2 class built around criterion tasks, and one who knows PYP units of inquiry may never have marked a timed DP answer. Ask what they would do in week one and in week five for your child's stage, and how they would handle a school test that lands in the middle of the plan. A vague answer about building concepts is not a plan.

Next, a written plan for the first four to six weeks. It need not be elaborate. For a DP1 student it might read: weeks 1-2 on the unit the school just finished, week 3 a timed question checked against a markscheme, weeks 4-6 a step ahead of the next school unit. An MYP plan should name the criteria the coming task is marked on. With a PYP child, the plan connects to the current unit of inquiry and says what reading or number work sits underneath.

Last, the trial class itself, plus the practical side of home classes: an adult at home for younger children, the class held in a shared room rather than a closed bedroom, and an agreed rule on cancellations. Watch punctuality in the trial, since a tutor who arrives late to the first class seldom becomes punctual by the tenth. Keep a simple log of dates, topics and homework. If the log shows the plan drifting by week four, raise it with the tutor; if nothing changes, ask IB Gram for a different match.
items: The tutor has taught this exact stage, subject and level, not just the IB generally
A written four-to-six-week plan exists before the second week of classes
The trial class started on time and used the student's own school material
Home classes run in a shared room with an adult at home for younger children
A class log records topics, homework and questions attempted each week

contentBlocks.heading: IB DP classes in Gurugram: a DP2 year planned month by month
contentBlocks.body:
The summer between DP1 and DP2 is the most valuable holiday in the programme and the easiest to waste. IB summer classes in Gurgaon work best as two or three classes a week for four to six weeks, not daily sessions. Use them to repair the DP1 topics that went badly in end-of-year tests, to move the EE and any IA drafts forward within the school's own deadlines, so they do not collide with DP2 teaching, and to keep one timed question per subject going each week. Leave at least two weeks with no classes at all.

The outline below assumes DP2 begins after the summer break, the school's mocks fall several months before May, and exams are in the May session. Shift every stage to your school's dates. First two months back: one class a week per subject that needs support, following school teaching and clearing IA work before the school's draft deadlines. Third and fourth months: the same base, one past-paper question in every class, and a running list of weak topics. The month before mocks: IB revision classes in Gurgaon mean a second weekly class for the two weakest subjects only, with timed practice. Mock weeks: pause, or keep short check-ins. The month after mocks: re-plan from the marked scripts. Final months before May: shorter, more frequent classes organised by paper and command term. May itself: brief check-ins at most. Early July: results.

Riya, in DP2 in Sector 15 with Economics and Physics at HL, shows how that plays out. Through the first term she has one weekend class in each subject, because her weekday evenings already go to school homework and a CAS commitment. Four weeks before mocks her family adds a midweek online class for Physics, the weaker subject. Both classes stop during mock weeks. Afterwards Physics returns to weekly, and Economics drops to fortnightly because her mock script showed narrower gaps there.

The DP2 winter break needs a specific plan rather than a promise to study. If mocks come after the break, winter classes are mock preparation and should look like the month before mocks. If mocks come before it, the break is for fixing what the mocks exposed.
items: Summer after DP1: two or three classes a week for four to six weeks
DP2 first term: one steady weekly class for each subject needing support
Month before mocks: a second weekly class for the two weakest subjects only
Mock weeks: pause classes or keep short check-ins so papers are sat rested
After mocks: rebuild the plan subject by subject from the marked scripts

contentBlocks.heading: When should Gurgaon families reduce or pause IB classes?
contentBlocks.body:
Reduce classes once the student has kept up with school work without help for a full unit, and pause them during mock weeks, final examinations, illness or major travel. If a month of classes has produced no change in the work itself, review before booking more: ask whether the problem is the tutor, the timetable or something classes cannot fix.

Progress shows up in the work before it shows up in grades. After two or three weeks the student should be able to explain what was covered and should be bringing questions to class. After four to six weeks, homework should need fewer corrections, and answers should match the command term, so evaluate produces a judgement rather than a description. A change in school grades usually takes a full unit or a term, because tests are spaced out. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and no timetable of classes promises one.

Some problems are not fixed by adding classes. A DP student carrying four HL subjects and three evening activities may need fewer classes and more sleep. For an anxious MYP student, one class plus a conversation with the school can do more than a third session. A tired PYP child is often better served by shorter classes and reading at home with a parent. And sometimes a student does not need a tutor at all, only the discipline to hand in work they already know how to do.

Reducing should be planned rather than sudden: two classes a week down to one for a month, then a fortnightly check-in, with the option to add a class back before the next test. Tell the tutor why the pattern is changing. A tutor who knows the student is stepping down because a unit went well can set a short practice routine for the gap weeks, and that routine is usually what stops the improvement from fading.
items: Weeks 2-3: the student explains last week's class and arrives with questions
Weeks 4-6: fewer homework corrections and answers that match the command term
One unit or term: school test results start to reflect the work
Pause for mocks, final exams, illness, travel or a heavy project deadline
No change after a month: compare the class log with school work before booking more

contentBlocks.heading: Booking a trial class in Gurgaon: what to prepare and what to watch
contentBlocks.body:
Before the trial class, gather what a tutor needs to plan around: the subject list, with HL or SL marked for DP students; the current unit or task sheet; the last two marked tests or criterion feedback; the term calendar; and the fixed commitments across the week. For DP2, add mock dates if the school has published them. With a PYP child, the current unit of inquiry and a recent piece of reading or number work is enough.

A good trial class runs in the actual slot you plan to use, on a normal school day, so you see the real energy level and, for home classes, the real traffic. It should include a short conversation about what feels hard, some teaching on a topic the student has struggled with, one question attempted alone, and a few minutes at the end where the tutor tells you what they noticed and what the first month of classes would target. For a DP student, that question should be discussed in terms of its command term.

Afterwards, you should be able to answer a few things. Did the student talk, or only listen? Can they tell you one thing they now see differently? Did the tutor propose a specific weekly pattern with a reason, such as two Economics classes because an IA draft is due, or one Maths class because the gaps are narrow? Ask the student privately too, because a student who liked the tutor but understood nothing is giving you useful information. If the trial felt generic, say so and ask for a different match before committing.

Then fix the first four weeks only. Agree days, times, mode and what each class covers, and put a review date in the calendar at week four. If the school timetable changes after the first month, the plan changes with it. IB classes in Gurgaon that begin with a short, reviewed plan are far easier to adjust than a whole term booked on trust.
items: Bring the last two marked tests or criterion feedback to the trial class
Hold the trial in the real weekday slot, not a convenient Sunday morning
Expect a short spoken summary of gaps and a proposed weekly pattern
Fix only the first four weeks, with a review date set at week four

faqs.question: How many IB classes a week does a DP1 student need?
faqs.answer: Usually one class a week for each subject where the student genuinely needs support, with Higher Level subjects first in line. A DP1 student comfortable in four subjects but struggling in Chemistry HL and English HL might need only two classes a week, each 60 to 90 minutes. Adding classes for subjects that are going well mostly takes time from homework, CAS and sleep. Review the pattern at the end of each school unit, rather than adding classes on impulse after one poor test.

faqs.question: Can IB classes start in the middle of a school term?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a mid-term start is often better than waiting for the next term to begin. The first two or three classes should work on whatever the school is teaching now, so the student feels a difference in school straight away, while the tutor notes the older gaps and fills them gradually. The one time to hold back is the week of a school test or a coursework deadline. Start the week after, when a freshly marked paper gives the tutor something concrete to work from.

faqs.question: Should classes carry on during the school's mock examination weeks?
faqs.answer: Mostly no; pause classes or cut them to short check-ins while mocks are running. Mock weeks are demanding, and an evening class on top of them usually costs more in sleep than it gives back. A 20 to 30 minute online check-in the evening before a paper the student is anxious about can help, if the student asks for it. Restart normal classes within a week of the last mock, and use the marked scripts to decide which subjects need more time and which can drop to fortnightly.

faqs.question: My daughter comes home to Sector 84 on a late school bus. Is a 7 pm class too late?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily; a 7 pm class works if she has eaten, rested and has no heavy homework due the next morning. In New Gurgaon, late weekday classes are often better online, so no one is travelling across sectors in the evening, with a longer home class at the weekend. Keep weekday classes to about 45 to 60 minutes and avoid two late classes on consecutive nights. If she looks worn out in a trial class at that hour, move the slot rather than pushing through a term of tired evenings.

faqs.question: Is a weekend-only timetable enough for an MYP student in Palam Vihar?
faqs.answer: Often yes for MYP 1-3, provided the weekend class is long enough and the student does a little independent work midweek. Weekends suit Palam Vihar and the rest of Old Gurgaon because weekday traffic near the older markets can make early-evening home slots unreliable. A 90-minute Saturday class can cover one concept and one criterion task. The pattern gets harder in MYP 4 and 5, when projects and, where the school offers it, eAssessment preparation add work, so a short online midweek class is worth adding then.

faqs.question: Will IB holiday classes leave my child with no real break?
faqs.answer: They should not; a well-planned holiday keeps whole weeks free of classes. Without a school bus to catch, classes can move to late morning, when a student who has slept properly gets more done in an hour than on a tired school evening, so fewer classes achieve more. Keep to one subject a day, and set a small amount of independent work between classes instead of a daily timetable. Block family travel and rest weeks on the calendar before any class is booked. A student who returns to school exhausted has lost what the holiday was for.

faqs.question: Can classes be paused for CAS trips, school exchanges or family travel?
faqs.answer: Yes; tell the tutor early and agree the restart date before the pause begins, since keeping the same slot depends on the tutor's availability. A week or two away usually does little harm if the first class back picks up exactly where the plan stopped. Longer gaps need something in between, such as a short practice set or an online class from wherever the student is, if the time zone allows. Avoid pausing in the month before the school's mocks, when a missed fortnight is much harder to recover.

faqs.question: How long should a class be for a PYP child?
faqs.answer: Between 45 and 60 minutes is usually right, and shorter is fine for the youngest children. After a full school day, a six- or seven-year-old rarely concentrates for longer, and a class that runs past their attention turns into a struggle about sitting still. Break the time into two or three short activities linked to the current unit of inquiry, with reading or number work inside them. Two short classes a week often work better than one long one, and some children need only one.

faqs.question: We have had six weeks of classes and nothing has changed. What now?
faqs.answer: Review before you stop: check the plan, then the slot, then the fit. Look at the class log alongside the student's school work. If classes covered what the plan promised but answers still miss the command term, the teaching approach needs to change, and the tutor should say how. If classes were often cancelled or fell straight after a tiring activity, fix the timetable first. If the student and tutor simply do not work well together, ask IB Gram for a different match instead of adding more classes to a pattern that is failing.

faqs.question: Can a brother in MYP and a sister in DP have home classes back to back on the same evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, subject to tutor availability, and back-to-back home classes can make a busy week easier to manage. Put the younger student first, while attention is fresher, and give the DP student the longer second slot. The subjects and levels decide whether one home tutor can teach both, and often the two need different tutors. Even then, two consecutive home classes on one evening protect the rest of the week. Keep the sibling who is waiting out of the study room. In societies such as Tata Primanti on the SPR, register both tutors at the gate in advance so neither class starts late.

faqs.question: What happens when a home class is missed because of a school event or test?
faqs.answer: Usually the class moves to another slot rather than being lost, provided a rule for missed home classes was agreed at the start. Give the home tutor as much notice as you can, because by late afternoon they may already be on their way to your sector. Depending on their schedule, the tutor may swap to another evening that week or hold a shorter online class instead. Share the school calendar with the tutor so clashes are spotted a week ahead, not on the afternoon itself. If a clash is predictable, such as a monthly sports fixture, build an alternative slot into the timetable from the beginning.

introSummary: An IB DP tutor in Gurgaon helps a DP1 or DP2 student with the subjects that are losing marks and, where needed, with the whole Diploma load: HL and SL choices, IA deadlines, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge (TOK), mocks, predicted grades and the May exams. Families often start by asking for home tuition in one subject. Often the real problem is the load. A DP2 student with a shaky HL Chemistry grade is frequently also carrying three IA drafts and an EE that has stalled, and fixing the chemistry alone will not fix the week. This page covers how the 45 points work, the DP1 and DP2 pressure points, subject tutors versus mentors, and how IB Gram builds shortlists across Gurugram.

contentBlocks.heading: How do we shortlist an IB DP tutor in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
We shortlist by working out what the Diploma is asking of your child this term, then matching tutors whose verified profiles fit that need. You send a query or book a free consultation, and we ask about subjects and levels, the school calendar with its IA and EE deadlines, your sector and free weekly slots.

A subject list alone rarely tells us enough. Maths could mean Maths AA at HL for a student with engineering in mind, or Maths AI at SL for a student whose strengths lie elsewhere, and those call for different tutors. So we ask for all six subjects with their levels, not only the one that worries you. We also check which exam session the school enters students for. At most Gurgaon IB schools that is May, and it fixes the end point of every plan that follows.

Then comes the decision many families have not thought about. Does your child need one subject fixed, or someone watching the whole Diploma? A DP1 student who has lost confidence in HL Physics after the first unit test needs a Physics specialist. A DP2 student with respectable grades, four IA drafts outstanding, an EE that has stalled and a TOK essay not yet started usually needs a mentor, sometimes alongside one subject tutor. We will tell you which we think it is, and why, before a shortlist is drawn up.

Nothing is final until a demo or trial session has run. A strong profile cannot tell you whether your son or daughter will admit, in front of this particular adult, what they do not understand, and that admission is where DP tutoring starts. An IB DP tutor in Gurgaon who looks right on paper and feels wrong in the room is still the wrong tutor. If the match does not work a few weeks in, ask for a different one.

2. We ask about the syllabus, school calendar, IA and EE deadlines, sector and free slots.

contentBlocks.heading: How are the 45 IB Diploma points made up, and what does 24 mean?
contentBlocks.body:
The IB Diploma is scored out of 45. Six subjects are each graded 1 to 7, giving a maximum of 42, and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) together add up to 3 more. Twenty-four points is the minimum total for the diploma, but only when none of the IB's failing conditions applies.

The Diploma Programme (DP) is a two-year course, DP1 and DP2, made up of six subjects from six groups. Three or four are taken at Higher Level (HL), each with 240 recommended teaching hours, and the rest at Standard Level (SL), with 150 hours each. The gap is bigger than families expect. An HL course is not an SL course with a few harder questions added, and four HLs make a noticeably heavier two years than three. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) carries no points, but it must be completed.

Put numbers on it. A student who earns a 4 in every subject reaches 24 before TOK and the EE add anything. A student with 6, 6 and 5 at HL and 6, 5 and 5 at SL holds 33 subject points, and TOK and the EE can take that to 36 at most. Those 3 points look small, but TOK and the EE carry a sharper risk: an E in either TOK or the EE is a failing condition, so a student can hold 30 subject points and still leave without the diploma. Unfinished CAS has the same effect, and the DP coordinator can give you the full list of failing conditions.

The final exams sit at the end of DP2. The IB runs May and November sessions, most Gurgaon IB schools use May, and May results are released in early July. An IB Diploma tutor in Gurgaon should plan backwards from that end point, because the school's coursework deadlines all come before it.
items: Maximum 45 points: six subjects graded 1-7, plus up to 3 from TOK and the EE.
24 points is the minimum, but an E in TOK or the EE is a failing condition.
HL subjects carry 240 recommended teaching hours; SL subjects carry 150.
Sessions run in May and November; May results are released in early July.

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing HL and SL subjects, and spotting a wrong choice in DP1
contentBlocks.body:
HL and SL choices decide how heavy the two years feel and which university courses stay open later. Many universities abroad publish IB entry requirements as a points total, and some also ask for particular grades in named HL subjects. That makes the choice partly a university decision taken by a sixteen-year-old who may not have settled on a course. Before HL choices are fixed, check the published requirements for every course on a rough shortlist.

The first weeks of DP1 show whether the choice was sound. A poor first test is not, on its own, a reason to drop an HL. Look at how the marks were lost. A student who understands the lesson but runs out of time needs practice. A foundational gap, such as algebra that never settled before the Diploma, can still be closed, but it costs hours the student may not have. And if one HL is swallowing the time meant for other subjects, the true cost shows up elsewhere. Schools set their own window for level changes, so ask the DP coordinator about it in the first term.

This is where a DP1 tutor in Gurgaon can help for a few weeks rather than two years. An IB HL tutor in Gurgaon who teaches the course can read the first tests and say whether the difficulty is fixable. An IB SL tutor in Gurugram does a different job, because SL subjects are often carried beside three demanding HLs and efficiency matters more than extension.

One assessment structure repeats across three sciences. In DP Physics, Chemistry and Biology, first assessed in 2025, Paper 1 has two parts, 1A multiple choice and 1B data-based questions, and Paper 2 has short-answer and extended-response questions. HL and SL share that structure, with HL adding Additional Higher Level (AHL) content. The internal assessment is a scientific investigation worth 20%, marked on four criteria of 6 marks each (Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation), in a maximum of 3,000 words.
items: Check each university course's published IB requirements before HL choices are final.
Judge a DP1 struggle by how marks were lost, not by the first score.
Ask the DP coordinator when your school's window for level changes closes.
Science IA: four criteria of 6 marks each, maximum 3,000 words, worth 20%.

contentBlocks.heading: DP home tuition across Gurgaon: sectors, societies and evening slots
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram shortlists DP tutors for families across Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana, and in every corridor the practical question is the same: when does a Diploma student have a free and alert hour? After school, CAS commitments and a TOK or EE meeting, weekday evenings are short, and evening traffic can stretch even a short trip between sectors. Where the student lives shapes which subjects are taught at home and which move online.

On Golf Course Road, in DLF Phase 5, DLF Phase 1, Sector 42, Sector 43, Sector 53, Sector 54, Ardee City and Wazirabad, home tuition for HL Maths and the sciences is often workable when the tutor is already based nearby. Societies such as DLF The Magnolias, DLF The Aralias, DLF Park Place, DLF The Crest and DLF The Belaire usually register visitors at the gate, so give security the tutor's name before the first session.

Golf Course Extension Road calls for a different plan. In Sector 56, Sector 57, Sector 58, Sector 59, Sector 60, Sector 62 and Sector 65, Sushant Lok 3, Ghata and Gwal Pahari, and in towers such as M3M Golf Estate, Ireo Grand Arch and Ireo Skyon, a hybrid week is often the sensible default in DP2. One home session at the weekend covers the heaviest HL subject, and shorter online sessions on weekdays handle IA and EE feedback.

In DLF Phase 2, DLF Phase 3 and DLF Phase 4, around MG Road and Cyber City, and in Sikanderpur, Chakkarpur, Sector 24, Sector 27 and Sector 28, office traffic fills the early evening. Families in DLF Beverly Park, Heritage City, DLF Hamilton Court, DLF Regency Park, DLF Richmond Park and Ambience Caitriona often do better with a later weekday slot or a weekend morning.
