contentBlocks.heading: The DP1 to DP2 calendar that Gurgaon families plan around
contentBlocks.body:
Parents at Gurgaon schools such as Pathways World School, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, The Shri Ram School, Aravali, and Heritage Xperiential Learning School each work to their own school's calendar, and those calendars differ. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel, and this page makes no claim about which programmes any of these schools offers. Treat what follows as a shape and take the dates from your own school.

DP1 starts deceptively calm. The first term is for settling HL and SL choices, and it is the easiest time to repair a weak foundation. At many schools the EE begins later in DP1: choosing a subject, meeting the supervisor at school and recording the first reflection session. IA planning and work towards the TOK exhibition often start in the same stretch. The exhibition uses three objects linked to one of 35 IA prompts, in up to 950 words. A student who drifts through DP1 rarely feels the cost until DP2, when it arrives all at once.

DP2 is where the pressure points cluster. IA season is rarely one deadline: a student might owe drafts in four or five subjects within a few weeks, alongside the final EE of up to 4,000 words and roughly 40 hours of work. The TOK essay, on one of six prescribed titles released for the session, in up to 1,600 words, often lands in the same stretch. Mocks and the school's predicted grades come round too, in an order that differs between schools. A DP2 tutor in Gurgaon who joins now has to work inside that calendar, not beside it.

Then comes the run to May, with results in early July. IB DP exam preparation in Gurgaon has its own page, and the point here is narrower. Every hour lost to a late IA in DP2 comes out of revision time.
items: Early DP1: settle HL and SL choices and repair weak foundations.
Later DP1 at many schools: EE subject, supervisor meetings and the first reflection.
TOK exhibition: three objects linked to one of 35 prompts, up to 950 words.
DP2: IA drafts, the final EE, the TOK essay, mocks and predicted grades crowd together.

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or hybrid: which works for a DP student in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
For many Diploma students in Gurgaon, hybrid works best: home lessons for the heaviest HL subject, where handwritten working and timed practice benefit from someone at the table, and online sessions for IA, EE and TOK feedback on shared documents. Pure home suits a student who drifts on screens; pure online suits crowded evenings and scarce subjects.

Home tuition earns its travel time with HL Maths and the sciences. The tutor watches a student work through a long question, sees exactly where the method breaks and corrects it on the page. An IB DP home tutor in Gurugram is also harder to ignore after a long school day. The trade-off is plain. Home tutoring depends on a tutor based within reach of your sector. They are the hardest to fit into weekday evenings, and a cancelled session is harder to move.

An IB DP online tutor solves different problems. IA and EE drafts are documents, and comments left on a shared file often do more than feedback given across a table and half forgotten by morning. Online also widens the field. If your child needs a specialist in a less common HL subject, the right person may be at the other end of Gurgaon, and online makes that tutor possible. Its weakness is attention. Online needs a student who logs in on time with the work ready, and it gives a disengaged DP2 student plenty of room to hide.

Hybrid is harder to organise and easier to live with. A student in Sector 57 might take HL Chemistry at home each Saturday and two short online slots on weekdays for IA drafts and TOK discussion. It needs one timetable everyone can see, and a clear rule about which work belongs to which session, or the online slots quietly turn into extra Chemistry. An IB DP tutor in Gurgaon who teaches hybrid well will set that rule in the first week.
items: Home: strongest for HL Maths and sciences, handwritten working and timed practice.
Online: strongest for IA, EE and TOK draft feedback on shared documents.
Hybrid: heaviest subject at home, drafts and discussion online during the week.
Home depends on where the tutor is based; online depends on student discipline.

contentBlocks.heading: Checking a Diploma tutor before the first lesson
contentBlocks.body:
Every tutor on an IB Gram shortlist has a verified profile that matches the needs you described. Verification tells you the profile is genuine. It cannot tell you whether this person will work with your child, and nobody should pretend it can. That part is yours to judge, and a demo or trial session is where you judge it.

Start with currency. The Diploma changes, and a tutor teaching from old notes misleads a student in small ways that add up to lost marks. Ask a science tutor how Paper 1 is now split into 1A and 1B, and how the investigation is marked on its four criteria. Ask anyone offering EE help which guide they work from. The EE guide was updated for first assessment in 2027, so criterion breakdowns copied from older material are unreliable, and your child should follow the version the DP coordinator issues.

Then ask about boundaries. An IB Diploma tutor in Gurgaon may question a research question, point out a weak evaluation or ask the student to justify a claim. The tutor must not write, rewrite or quietly polish assessed work. The EE is supervised by a teacher at the student's school, with reflection sessions recorded along the way, and outside help that shows up as a sudden change in the student's writing puts the student, not the tutor, in difficulty. A good answer to this question sounds careful. A vague one is a warning.

In the trial, notice what the tutor asks before teaching anything. A tutor who wants to see the last school test, the teacher's comments and the IA deadline list is diagnosing. One who launches into a prepared lecture is not. Afterwards, ask your child two things: could they say what they did not understand, and would they say it to this tutor next week? The second answer matters more.
items: Profiles are verified before shortlisting; fit is tested in the demo or trial.
Ask science tutors about Paper 1A, Paper 1B and the four IA criteria.
Ask EE mentors which guide they use, since it was updated for 2027.
Confirm the tutor comments on IA and EE drafts and never writes them.

contentBlocks.heading: Does your child need a subject tutor or a DP mentor?
contentBlocks.body:
Your child needs a subject tutor if one or two subjects are losing marks while deadlines and the rest of the load are under control. A DP mentor makes more sense when the problem is the whole Diploma: several IAs due together, a stalled EE, TOK slipping and no working plan. Some DP2 students need both for a while.

The single-subject route is simpler and, for many students, enough. An IB DP Maths tutor who works on HL problem-solving once or twice a week, or an IB DP Physics tutor in Gurgaon who fixes how a student handles data-based questions, will often move that subject on its own. It suits a student who is organised, meets school deadlines and has one clear weak spot. A mentor would be wasted on that student.

A DP mentor works across subjects. The job is to hold the calendar, set the week's priorities, read drafts for structure and argument, keep the EE moving between supervisor meetings and notice when TOK has been left too late. A mentor does not replace specialist teaching in HL Chemistry, and a good one says so. Mentoring suits the capable but overloaded student whose grades are decent and whose week is chaos, and the student who has lost a term to illness or a family move.

The clearest test is the IA stack. Picture a DP2 student in Ardee City with four IA deadlines, in Physics, Biology, Maths and Economics, inside a few weeks, and the EE final draft and TOK essay behind them. Nobody writes four assessed pieces well in parallel, let alone six. A workable method starts with one sheet holding every school draft date and final deadline, then works back from each. Science data collection comes first, because students may investigate in groups of up to three but each writes an individual report. Where the student controls the timing, avoid finishing two drafts in the same week. Keeping that sheet honest is most of what a mentor is for.
items: Subject tutor: one or two weak subjects, with deadlines otherwise under control.
DP mentor: several IAs, the EE and TOK slipping at the same time.
Put every school IA draft date and final deadline on a single sheet.
Collect group science data early; each student still writes an individual report.

contentBlocks.heading: When should progress show, and where do predicted grades fit?
contentBlocks.body:
Expect better habits within the first few weeks and better school marks over a term, not a fortnight. Predicted grades are set by teachers and usually draw on a longer record of tests, mocks and coursework, so tutoring that begins shortly before predictions are issued helps with the assessments still to come but rarely rewrites that record.

Predicted grades matter because of timing. May results arrive in early July, and many universities abroad make offers well before then, so the predicted grade is often the figure an admissions team actually weighs. A prediction two points short of a course's requirement can cost the offer, however well May goes. Families asking for help with IB predicted grades usually hope for a shortcut. There is not one. What moves a prediction is steadier work in the tests and coursework teachers are already watching, plus an early conversation with the school's university counsellor about how and when predictions are set.

In the first month, look for small, visible things. The student arrives with questions, corrections from school tests get done, and the IA sheet is current. By the end of a term, marks in the target subject should be starting to move and the late nights before deadlines should be fewer. If none of that has happened after a month, talk to the tutor before changing anything.

No tutor can guarantee a grade, a prediction or the diploma, and an honest IB DP tutor in Gurgaon will tell you so on the first call. A student carrying four HLs they never wanted may need a conversation with the DP coordinator more than extra lessons. A late start in DP2 narrows the job to protecting the subjects closest to the next grade. And some students do not need a tutor at all: an organised student with steady marks and a responsive teacher may need nothing more than a clear calendar.
items: First few weeks: questions brought to sessions, test corrections done, IA sheet current.
Predicted grades draw on a longer record, so late tutoring shifts them slowly.
Ask the university counsellor how and when your school issues predicted grades.
No tutor can guarantee a grade, a prediction or the diploma.

contentBlocks.heading: Starting with an IBDP tutor in Gurgaon: what to have ready
contentBlocks.body:
The first conversation goes faster with a few things to hand. Have the six subjects with their levels, the latest report or test results, the school's IA and EE deadline list if it has been shared, and a note of when your child is genuinely free. Mention the exam session, your sector and whether home tuition, online or hybrid suits the household. If your child has already met the DP coordinator about levels or deadlines, note what was said.

Share university plans too, even vague ones. A student thinking about medicine abroad and one leaning towards design are managing different risks inside the same Diploma, and the shortlist should reflect that. Be candid about what has not worked before: a previous tutor who lectured, a batch class that ignored IA work, or a student who resents being tutored at all. That last one changes the match more than any subject does.

The first session is mostly diagnosis. A good tutor looks at recent tests and teacher comments, asks the student to talk through a question they got wrong, and checks where each IA and the EE stand against the school's dates. You may want to sit in for the opening part and then leave; many DP students speak more freely once a parent has gone. By the end, the student should know the next two weeks of work, and you should know how the tutor will report back. For mentoring, expect the first session to produce the single deadline sheet, with every school date on it.

If the trial feels wrong, say so straight away. Changing tutors in week two is far easier than discovering during DP2 mocks that the arrangement never worked. And a DP1 student with no immediate crisis can start lightly while HL choices settle, then step up once EE and IA work begins.
items: Six subjects with HL or SL levels, plus the latest report or test results.
School IA, EE and TOK deadlines, and the exam session your child is entered for.
Your sector, free weekly slots and a preference for home, online or hybrid.
First session: diagnosis, a two-week work plan and how updates will reach you.

faqs.question: Is 24 points enough to be awarded the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Twenty-four is the minimum total, but it is not enough on its own. The diploma is withheld if any of the IB's failing conditions applies, and two rules matter from the start of DP1: an E grade in either Theory of Knowledge or the Extended Essay is a failing condition, and Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) must be completed. So a student with 28 subject points and an E in TOK does not receive the diploma.

faqs.question: Can my child still move from HL to SL during DP1?
faqs.answer: Possibly, but only within the window your school allows, so ask the DP coordinator now rather than at the end of term. The longer a student waits, the more IA planning and classwork have been built on the original choice. Before asking, check two things. Does any university course your child is considering name that subject at HL? And is the difficulty really about the level, or about a gap that a few weeks of focused help could close?

faqs.question: My daughter is doing well in five subjects but struggling in HL Maths. Does she need a DP mentor?
faqs.answer: Probably not, because a subject specialist is the simpler and better choice for a student with one clear weak spot. An IB DP Maths tutor working with her on HL problem-solving targets the actual problem. A mentor adds planning and draft-reading across subjects, which an organised student does not need. If her IA deadlines start slipping in DP2, or Maths begins eating the hours meant for other subjects, revisit the question then.

faqs.question: How can a tutor help with predicted grades without doing my child's work?
faqs.answer: A tutor helps by strengthening the work teachers already see, never by touching assessed drafts. Teachers base predictions on the record in front of them, so the useful help is steady: stronger answers in school tests, better-planned IAs and an EE that stays on schedule. A tutor can challenge an argument or point out a weak evaluation. Writing or rewriting any part of an IA, the EE or TOK work is an academic integrity problem, and it is the student who carries the consequences.

faqs.question: My son has four IA deadlines in the same month. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: Start with whichever IA still needs data, because that IA cannot be written until the data exists. Then sort the rest by stage: not started, drafted or nearly final. A nearly final IA deserves an evening, not a week. If two deadlines clash, your son should raise it with his teachers early, since a request made weeks ahead lands differently from one made the night before. And if the list still cannot be met, that is when a DP mentor earns a place.

faqs.question: We live in Sector 67 near the Southern Peripheral Road. Will a home tutor come on weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: It depends on tutor availability and where the matched tutor is based. Along the SPR, in Sector 66, Sector 68, Sector 70 and Sector 72, Ansal Esencia, Bhondsi and societies such as Tata Primanti, home tutoring works when a suitable tutor lives within reach. Evening traffic can stretch a short trip, though, and a specialist in a less common HL subject may be based across Gurgaon. A practical arrangement is often a weekend home lesson with weekday sessions online.

faqs.question: The tutor is not working out. Can we change without starting from scratch?
faqs.answer: Yes: tell IB Gram what is not working and ask for a different match. The subjects, levels, calendar, deadlines and schedule you shared at the start still apply, so the new shortlist does not start from zero. Be specific about the problem. Too much lecturing, no attention to the IA drafts or two cancellations in mock week each point towards a different kind of tutor. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit again.

faqs.question: It has been a month of DP tutoring and the marks have not moved. Should we stop?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, because a month is usually too short for school marks to move. What should have changed is how your child works in that subject, so ask the tutor what they have diagnosed and what you should see a month from now. Write the answer down. If it is vague, ask IB Gram for a different match. If it is specific and your child is doing the work, give it that month and hold the tutor to the answer.

faqs.question: Should a DP1 student start tutoring straight away or wait for the first school report?
faqs.answer: Wait a few weeks unless there is a gap you already know about, such as shaky algebra going into HL Maths. The early weeks of DP1 show how your child copes with the volume of HL work. But do not wait for the end of term. If the first tests show marks lost for reasons the student cannot explain, a few weeks with a DP1 tutor in Gurgaon, before the school's level-change window closes, can settle whether the subject choices are right.

faqs.question: We live in DLF Phase 3 and our daughter's evenings are full of CAS and school activities. Is home tutoring realistic in DP2?
faqs.answer: It can be, if the slot is chosen around her energy and the traffic. Early-evening traffic around Cyber City and MG Road can stretch a short trip, so a later weekday slot or a weekend morning at home often holds up better. Societies such as DLF Beverly Park and Heritage City usually want the tutor's name at the gate. If weekday evenings are truly full, keep home tuition for her heaviest HL subject and move IA feedback online.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram match an MYP student with a tutor in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram matches an MYP student by starting with evidence, not a subject name. You send a query or book a free consultation. The detail matters because 'MYP tutor' covers very different jobs. A Grade 6 student who has never planned a two-week task needs someone patient with routines and planners. For a Grade 9 student losing levels on written explanations in sciences, the right person reads rubrics line by line. An MYP 5 student running a Personal Project alongside every other subject's deadlines needs a tutor who can plan backwards from school checkpoints. So the most useful thing you can share on the first call is recent marked work: two or three tasks with their criterion scores and the teacher's comments. A report-card grade tells a tutor what happened. The task tells them why.

Subject knowledge alone is not the test. A tutor who has taught CBSE Class 10 science well for years can still mark an MYP task the way a board examiner would, rewarding the correct final answer when the rubric asks for far more. So MYP experience sits beside subject depth on the shortlist, not behind it. The school calendar matters too: a tutor with free Tuesdays in a quiet month may have no room in the fortnight before unit deadlines, exactly when an MYP student needs help. And where the closest suitable tutor lives across the city, online or hybrid lessons are often the sensible route to an IB MYP tutor in Gurgaon who genuinely knows the criteria.

contentBlocks.heading: MYP 1 to MYP 5, and how the last two years shape DP choices
contentBlocks.body:
The MYP lasts five years, MYP 1 to MYP 5, for students of roughly 11 to 16, which families here usually know as Grades 6 to 10. Students study across eight subject groups, and every subject is assessed against four criteria. Two projects sit inside the programme: the Community Project in MYP 3 or 4, and the Personal Project in MYP 5. MYP 5 can also bring eAssessment, made up of on-screen examinations plus ePortfolios, but it is optional and each school decides whether to offer it.

What a tutor does changes with the year. In MYP 1 and 2 the work is mostly habits: reading a task sheet, keeping a planner, handing in drafts on time. MYP 3 is often the first pinch point, because tasks get longer and the Community Project may begin that year or the next, so a Grade 8 IB tutor in Gurgaon usually spends more time on planning and research than on content. By MYP 4 and 5 the stakes feel real, and there is less room to learn habits slowly.

The DP that follows is a two-year course of six subjects from six groups, with three or four at Higher Level (HL, 240 recommended teaching hours) and the rest at Standard Level (SL, 150 hours). That gap in hours is why MYP 4 and 5 matter: they are the last low-stakes chance to find out which subjects a student can sustain at depth. Judge the pattern across a year, not one final grade. A student whose Individuals and Societies scores hold up on every task, long research pieces included, has real evidence for HL there.

A tutor's role here is modest but useful: showing the student where their scores come from and helping them prepare questions for the school's DP coordinator, who can explain the school's rules on subject combinations. The choice belongs to the student, the family and the school.
items: Community Project in MYP 3 or 4; Personal Project in MYP 5.
MYP 5 eAssessment is optional, and each school decides whether to offer it.
DP HL subjects carry 240 recommended teaching hours; SL subjects carry 150.
Treat a full year of MYP 4-5 criterion scores as evidence for HL choices.

contentBlocks.heading: How does an MYP criterion score become a 1-7 grade?
contentBlocks.body:
Each MYP subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, and each criterion is scored from 0 to 8. The four scores are added together to give a total out of 32, and the IB's grade boundaries convert that total into a final grade from 1 to 7. So every criterion carries a quarter of the weight.

A worked example makes the point. Say a student's criterion scores in MYP Sciences are 7, 6, 3 and 4, a total of 20 out of 32. Pushing the 7 up to an 8 adds one mark. Lifting the 3 to a 6 adds three, and it is usually the more realistic gain, because a low score on one criterion tends to trace back to one repeatable habit, such as never explaining why a result looks the way it does. Which grade 20 or 23 falls into depends on the boundaries, and the school's MYP coordinator can show you how they apply.

The same arithmetic plays out differently by subject. An MYP science tutor in Gurgaon spends much of the time on written reasoning: why a method was chosen, what a set of results shows and what limits the conclusion. In MYP Language and Literature, an MYP English tutor in Gurgaon works on building an argument about a text with precise evidence. For MYP Individuals and Societies the gap is usually research: framing a question, then finding, citing and weighing sources. MYP Mathematics has its own logic, and a maths specialist should handle that depth.

Good MYP criteria help follows the same order every time. The tutor reads the task rubric first, then the student's work, then the teacher's comment, and picks the single lowest criterion to work on. The next task is then planned against that criterion from the first day, and the student checks the draft against the rubric before handing it in.
items: The criterion total out of 32 converts to a 1-7 grade through IB boundaries.
Lifting the lowest criterion usually moves the total more than polishing the highest.
Sciences: written reasoning about method and results, not only correct answers.
Language and Literature: an argument about a text, backed by precise evidence.
Individuals and Societies: framing questions, citing sources and weighing them.

contentBlocks.heading: School calendars and MYP 5 pressure points for Gurgaon families
contentBlocks.body:
Gurgaon has many schools, among them Pathways World School; Lancers International School; Scottish High International School; GD Goenka World School; The Shri Ram School, Aravali; and Heritage Xperiential Learning School. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. This page does not say which programmes any named school offers, so confirm that, and every date, with the school itself.

At international schools in Gurgaon generally, MYP tasks run over several weeks with a draft or checkpoint along the way, and several subjects can land their deadlines in the same fortnight near the end of a term. That is where Grade 7 and 8 students who were coping start to slip. Nothing is individually hard. There is simply too much due at once, and a student who has not planned backwards ends up writing three tasks in four evenings. A tutor who sees the term's task calendar can spread the load; one who only sees tonight's homework cannot.

MYP 5 stacks more on top: Personal Project milestones, DP subject-choice discussions and, where the school offers it, eAssessment. An MYP eAssessment tutor works on what is different about on-screen examinations, such as typing extended answers under time and planning before typing. Students who write well on paper sometimes lose their structure on screen, so practice belongs on a computer, using any practice material the school provides, and it should begin well before the sitting. For ePortfolios, ask the coordinator what the school needs and by when; the tutor's job there is keeping the student on schedule and the work entirely the student's own.

The winter break, or the summer before MYP 5, is a calmer time to fix one weak criterion or sketch a Personal Project plan.

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or hybrid: which suits an MYP learner in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
For MYP 1 to 3, home lessons usually work best, because younger students need someone beside them to build routines and stay focused. For MYP 4 and 5, online lessons handle draft feedback and project planning well. Hybrid, with home sessions for teaching and short online check-ins before deadlines, often suits a busy MYP 5 student.

Put plainly, the three modes compare like this for an MYP student. Home tutoring lets the tutor see how the student actually works, from the desk and the planner to whether the school laptop is open on the right task; its weakness is travel, gate entry and a smaller pool of tutors who can reach your sector. An MYP online tutor can be chosen from a much wider group and can put a draft beside its rubric on screen, but an 11- or 12-year-old drifts more easily on a screen. Hybrid pairs a home session for teaching and planning with an online check-in timed to a school checkpoint. It needs more coordination but follows the MYP rhythm of long tasks with sharp deadlines.

Take a Grade 10 student in Ireo Skyon with a Personal Project checkpoint and a sciences task due in the same week. A Saturday home session plans both. A shorter online session on Wednesday evening checks the science draft against its rubric, and nobody has to drive along Golf Course Extension Road to do it. For a Grade 6 child in Malibu Towne on Sohna Road who forgets to open the planner, the same pattern fails. That child needs someone at the table.

Home is not automatically better, though. If the only tutor who can reach your home has never worked with MYP criteria, an IB MYP tutor in Gurgaon who teaches online and reads rubrics well will usually help more. Decide on the mode after the first marked task comes back, not after the first week.
items: Home: best for MYP 1-3 routines, limited by travel and evening traffic.
Online: the widest choice of MYP-experienced tutors, but it needs a focused student.
Hybrid: home teaching plus short online check-ins timed to school checkpoints.
A criteria-savvy online tutor usually beats a nearby tutor who has never taught MYP.

contentBlocks.heading: Checking an IB middle years tutor before lessons begin
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and whose experience matches what you described. Verification tells you the profile is genuine. It cannot tell you whether this person will suit a 13-year-old who goes quiet when corrected, or whether they understand criterion-based marking as well as they say. That part is yours to check, and the demo session is the place to do it.

Five questions sort most candidates quickly. Ask the tutor to explain, in two minutes, how four criterion scores become a 1-7 grade; an experienced MYP tutor will do it plainly and point you to the school's coordinator for the boundaries. Hand over one real marked task and ask how they would use its rubric with your child next week. Ask what they will and will not do on the Personal Project, and notice whether they raise the limits before you prompt them. Ask whether they have taught students who moved from CBSE or ICSE, and what they changed first. Finally, ask how they would prepare an MYP 5 student at a school that does not offer eAssessment.

During the demo, watch the balance of talk. In a good MYP session the student spends much of the time explaining their own work, with the tutor asking rather than telling. Be wary if the tutor picks up a pen and starts rewriting your child's paragraph, promises a particular grade, or offers to 'take care of' the project. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and a tutor who implies otherwise is telling you something about how they work.

For home lessons, share the society's gate-entry process in advance, keep sessions in a common room rather than a bedroom, and stay at home for the first few sessions with a younger child. None of this signals distrust. It simply gives everyone a clear, comfortable routine from the start.
items: Hand over one real marked task and watch how the rubric gets used.
Ask directly what they will and will not do on the Personal Project.
Treat any promise of a particular grade as a reason to keep looking.
For home lessons, arrange gate entry and keep sessions in a common room.

contentBlocks.heading: Why do CBSE and ICSE students struggle in their first MYP term?
contentBlocks.body:
They struggle because MYP work is judged against criteria, not against a single correct answer. A student from CBSE or ICSE often writes short, accurate responses and then loses levels wherever the task rubric asks for explanation, organisation or reflection. The knowledge is usually fine. The habits the rubric rewards are new.

The problems tend to arrive in a predictable order. The first marked task comes back with a 3 or a 4 on a criterion the student expected to do well on, and the family reads it as a failing percentage. Next, the long deadlines bite. CBSE and ICSE homework is often due the next day, while an MYP task may run for three weeks with a checkpoint in the middle, so the student leaves everything for the last two evenings. Then comes research: copying a paragraph from a website without naming the source may have passed unnoticed before, but in an MYP classroom it usually becomes an academic integrity conversation.

Consider a student who topped her ICSE class and joins MYP 4 in Grade 9. Her first Individuals and Societies task comes back with a 6 on one criterion and a 2 on another, because she answered every question set but never questioned her sources. Extra content lessons would be the wrong fix. What she needs is a handful of sessions on reading the rubric before writing, planning the task against it and checking the draft against it again.

This is where MYP criteria help earns its keep. In the first month a tutor rebuilds the basics: opening the rubric before starting, working from a planner that counts back from each deadline, and redrafting at least once. Parents can help by dropping comparisons with old board percentages entirely. Expect the change to show on the next task, not the one already handed in, and start early if your child joins in MYP 5, when there is the least time to adjust.
items: Leaving a three-week task until the final two evenings before the deadline.
Copying website text without naming a source, which schools treat as an integrity issue.
Reading a 4 out of 8 as a percentage and panicking at home.
Writing reflections as a summary of what was done, not what was learned.

contentBlocks.heading: Progress, honest limits and MYP Personal Project help
contentBlocks.body:
Progress in the MYP shows up in habits before it shows up in scores. In the first few weeks, look for a student who opens the rubric without being reminded and can name the criterion they are working on. When the first task completed with the tutor is marked, look for movement on the one criterion the lessons targeted. Over a term, the signs are fewer late-night rescues, steadier criterion scores across subjects and a student who can explain a teacher's comment in their own words. No tutor can guarantee a grade.

There are also things a tutor cannot do. A task already submitted stays marked as it is. Weekly lessons will not fix a student who does no work between them. Starting a few weeks before a major MYP 5 deadline narrows the options to damage control. And some students do not need a tutor at all, because a clear planner, a conversation with the class teacher and a parent who checks the school platform once a week are sometimes enough.

The Personal Project needs its own rules, since this is where outside help most easily crosses a line. Legitimate MYP Personal Project help means asking questions until a vague interest becomes a goal the student can realistically achieve in the time, building a timeline around the school's checkpoints, teaching how to find, read and cite sources, and pointing out where the reasoning in a draft is thin.

What a tutor may not do is just as clear. The tutor does not choose the topic, make or fix the product, write or reword any part of the report, supply sources the student has not read, or help create evidence of a process that did not happen. The school's academic integrity policy applies to every word, so tell the teacher overseeing the project that outside help is involved. The Community Project in MYP 3 or 4 follows the same logic.
items: First marked task: movement on the one criterion the lessons targeted.
Personal Project: a tutor may question, plan and teach research and citation.
Personal Project: a tutor may not choose the topic, make the product or write.
Tell the teacher overseeing the project that outside help is involved.

contentBlocks.heading: Starting IB MYP tuition in Gurgaon: what to prepare
contentBlocks.body:
Starting IB MYP tuition in Gurgaon goes faster when a few things are ready before the first call. Gather two or three recent marked tasks with their criterion scores and teacher comments, plus the rubric and deadline for the next task in the subject that worries you most. If the school posts tasks on an online platform, a screenshot of the term's task calendar helps. Note your sector or society, and the weekday hours that are genuinely free once school buses, activities and dinner are accounted for.

For an MYP 5 student, add a few more details: where the Personal Project stands against the school's checkpoints, whether the school offers eAssessment, and when DP subject choices are due. An MYP 5 tutor in Gurugram planning the year needs this, because all of it competes for the same evenings. If you do not know the answers yet, the school's MYP coordinator will, and asking before the demo saves a session.

The first session, often the demo itself, should be diagnostic rather than a lecture. A good IB MYP tutor in Gurgaon reads a marked task alongside the student, asks the student to explain why they think a criterion scored low, picks one criterion to work on and agrees a small plan for the next checkpoint. With a Grade 6 or 7 child, a fair share of that first session may go on the planner and the school platform instead of subject content, which is exactly right at that age. Ask the tutor to keep the last few minutes for telling you what they noticed and what they would do next.

If the demo does not feel right, say so. A different match can be requested, and it is far better to ask early than to push through a whole term with the wrong fit.
items: Two or three recent marked tasks, with criterion scores and teacher comments.
The rubric and deadline for the next task in the weakest subject.
MYP 5: Personal Project stage, eAssessment status and DP choice deadlines.
Your sector or society, and the weekday hours that are genuinely free.

faqs.question: What does a score of 5 out of 8 on one MYP criterion mean?
faqs.answer: It means the work was placed at level 5 on one of the four criteria for that subject, and it should not be read as 62 per cent. The four criterion scores, each out of 8, add up to a total out of 32, and the IB's grade boundaries turn that total into a 1-7 grade. A single 5 tells you little until you see the other three. Ask for all four, then read the teacher's comment on the lowest, which usually points to the quickest gain on the next task.

faqs.question: My daughter moved from CBSE into MYP 4 and her first science task scored low. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: Yes, a low first criterion score is common after a move from CBSE, and it usually does not mean the science itself is weak. Board-exam habits reward the accurate answer, whereas an MYP rubric often wants written reasoning about how the work was done and what the results show. Before booking content lessons, ask the science teacher which criterion scored lowest and why. An MYP science tutor in Gurgaon can then target that one criterion before the next task.

faqs.question: Does a Personal Project tutor need to know the project's subject?
faqs.answer: No, a tutor guiding the Personal Project needs to be good at planning, questioning and research habits far more than at the topic itself. Picture a student in Nirvana Country designing a composting system for the society garden. The useful tutor asks what success would look like, how the student will measure it, which sources are reliable and what the next school checkpoint needs. A composting expert may be tempted to improve the design directly, which quietly turns the product into the tutor's work.

faqs.question: Our school does not offer MYP eAssessment. Does my child still need exam practice in MYP 5?
faqs.answer: Not for eAssessment itself, because it is optional and each school decides whether to offer it, so the school's own MYP 5 assessments are what matter. Ask the MYP coordinator what those look like and practise that format. Some timed writing is still worth doing. DP examination sessions run in May, the session most Gurgaon IB schools use, and November, and a student who has rarely written under time in the MYP will find those papers harder to pace.

faqs.question: Do MYP 5 grades decide which DP subjects my child can take at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: They can influence it, but whether MYP grades affect HL entry depends on the school, so ask the DP coordinator well before choices are due. HL carries far more teaching hours than SL, so a poor fit costs a lot of time. Look at MYP 4 and 5 criterion scores in that subject across the whole year, and if they dip whenever a task gets long or open-ended, discuss it honestly before committing.

faqs.question: Does online MYP tutoring really work for a Grade 7 student, or is home tuition better?
faqs.answer: It can, but for many Grade 7 students online works better as a follow-up to home sessions than as the only format. At 12, attention slips faster on a screen, and a tutor cannot see whether the planner is open or a phone is under the desk. Short online sessions reviewing a draft usually go well; long online teaching sessions often do not. If you choose online, keep the laptop in a shared room and sit in for the last few minutes to hear what was agreed.

faqs.question: We live in Sobha City on Dwarka Expressway. Will a tutor come home on weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: Possibly, subject to tutor availability, but on Dwarka Expressway a weekend home session plus weekday online lessons is often easier to arrange. Tutors based elsewhere in Gurgaon may be reluctant to cross the city in weekday evening traffic. Tell IB Gram your society and exact free hours so the shortlist reflects who can realistically reach you. For an MYP 1 or 2 child, waiting longer for a home tutor can be worth it; for MYP 5, a strong online tutor is usually the better call.

faqs.question: The tutor is not working out after three weeks. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Tell IB Gram what is not working and ask for a different match; you do not have to persist with a poor fit. Be specific, because it shapes the next shortlist: 'he rewrites my son's paragraphs' is a different problem from 'she keeps arriving late from Sector 57'. Before switching, check whether a marked task has come back yet. Three weeks is often too soon to judge criterion scores, but long enough to see whether your child understands the tutor and does the work between sessions.

faqs.question: Criterion scores have not changed after a month of tutoring. Should we worry?
faqs.answer: Not yet, unless nothing has changed in how your child works, because criterion scores only move when a new task is marked. An MYP task can take weeks from being set to being returned, so a month of lessons may cover a single task. If working habits have changed, the next scores have something to move on. If they have not, raise it with the tutor, and if that goes nowhere, ask for a different match.

faqs.question: Does a Grade 6 student in MYP 1 need home tuition at all?
faqs.answer: Often not, because in MYP 1 a steady home routine and a conversation with the class teacher are usually enough. A tutor makes sense in Grade 6 when a specific problem lasts beyond the first term: reading well below the class, tasks repeatedly not submitted, or gaps left by a move from another board. Otherwise, sit with your child once a week and check the school platform together. If work hours make that impossible, a tutor who sets the routine over a few weeks and then steps back is a sensible middle path.

If you choose online, keep the laptop in a shared room and sit in for the last few minutes to hear what was agreed.

mainEntity.name: We live in Sobha City on Dwarka Expressway. Will a tutor come home on weekday evenings?

Tutors based elsewhere in Gurgaon may be reluctant to cross the city in weekday evening traffic. Tell IB Gram your society and exact free hours so the shortlist reflects who can realistically reach you. For an MYP 1 or 2 child, waiting longer for a home tutor can be worth it; for MYP 5, a strong online tutor is usually the better call.

mainEntity.name: The tutor is not working out after three weeks. What should we do?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tell IB Gram what is not working and ask for a different match; you do not have to persist with a poor fit. Be specific, because it shapes the next shortlist: 'he rewrites my son's paragraphs' is a different problem from 'she keeps arriving late from Sector 57'. Before switching, check whether a marked task has come back yet. Three weeks is often too soon to judge criterion scores, but long enough to see whether your child understands the tutor and does the work between sessions.

mainEntity.name: Criterion scores have not changed after a month of tutoring. Should we worry?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not yet, unless nothing has changed in how your child works, because criterion scores only move when a new task is marked. An MYP task can take weeks from being set to being returned, so a month of lessons may cover a single task. If working habits have changed, the next scores have something to move on. If they have not, raise it with the tutor, and if that goes nowhere, ask for a different match.

mainEntity.name: Does a Grade 6 student in MYP 1 need home tuition at all?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often not, because in MYP 1 a steady home routine and a conversation with the class teacher are usually enough. A tutor makes sense in Grade 6 when a specific problem lasts beyond the first term: reading well below the class, tasks repeatedly not submitted, or gaps left by a move from another board. Otherwise, sit with your child once a week and check the school platform together. If work hours make that impossible, a tutor who sets the routine over a few weeks and then steps back is a sensible middle path.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram find an MYP Maths tutor in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram builds a shortlist from the details that decide fit in MYP Mathematics: your child's MYP year, standard or extended maths, the weakest criteria on the last report, your sector and your free evenings. It suggests only tutors with verified profiles who match, and a demo session can be arranged before you commit.

Those details matter more in MYP maths than in most tuition. A capable general maths tutor can teach simultaneous equations well and still not see why a student lost marks on criterion C for a muddled line of reasoning. MYP maths is marked against criteria rather than answers alone, so the tutor has to read a task sheet the way your child's maths teacher does. Experience matters in a specific way too. A tutor who regularly works with extended maths students heading for DP AA is a different match from one who is good at rebuilding confidence in an MYP 2 student after a school move.

Tell us about the school calendar as well. If a criterion D task is due in three weeks, the opening sessions should look very different from a plan built around an end-of-unit test next month. And if your child is in MYP 5 at a school that offers the eAssessment, mention it on the first call so that on-screen practice can be planned into the weeks before it. Location changes the answer too: a tutor who can reach DLF Phase 5 on a Tuesday evening may not suit a family in Sector 109, where a midweek online session is often the realistic choice.

Nothing is locked in after the demo. If the tutor's pace, explanation style or timing does not suit your child, ask for a different match. The second search starts with more information, because by then everyone knows what did not work.

contentBlocks.heading: Does standard or extended maths in MYP 4-5 decide the DP course?
contentBlocks.body:
Not on its own, but it shapes the options. Schools often split MYP 4-5 maths into standard and extended mathematics, and extended covers additional topics that prepare for DP Mathematics Analysis and Approaches (AA). Which DP maths course and level a student may then take is set by the school, so ask the DP coordinator before MYP 5 ends.

In the DP, mathematics comes as two courses, Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation (AI), and each can be taken at Standard Level (SL) or Higher Level (HL). Families sometimes treat AI as the soft option and AA HL as the prestige one, but neither label helps a fifteen-year-old choose. Read the school's course descriptions and look honestly at the MYP maths record. Whichever course follows, every DP maths student completes the mathematics exploration, an Internal Assessment (IA) worth 20% of the final grade, and MYP investigation habits carry straight into it.

For a family in MYP 4, the live question is usually whether to push for extended maths. Look at criterion A levels on the harder, unfamiliar questions rather than the overall score. A student placed in standard maths who later wants AA can narrow the gap with an MYP extended maths tutor through MYP 5 and the summer before the first DP year, but that is extra work in the same year as the Personal Project. If the school allows a move from extended to standard, it is no failure when it rebuilds confidence.

In MYP 5, the MYP eAssessment, on-screen examinations plus ePortfolios, is optional, and each school decides whether to offer it. If your child's school does, an MYP 5 Maths tutor should build in practice at reading and answering maths questions on a screen, because a student who has only worked on paper can lose time to the format. If the school does not offer it, ignore anything sold as eAssessment preparation.
items: Extended mathematics covers additional topics that prepare students for DP Mathematics AA.
Ask the maths department for the unit list of each track in MYP 4-5.
DP Mathematics AA and AI can each be taken at SL or HL.

contentBlocks.heading: The four MYP maths criteria and what full marks look like
contentBlocks.body:
Every MYP subject is assessed against four criteria, each scored 0-8, and the total out of 32 converts to a final grade from 1 to 7 through IB grade boundaries. In mathematics the four are A Knowing and understanding, B Investigating patterns, C Communicating, and D Applying mathematics in real-life contexts. A student can be strong on one and weak on another, so good MYP maths criteria help starts by finding out which of the four is costing marks.

Criterion A is the closest to a conventional maths test, but an 8 rarely comes from routine questions alone. In a unit on linear equations, the final questions might show two mobile data plans in a table and ask when they cost the same. What separates an 8 from a 5 is usually whether the student picks a method unprompted, carries it through accurately and gets those unfamiliar questions right.

Criterion C marks how the mathematics is written, not whether the answer is right. A page of correct numbers with no defined variables, no units and an untitled graph will not score well here. A full-marks answer needs correct notation throughout, confident movement between a table, a graph and an equation, and working a classmate could follow without asking a question.

Criterion D asks for mathematics applied to a real situation, followed by a judgement about the result. Suppose the task is to model a Sector 67 family's electricity use across the summer months. A full-marks answer picks out the relevant information, applies a sensible model correctly, then discusses how accurate the result is and whether it makes sense for that household. Students used to answer-only marking often stop at the number, yet the discussion after it is where D is won or lost. Criterion B gets its own section below, because investigations are the task type that surprises families most.
items: A Knowing and understanding: accurate methods on unfamiliar problems, not only practised ones.
B Investigating patterns: a general rule, a justification and verification on new cases.
C Communicating: correct notation, labelled graphs and working another student can follow.
D Applying mathematics in real-life contexts: model, solve, then judge accuracy and sense.

contentBlocks.heading: Gurgaon school calendars and the jump from CBSE or ICSE maths
contentBlocks.body:
Gurgaon children attend many schools, among them Pathways World School, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, The Shri Ram School, Aravali and Heritage Xperiential Learning School. Each sets its own calendar, and which programmes and maths tracks a school offers is for that school to confirm. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here or with the International Baccalaureate.

Criterion-based summative tasks tend to arrive at the end of units, sometimes several in one fortnight, and reports often show a level for each criterion rather than one mark. The Community Project takes time in MYP 3 or 4, and in MYP 5 the Personal Project competes with maths for evenings and weekends. A student coping well in the first weeks can be overwhelmed when a criterion D task and a Personal Project deadline land together, so share the unit calendar with the tutor each term.

The other local pattern is the move from CBSE or ICSE into an IB school, which can happen at any point in the MYP years. These students are usually quick and accurate with procedures. What they have rarely been asked to do is explain why a method works, find and test a general rule, write a conclusion in words, or judge whether an answer is reasonable. Topics may also arrive in a different order, so a child can be ahead in algebra and behind in statistics at the same moment.

So the first job of a Grade 9 IB Maths tutor in Gurgaon working with a CBSE or ICSE arrival is not more worksheets. It is teaching the student to write reasoning down and to start an open task without being handed a method. That shift takes patience, and it moves faster when the tutor works from the school's own rubrics.

CBSE or ICSE arrivals usually need practice explaining reasoning, not more procedural drills.
Topic order differs between boards, so check for gaps unit by unit, not by grade.

contentBlocks.heading: Should MYP Maths lessons in Gurgaon be at home, online or hybrid?
contentBlocks.body:
For most students in MYP 4-5, online maths lessons work well and save travel time, while younger students in MYP 1-2 tend to concentrate better with a tutor beside them at home. Hybrid, meaning a home session for investigations and an online session for doubts, suits many families in between.

The trade-off is plain. Home tutoring gives the tutor a direct view of the notebook, which matters for criterion C habits and for a younger child who drifts off, but it depends on traffic, gate entry and a tutor who lives within reach. Online tutoring removes travel and makes a short midweek session as easy from Sector 104 as from Sector 70, but it needs a student who can write working on a tablet, or hold a notebook up to the camera, without losing the thread. Hybrid takes more planning, since the family has to keep the timetable straight and the tutor has to track work across both formats.

Age shifts the balance. At 11 or 12, in MYP 1 or 2, attention on a screen fades sooner, and much of a tutor's value lies in watching how the child sets out a problem on paper. By MYP 5, most students handle an MYP Maths online tutor comfortably, and if the school offers the on-screen eAssessment, regular work on a screen is useful practice in its own right.

Online is the wrong call for a student who switches the camera off or needs constant prompting to write anything down. Home is the wrong call when the tutor keeps arriving late after a slow crawl through evening traffic, and a one-hour session quietly becomes forty minutes. If you are unsure, run the demo online and one early session at home, then compare the two notebooks side by side. Families can also change the pattern later, moving online in MYP 5 once the timetable is fuller.
items: Home tuition: best for MYP 1-2 students and for building written working habits on paper.
Online: practical in MYP 4-5, with no travel and easy short midweek sessions.
Hybrid: a weekend home session for investigations and a weekday online session before tasks.
Compare a home session and an online session before settling on one pattern.

contentBlocks.heading: How Gurgaon parents can check an IB Maths tutor for MYP
contentBlocks.body:
Before you hire an IB MYP Maths tutor in Gurgaon, know what has already been checked. IB Gram shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and who match your child's board, level, school calendar, location and schedule. That is the starting point. Test a few things yourself as well, because a strong maths background does not mean a tutor understands criterion-based marking.

Start with one question. Ask the tutor to explain, in a couple of minutes, what a full-marks response on criterion B needs. A tutor who knows MYP maths will talk about stating a general rule, showing why it holds and testing it on a case the student has not used yet. A tutor who does not will talk about spotting the pattern correctly and stop there. Then ask whether they have taught both standard and extended maths, and how the plan would differ for a student heading towards DP AA and one heading towards AI.

Hand over a marked task with the teacher's comments and watch what the tutor notices first. The useful ones go straight to the weakest criterion and ask to see the working. Ask about boundaries as well. Schools expect submitted tasks and investigations to be the student's own work, so a tutor who offers to write, correct or finish anything that will be handed in is putting your child at risk. Good tutors practise the same skills on a parallel task with different numbers or a different pattern and leave the school submission alone.

During the demo, notice who does most of the writing and talking: your child should be working, and the tutor should keep asking why an answer makes sense. Afterwards, ask your child to explain one idea without prompting. If the tutor talked for the whole hour while your child nodded along, ask for a different match.
items: Ask the tutor to explain what full marks on criterion B actually requires.
Give the tutor a marked task and note which criterion they look at first.
Agree that submitted school tasks stay untouched and practice uses parallel tasks.
After the demo, ask your child to explain one idea without any prompting.

contentBlocks.heading: Investigating patterns in MYP maths: rule, justification, verification
contentBlocks.body:
A criterion B investigation in MYP Mathematics is a task in which the student explores a pattern, describes it as a general rule, explains why the rule works and then checks it on new cases. The reasoning is what gets marked. A student who reaches the right formula by trial and error, but cannot justify or verify it, should not expect the higher levels.

In a familiar starter task, squares are built in a row from matchsticks: one square needs 4 sticks, two squares need 7 and three need 10. A student records these in a table and notices that the count rises by 3 each time. That is only pattern spotting. The rule comes next: for n squares, the number of sticks is 3n + 1. Justification is the step most often skipped. The first square needs 4 sticks, and every square added after it shares one side with the square before, so it needs only 3 new sticks. That gives 4 + 3(n - 1), which simplifies to 3n + 1. Verification means testing the rule on a case that was not used to find it: for 10 squares the rule predicts 31 sticks, and a quick drawing confirms it.

In MYP 4-5 the patterns usually get harder, such as sequences that do not grow by a constant amount, but the shape of a strong response does not change. Marks slip away when the rule is tested only on the values used to build it, when the justification simply repeats the pattern in words, or when the student never says whether the rule holds for every case. A good IB Middle Years maths tutor makes this habit automatic on practice tasks, and never supplies the rule for a task the school will mark.

The write-up still matters, because a correct rule that is poorly communicated loses marks on criterion C whenever C is assessed on the same task. The habit also outlasts MYP, since the DP mathematics exploration is marked on five criteria, including Reflection and Use of mathematics.
items: State the general rule in algebra, for example sticks = 3n + 1.
Justify the rule from the structure of the pattern, not by repeating the numbers.
Verify the rule on a new case that was not used to find it.
Say whether the rule holds for every case, and explain any limits you find.

contentBlocks.heading: What progress in MYP Maths looks like over one term
contentBlocks.body:
With any IB MYP Maths tutor in Gurgaon, progress shows up in criterion levels on real school tasks, not in the number of worksheets finished. Over one term, a realistic aim is movement on the one or two criteria the tutor has targeted, with the others holding steady. Criterion C often moves first, because it depends on habits. Criterion B tends to take longer, since investigating is a way of thinking rather than a technique.

Expect very little change on paper in the first month. The first summative task after tuition begins may have been half-prepared before the tutor arrived, and one task is a small sample. The honest checkpoint is the second or third marked task. By then the write-ups should be clearer, the student should be attempting the unfamiliar questions, and the justification step should be on the page. If none of that is visible by mid-term, the plan or the match needs to change.

No tutor can guarantee a grade, and the final 1-7 grade depends on criterion totals converted through IB grade boundaries. A tutor also cannot rescue a timetable that leaves no room to practise between sessions: two sessions a week with no independent work often achieve less than one session plus two short practice slots at home. And some students do not need a tutor at all. A child in MYP 1 or 2 with 6s and 7s across the criteria, who simply dislikes one unit, may be better served by a conversation with the class teacher.

The numbered plan in this section is how a well-run term of MYP standard maths help or extended support usually looks. Share it with any IB MYP Maths tutor in Gurgaon you are considering, and ask for a brief written note of the first fortnight's findings so that everyone agrees on what is being fixed.
items: 1. Weeks 1-2: diagnose from the last report, two marked tasks and a short unseen problem.
2. Map the term's units and summative task dates from the school calendar.
3. Each week: close content gaps for criterion A and rewrite working for criterion C.
4. Every fortnight: one practice investigation with rule, justification and verification for criterion B.
5. Before each real-life task: rehearse a parallel criterion D problem and discuss accuracy.
6. End of term: compare criterion levels with the family and reset targets.

contentBlocks.heading: What should your child bring to the first MYP Maths session?
contentBlocks.body:
Bring the latest maths report with criterion levels, two or three marked tasks with teacher comments, the current unit outline and the school's assessment calendar for the term. If your child is in MYP 4 or 5, note whether the class is standard or extended maths, and whether the school offers the eAssessment.

The first session is mostly diagnosis. Expect the tutor to go through the marked tasks with your child, ask them to talk through one solution aloud, and set a short unseen problem, often a small investigation, to see how they handle a task when no method is given. For a student who has come from a CBSE or ICSE school, the tutor may also run through a few topics quickly to find where a different teaching order has left gaps. Very little new content gets taught that day, and that is deliberate. It also helps to ask your child beforehand which criterion feels hardest, since their answer is a useful starting point.

Sort out the practical side beforehand. For home tuition in a gated society, register the tutor at the gate the day before. For online lessons, keep the notebook, a pencil and the school's task sheets on the desk, along with a device on which the tutor can see the working. Keep a parent free for the last ten minutes, when the tutor should explain what they found and suggest how often to meet.

Timing helps too. IB MYP Maths tuition in Gurugram is easiest to start at the beginning of a unit, or in the holidays before MYP 4 or MYP 5, because the tutor then has time to diagnose before a marked task arrives. Starting three days before a criterion D deadline leaves room for little more than reassurance, so if you already know a hard term is coming, begin the search early.
items: The latest maths report showing a level for each criterion from A to D.
Two or three marked tasks with teacher comments, including one investigation if possible.
The current unit outline and the term's assessment calendar from the school.
A note of the standard or extended track and any eAssessment plans.

faqs.question: My child scores 90% in maths tests but only 4 out of 8 on criterion B. Why?
faqs.answer: Because criterion B rewards a justified and verified general rule, not accurate calculation. A student who does well in tests has usually mastered the skills criterion A looks for, but an investigation asks for something different: a rule stated in algebra, an explanation of why it holds and a check on a new case. The fix is regular practice on parallel investigations, with the tutor asking for the justification every time. Students usually improve once they see the missing steps.

faqs.question: Should my daughter move from standard to extended maths in MYP 5?
faqs.answer: Only if her criterion A levels on unfamiliar problems are strong and the school agrees she can manage the pace. Extended mathematics covers additional topics that prepare for DP Mathematics AA, so the move makes most sense for a student seriously considering AA. Ask the maths teacher for an honest view, and confirm the school's policy on switching tracks. If she moves, a tutor can help her cover the extended topics she missed, with the work planned around the Personal Project in MYP 5.

faqs.question: Is it worth hiring an MYP maths eAssessment tutor?
faqs.answer: Only if your child's school offers the MYP eAssessment, because it is optional and each school decides whether to run it. Where it is offered in MYP 5, it includes on-screen examinations, so an MYP maths eAssessment tutor should spend time on answering maths questions on a screen and setting out clear working in that format. The tutor can also work on pacing and on the criteria that are weakest on recent reports. Confirm the details with the MYP coordinator first.

faqs.question: My son is joining Grade 9 from a CBSE school. How much maths catch-up will he need?
faqs.answer: He will usually need less content catch-up than you fear, and more work on explaining and writing up mathematics. A CBSE student is often fluent with procedures, but MYP maths also assesses investigations under criterion B, communication under criterion C and real-life reasoning under criterion D. The hardest adjustment is usually his first investigation, not the tests. Starting before he joins, or in his first month, gives him time to adapt before marked work arrives.

faqs.question: Will the tutor help write my child's maths investigation?
faqs.answer: No, and be wary of any tutor who offers to. Schools expect submitted tasks to be the student's own work. A good tutor teaches the investigation method on a parallel task with a different pattern, then lets your child tackle the real one alone. The tutor can explain what criterion B asks for and give feedback on a practice write-up. The DP works the same way: the teacher can comment on one draft of the mathematics exploration and the work must be the student's own.

faqs.question: We live in Sector 108 on Dwarka Expressway. Can a home tutor come on weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: Possibly, but it depends on whether a matched home tutor already works nearby, and weekday online sessions are often the more reliable choice there. In societies such as Sobha City, Godrej Summit and ATS Kocoon, gate entry takes time, and a tutor travelling from central Gurgaon meets evening traffic in both directions. Many families along the expressway combine a weekend home tuition session with a weekday online one. Share your society and free evenings when you enquire.

faqs.question: Is home tuition better than online for MYP Maths at 11 or 12?
faqs.answer: Usually yes: home tuition tends to suit this age better, unless the child is already comfortable learning on a screen. At that age attention drifts sooner online, and the tutor needs to see working on paper. Online can still work with shorter sessions and the notebook visible on camera. Where home visits are hard, for instance near Bhondsi on the Southern Peripheral Road, try an online demo and judge it by what your child can explain afterwards rather than by how the session felt.

faqs.question: It has been a month and the criterion levels have not moved. Should we stop?
faqs.answer: Not yet, because one month and one marked task are too small a sample to judge. Criterion levels change only when a new summative task is marked. Look at the notebooks instead, and check whether the working is clearer and the justification step is now on the page. If nothing has visibly changed after the second or third marked task, raise it with the tutor, and if the approach still does not change, ask IB Gram for a different match.

faqs.question: The tutor is not working out for my child. Can we change?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can ask IB Gram for a different match if the fit is wrong. Be specific about what did not work, such as pace, explanation style, punctuality on weekday evenings or inexperience with extended maths. That detail shapes the next shortlist. A demo or trial session with the new tutor can be arranged before regular lessons restart. Share the notes and marked tasks from earlier sessions so the diagnostic work is not lost.

faqs.question: Does a child in MYP 1-3 need a maths tutor, or should we wait?
faqs.answer: Many students in MYP 1-3 do not need a tutor, and waiting is sensible if criterion levels are steady. Tutoring earns its place at this stage when a child who joined from another board is struggling with investigations, or when one criterion keeps pulling the grade down after a poor report. For a family on Golf Course Road or in Sushant Lok 2, a short run of home sessions focused on that one criterion can be enough. Otherwise, steady practice at home and a word with the class teacher are often enough.

mainEntity.name: My child scores 90% in maths tests but only 4 out of 8 on criterion B. Why?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because criterion B rewards a justified and verified general rule, not accurate calculation. A student who does well in tests has usually mastered the skills criterion A looks for, but an investigation asks for something different: a rule stated in algebra, an explanation of why it holds and a check on a new case. The fix is regular practice on parallel investigations, with the tutor asking for the justification every time. Students usually improve once they see the missing steps.

mainEntity.name: Should my daughter move from standard to extended maths in MYP 5?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if her criterion A levels on unfamiliar problems are strong and the school agrees she can manage the pace. Extended mathematics covers additional topics that prepare for DP Mathematics AA, so the move makes most sense for a student seriously considering AA. Ask the maths teacher for an honest view, and confirm the school's policy on switching tracks. If she moves, a tutor can help her cover the extended topics she missed, with the work planned around the Personal Project in MYP 5.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth hiring an MYP maths eAssessment tutor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if your child's school offers the MYP eAssessment, because it is optional and each school decides whether to run it. Where it is offered in MYP 5, it includes on-screen examinations, so an MYP maths eAssessment tutor should spend time on answering maths questions on a screen and setting out clear working in that format. The tutor can also work on pacing and on the criteria that are weakest on recent reports. Confirm the details with the MYP coordinator first.

mainEntity.name: My son is joining Grade 9 from a CBSE school. How much maths catch-up will he need?

acceptedAnswer.text: He will usually need less content catch-up than you fear, and more work on explaining and writing up mathematics. A CBSE student is often fluent with procedures, but MYP maths also assesses investigations under criterion B, communication under criterion C and real-life reasoning under criterion D. The hardest adjustment is usually his first investigation, not the tests. Starting before he joins, or in his first month, gives him time to adapt before marked work arrives.

mainEntity.name: Will the tutor help write my child's maths investigation?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, and be wary of any tutor who offers to. Schools expect submitted tasks to be the student's own work. A good tutor teaches the investigation method on a parallel task with a different pattern, then lets your child tackle the real one alone. The tutor can explain what criterion B asks for and give feedback on a practice write-up. The DP works the same way: the teacher can comment on one draft of the mathematics exploration and the work must be the student's own.

mainEntity.name: We live in Sector 108 on Dwarka Expressway. Can a home tutor come on weekday evenings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Possibly, but it depends on whether a matched home tutor already works nearby, and weekday online sessions are often the more reliable choice there. In societies such as Sobha City, Godrej Summit and ATS Kocoon, gate entry takes time, and a tutor travelling from central Gurgaon meets evening traffic in both directions. Many families along the expressway combine a weekend home tuition session with a weekday online one. Share your society and free evenings when you enquire.

mainEntity.name: Is home tuition better than online for MYP Maths at 11 or 12?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually yes: home tuition tends to suit this age better, unless the child is already comfortable learning on a screen. At that age attention drifts sooner online, and the tutor needs to see working on paper. Online can still work with shorter sessions and the notebook visible on camera. Where home visits are hard, for instance near Bhondsi on the Southern Peripheral Road, try an online demo and judge it by what your child can explain afterwards rather than by how the session felt.

mainEntity.name: It has been a month and the criterion levels have not moved. Should we stop?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not yet, because one month and one marked task are too small a sample to judge. Criterion levels change only when a new summative task is marked. Look at the notebooks instead, and check whether the working is clearer and the justification step is now on the page. If nothing has visibly changed after the second or third marked task, raise it with the tutor, and if the approach still does not change, ask IB Gram for a different match.

mainEntity.name: The tutor is not working out for my child. Can we change?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can ask IB Gram for a different match if the fit is wrong. Be specific about what did not work, such as pace, explanation style, punctuality on weekday evenings or inexperience with extended maths. That detail shapes the next shortlist. A demo or trial session with the new tutor can be arranged before regular lessons restart. Share the notes and marked tasks from earlier sessions so the diagnostic work is not lost.

mainEntity.name: Does a child in MYP 1-3 need a maths tutor, or should we wait?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many students in MYP 1-3 do not need a tutor, and waiting is sensible if criterion levels are steady. Tutoring earns its place at this stage when a child who joined from another board is struggling with investigations, or when one criterion keeps pulling the grade down after a poor report. For a family on Golf Course Road or in Sushant Lok 2, a short run of home sessions focused on that one criterion can be enough. Otherwise, steady practice at home and a word with the class teacher are often enough.

introSummary: An IB PYP tutor in Gurgaon works with children aged 3 to 12 in the International Baccalaureate (IB) Primary Years Programme (PYP), and helps most when a child has a specific gap in reading, number sense or inquiry work, not when the family simply wants an extra class. The PYP has no external examinations, so good home tuition or online support at this stage is not exam coaching. It looks like reading aloud together, maths with real objects, and a child learning to ask sharper questions about the class's current unit of inquiry. The sections below cover when to get help and when to hold off, what a good session looks like, the final-year PYP exhibition, and the move into the Middle Years Programme (MYP) or another board, for families across Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram matches a PYP tutor to your Gurgaon child
contentBlocks.body:
A request for a primary-age child needs different questions from a request for a teenager, because there is no external exam to prepare for. What matters is the child: how old they are, how long they can concentrate after school, what the class is exploring this term, and whether the worry is reading, maths, confidence or the exhibition. So when you send a query or book a free consultation for an IB PYP tutor in Gurgaon, IB Gram asks about the board and grade, the school calendar, where you live and which afternoons or weekend mornings are realistic.

It helps to describe the problem in your own words. 'Riya reads fluently but cannot tell me what the chapter was about' points to a different tutor from 'Kabir still counts on his fingers in Grade 4 and cries before maths homework'. The first is a comprehension and vocabulary brief, suited to someone who works as an IB PYP English tutor. The second needs a patient IB PYP maths tutor who is happy to start with beads, coins and a measuring jug before any written sums. Details like these save everyone a wasted trial session.

From there, IB Gram shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and who match your child's age, the subject worry, your location and your schedule, subject to tutor availability. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit, and you decide after watching how your child responds. If the fit is wrong a few weeks in, you can ask for a different match. It happens with young children, and it is nobody's failure: a six-year-old may simply warm to a different voice.

Nothing is promised beyond that. A good match is a starting point, and the real test is whether your child looks forward to the second session.

2. IB Gram asks about board, grade, current unit, school calendar, location in Gurgaon and schedule.
