acceptedAnswer.text: It is not necessarily too late, but a September start leaves fewer weeks, so the plan has to be narrower. First confirm with the DP coordinator that registration is still possible, since deadlines run through the school. Then cut anything not tied to the papers being resat: diagnose in the first week, rebuild only the topics that cost the most marks and move to timed sections quickly. A single-subject resit absorbs a late start far better than three subjects do.

mainEntity.name: Can we ask for a re-mark and prepare for a retake at the same time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and it is usually sensible, because the enquiry upon results has a short deadline after results come out, while retake preparation takes months. Raise both with the DP coordinator in one conversation: whether a re-mark suits a particular subject, what it can and cannot change, and what the retake deadlines and costs are. Early diagnosis sessions with a tutor help either way, and if the re-mark changes the picture, the plan can be adjusted.

mainEntity.name: My child missed the IB Diploma by one or two points. What should we do first?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask the DP coordinator exactly why the diploma was not awarded, before booking any lessons. It needs at least 24 points, subject to the IB's failing conditions, so a student can fall short on points or on a condition, and each calls for a different fix. Families looking for IB failed diploma help often panic in July. The calmer route is to confirm the reason, ask about a re-mark if a grade looks wrong, and then choose the subjects with the most recoverable grades.

mainEntity.name: Will a university hold a conditional offer while my child resits in November?

acceptedAnswer.text: That depends entirely on the university, so ask its admissions office in writing as soon as results arrive. Attach the results, name the subjects being resat in November, and ask two questions: can the place be held or deferred, and would November results be considered at all? Answers vary between countries, universities and even courses. Share every reply with the coordinator and the tutor; the answers should decide how many subjects are worth resitting.

mainEntity.name: Can a home tutor come to our society in Sector 108 on weekday mornings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often yes, subject to tutor availability, because a retake student is free in school hours and daytime slots are easier to arrange than weekday evenings. Societies along Dwarka Expressway, such as Godrej Summit, Sobha City and ATS Kocoon, usually require visitor registration, so add the home tutor to the approved list before the first lesson. Mention your tower and preferred days in the query, since they shape which tutors can reach Sector 108 on a fixed weekly pattern.

mainEntity.name: What happens if a home session is missed because of traffic near Hero Honda Chowk?

acceptedAnswer.text: Agree a rescheduling rule before lessons start, so a missed home session is moved rather than lost. Congestion near Hero Honda Chowk and along NH-48 can stretch a short trip at almost any hour, which is why longer, less frequent home sessions often suit families around Manesar. A practical fallback is to take that one lesson online at the same time. If delays become regular, agree a different day with the tutor or ask IB Gram for a better-placed match.

mainEntity.name: Does online retake tutoring work as well as home tuition?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can, for a motivated student reviewing papers, but home tuition usually works better for a student who has lost momentum since July. Online lessons widen the choice of tutors and suit a student already working or studying away from home. The weakness is accountability: without school, a student can drift between online sessions unnoticed. A fair test is three or four weeks online. If set work arrives without reminders and repeated errors start to fall, it is working.

mainEntity.name: What should we do if the retake tutor is not working out after a few weeks?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask IB Gram for a different match, but first check the problem against evidence rather than mood. Look at the marked timed sections: if scores and recurring errors have not moved after several weeks of regular lessons, the approach is not working. Pleasant but vague lessons, with no written plan and no timed practice, are also a reason to change. Share the diagnosis and marked work with the new tutor so nothing is repeated, because November will not wait.

mainEntity.name: Our child has lost all motivation since the July results. Should they still retake?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not automatically, because a retake only helps if the student wants the better grade for a reason of their own. Talk it through together: what the grade would change, which university route it opens and what the months until November would involve. If they would really be sitting the papers for someone else, look at other plans for the year. Where low mood lasts for weeks, speak to a counsellor or doctor first. Motivation often returns with a fixed routine and one small first target.

It is a normal request, and a good IGCSE tutor in Gurgaon expects families to make it when something is not working.

contentBlocks.heading: Cambridge IGCSE or Edexcel: what actually differs for your child?
contentBlocks.body:
Both are usually two-year courses taken across Grades 9 and 10, and students commonly go on from either to the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP), to A Levels, or to the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) or the Indian School Certificate (ISC) in Class 11. What differs in practice is the grading scale, the exam series on offer and the way tiers work. Those three things change how a tutor plans.

Cambridge IGCSE is set by Cambridge International Education. Most of its syllabuses are graded from A* to G, although some subjects also have a 9-1 version under a different syllabus code. Many Cambridge subjects are split into Core and Extended tiers, and the ceiling is fixed: a Core candidate cannot be awarded higher than grade C, while an Extended candidate can reach A*. Cambridge runs three series each year. February/March is offered only in India. The others are May/June and October/November.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is graded 9-1 and runs two series, January and May/June. Its Mathematics A is tiered as Foundation or Higher. Its sciences are not tiered at all, so every candidate sits the same papers, with practical skills assessed inside the written papers rather than in a separate practical paper. A Cambridge IGCSE tutor in Gurgaon who has only ever prepared students for Cambridge will know most of the content but not the Edexcel paper style. An Edexcel IGCSE tutor in Gurugram carries the opposite gap.

So the first thing a tutor should ask is not which subject, but which board, which code and which tier. Plenty of parents do not know the answer offhand, and that is fine. Your child's school does. One short email to the IGCSE coordinator settles it, and it is worth sending before you speak to any tutor, because it narrows the shortlist to people who have taught that exact exam recently.
items: Cambridge IGCSE: most syllabuses graded A* to G; some have 9-1 versions under different codes.
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE: graded 9-1, with exam series in January and May/June.
Cambridge series: February/March (offered only in India), May/June and October/November.
Cambridge Core tier tops out at grade C; the Extended tier can reach A*.
Edexcel sciences are untiered; Edexcel Mathematics A offers Foundation or Higher tiers.

contentBlocks.heading: The Maths and science papers an IGCSE tutor must know by name
contentBlocks.body:
The subjects Gurgaon families ask about most are Mathematics and the three sciences, with English and Economics close behind. Maths is where the syllabus code changes the most. For Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, from the 2025 exams, Core candidates sit Paper 1, which is non-calculator, and Paper 3, which allows a calculator. Extended candidates sit Paper 2 without a calculator and Paper 4 with one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, code 4MA1, is tiered Foundation or Higher, and each tier sits two calculator papers.

That difference should shape every week of lessons. An IGCSE Maths tutor in Gurgaon teaching a 0580 Extended student has to build in regular non-calculator work for Paper 2: written arithmetic and algebra done by hand, against the clock, with every line of working visible. A 4MA1 Higher student never faces a non-calculator paper, so the same lesson time is better spent on long multi-step problems and on checking calculator output for silly slips. Put the two students side by side and the homework looks nothing alike, even when the topic name is the same.

The Cambridge IGCSE sciences examined from 2023 share one structure. Core candidates sit Paper 1, multiple choice, and Paper 3, theory. Extended candidates sit Paper 2, multiple choice, and Paper 4, theory. Practical skills are assessed through Paper 5, a practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, and the school chooses which. The weighting is multiple choice 30%, theory 50% and practical 20%. Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered, with Paper 1 and Paper 2 for the separate sciences and practical skills tested inside those written papers.

For an IGCSE science tutor in Gurgaon, that practical fifth of the marks is the part most easily neglected. A student entered for Paper 6 answers questions about experiments on paper rather than at a bench, and that is a skill of its own. Ask the tutor which practical paper they are preparing your child for. If they cannot say, you have learned something useful before paying for a term.
items: 0580 Core, from the 2025 exams: Paper 1 non-calculator and Paper 3 calculator.
0580 Extended, from the 2025 exams: Paper 2 non-calculator and Paper 4 calculator.
Edexcel 4MA1: Foundation or Higher tier, with two calculator papers in each tier.
Cambridge sciences weighting: multiple choice 30%, theory 50%, practical 20%.
Practical route: Paper 5 practical test or Paper 6 alternative to practical, chosen by the school.

contentBlocks.heading: The two-year IGCSE timeline and exam series facing Gurgaon families
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE is usually a two-year course: Grade 9 builds most of the content, and Grade 10 ends in the exams. For tutoring, the date that matters most is the series your child is entered for, because it fixes how many months of teaching are left. Cambridge IGCSE candidates can sit the February/March series, which is offered only in India, as well as May/June and October/November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE candidates have January and May/June.

A February/March entry pulls the finish line forward by a whole term. A student sitting in March loses the stretch that a May/June candidate spends on timed past papers after the school's own tests, and a tutor who quietly plans for May/June will run out of weeks. If an October/November or January entry is being discussed, perhaps to retake one subject or to spread the load, talk to the school before booking extra lessons. It moves the point at which tutoring should be most intense.

The school names on this page, such as Scottish High International School, Pathways World School, Lancers International School, GD Goenka World School, DPS International Edge and Excelsior American School, appear only as local context. This page makes no claim about which programme or board any of them offers, and IB Gram is not affiliated with any of these schools. What parents at international schools across Gurgaon tend to describe is similar anyway: internal tests that do not always resemble the external paper, subject and tier decisions made before Grade 9 has settled, and a Grade 10 year crowded with projects, sport and choices about Class 11.

So plan backwards from the series date rather than forwards from the textbook. At the start of each term, ask the school for its assessment calendar and share it with the tutor. A school test week then stops colliding with a lesson plan built around a paper your child will not sit for months, and your child is not left juggling two competing sets of priorities in the same fortnight.
items: Grade 9: build the content and learn how papers for the chosen code are set.
Grade 10: finish content early enough to leave room for timed past-paper practice.
The Cambridge February/March series is offered only in India and shortens the Grade 10 runway.

Ask the coordinator for the entry series and the school's internal test dates each term.

contentBlocks.heading: IGCSE home tuition, online or hybrid: which suits your child in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
Start with home tuition whenever a suitable tutor can reach your sector or society reliably on school evenings. Choose online when the right specialist for the syllabus code and tier lives far away, or traffic makes timing unpredictable. Hybrid works when you want supervised papers at home and flexible weekday sessions online.

An IGCSE home tutor in Gurgaon sees the working as it happens. On a non-calculator Maths paper that matters, because the tutor watches a sign error appear instead of spotting it later in a blurry photo. And homework is harder to quietly skip when the same person will be back at the same table in three days. Home lessons suit families on Golf Course Road, in the DLF Phases or around Sushant Lok when a good match is based nearby. The cost is travel. A tutor crossing from Sohna Road to Cyber City on a weekday evening loses time you never see, and one heavy-rain evening can wipe out a lesson.

Online is the first alternative, and an IGCSE online tutor in Gurugram widens the choice. A family in Sector 108 on Dwarka Expressway or Sector 85 in New Gurgaon no longer has to settle for whoever lives closest, and lessons start on time. But the limits are real. A 15-year-old can drift off camera, and preparing for a practical paper is harder through a screen. The detail of how online IGCSE lessons run belongs on its own page; for this decision, the honest question is whether your child stays focused without someone in the room.

Hybrid, the second alternative, is where many Grade 10 families land once the series gets close. A weekend home session covers a full timed paper under supervision, and shorter online sessions during the week handle doubt-solving without the evening drive. It works best when the same IGCSE tutor in Gurgaon runs both, so the plan for the code, the tier and the series stays in one person's head. None of the three is automatically better, and a disciplined student on the SPR may do better online than a distracted one with a tutor at home in DLF Phase 3.
items: Home tuition first: best for supervised timed papers and students who need their working watched.
Online as an alternative: the widest choice of specialists and no travel, but focus is harder to hold.
Hybrid: a weekend home session for full papers, weekday online sessions for doubts.
SPR, New Gurgaon and Dwarka Expressway families often find online widens the shortlist most.
Keep one tutor across both modes so the plan for code, tier and series stays intact.

contentBlocks.heading: What IB Gram checks, and what you should check in the trial
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram shortlists only tutors whose profiles have been verified, and only those whose profiles match your child's board, syllabus, level and schedule. Treat verification as a floor, not a verdict. It tells you the profile in front of you is genuine. It cannot tell you whether this particular tutor will take your daughter from shaky Paper 4 answers to confident ones, and nobody can promise that from a profile.

So the trial is your own check. Before it, write the syllabus code, the tier and the series on a slip of paper, and notice whether the tutor asks for them without prompting. Someone used to Cambridge will want to know Core or Extended straight away. Someone used to Edexcel will ask Foundation or Higher for Maths, and will already know the sciences carry no tier. If the tutor talks about the IGCSE syllabus as though only one existed, press gently.

Then watch the marking. Hand over a question your child got wrong in a school test and ask where exactly the marks went. A strong tutor points to the method line that was skipped, the missing unit, the part of the question left unanswered. A weaker one simply solves it again, neatly, and moves on. Parents comparing IGCSE tutors in Gurgaon often start with degrees and years of experience. Searching for the best IGCSE tutor in Gurgaon, though, really means finding someone who can show your child where marks leak on the paper they will actually sit, and the trial is the only place that shows up.

Check the ordinary things as well. Notice whether the lesson started on time, and whether the tutor told you, not only your child, what comes next. For home tuition, see how the tutor handled the society gate and your household's routine. If any of these slip twice in the first few weeks, raise it early, and ask for a different match if it continues.

See whether the tutor asks for syllabus code, tier and exam series without prompting.
Bring one wrongly answered school question and ask where exactly the marks were lost.

contentBlocks.heading: Why the syllabus code and tier matter before you book anyone
contentBlocks.body:
A syllabus code is the short reference that identifies the exact subject specification your child is examined on, for example 0580 for Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics or 4MA1 for Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A. The tier is the level of paper within that code. Together they decide which papers your child sits, which grades are within reach and which past papers are worth practising. Get either one wrong and good teaching goes into the wrong exam.

Take Riya, in Grade 9 and living in Sector 50, whose school has entered her for Core Mathematics. Core caps her at grade C. If she is capable of more, the conversation that matters is with the school about Extended, not with a tutor about extra hours. Her previous home tutor never asked. He spent a term on Extended-style questions she would never see, while her Paper 1 non-calculator work, the paper she will actually sit, stayed untouched. The reverse happens just as often, with an Extended candidate drilled on Core-level questions and then surprised by Paper 4.

The code trap is quieter. Some Cambridge syllabuses also exist as a 9-1 version under a different code, so two students in the same Gurgaon society, both saying they take the same IGCSE subject, may be sitting different syllabuses graded on different scales. Past papers for the wrong code can look very similar, and a month of practice on them is a month gone. Board confusion works the same way: a student sitting Edexcel sciences has no separate practical paper, so a tutor drilling Paper 6 technique is preparing for an exam that is not coming.

Three practical questions usually follow. Fees depend on the subject, level, mode, lesson frequency and how close the series is, so no honest page can put one figure on them. Online lessons get a fuller treatment on their own page. And coaching batches only make sense when everyone shares the same code, tier and series, which a batch mixing CBSE Class 10 with IGCSE, or Core with Extended, cannot offer.
items: Syllabus code: identifies the exact specification, such as 0580 or 4MA1, your child sits.
Tier: decides which papers are sat and the highest grade that can be awarded.
Cambridge Core caps at grade C, so a tier question is a school conversation first.
Some Cambridge subjects have 9-1 versions under different codes; check before downloading past papers.
Fees vary with subject, level, mode, frequency and how close the exam series is.

contentBlocks.heading: How can you tell whether IGCSE tutoring is working after a month?
contentBlocks.body:
After four weeks, look for three things. Your child can explain what went wrong on a recent question without being prompted. The same type of mistake turns up less often in homework and school tests. And the tutor can tell you, in a couple of sentences, what has been covered and what comes next. Marks themselves may not have moved yet, and that is normal.

Grades lag behind skills. A Grade 9 student who has been dropping method marks on Extended Paper 4 may need a full cycle of school tests before the change reaches a report card. So judge the first month by the working, not the percentage. Ask to see an attempt from the first week and one from the fourth on the same topic. If the second is not visibly better set out, with steps shown and units kept, something in the plan needs to change.

No tutor can guarantee a grade, and a good one will not try. Starting in the last few months before a February/March series narrows what is possible: there is time to fix exam technique and a handful of weak topics, not to rebuild two years of content. Some students do not need a tutor at all. A student who is steady on past papers for the right code and tier, and who asks teachers for help when stuck, may need only a few sessions before the series, or none.

If a month has gone by with no change in the working, talk to the tutor before anything else, because the plan may be at fault rather than the person. If the second month looks exactly like the first, ask IB Gram for a different match. Waiting a full term out of politeness is the most expensive option available to you.
items: By week four, your child explains their own errors without the tutor pointing to them.
Recurring slips, such as dropped units or skipped steps, appear less often in school work.
The tutor gives you a clear update on topics covered and what is planned next.
Marks can lag skills by a school test cycle, so judge the working before grades.
No tutor can guarantee a grade; be wary of anyone who promises one.

contentBlocks.heading: What to prepare before the first IGCSE lesson in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Before you send a query, gather a few facts. You need the board and syllabus code for each subject, the tier, the exam series, your child's two most recent school test papers with the teacher's comments, and a realistic weekly timetable that includes school timings, sport and travel. Add your sector and society name, and say whether home tuition is possible for your family or whether online or hybrid lessons would suit better.

Then send a query or book a free consultation. IB Gram will ask about the board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, and shortlist tutors with verified profiles who fit. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit, subject to tutor availability. Starting IGCSE tuition in Gurugram this way takes a little longer than calling the first name you are given, and it saves the weeks lost to a mismatch.

The first session should not be a lecture. A useful one opens with a short diagnostic on one past-paper question for the right code and tier, looks at a recent school test together, and ends with the tutor telling both you and your child which topics come first and why. For a Grade 10 IGCSE tutor, that first hour also fixes the plan against the series date. In Grade 9, it is more about finding gaps before they widen into a Grade 10 problem.

If your child is nervous about being tested in the very first lesson, tell the tutor beforehand. Diagnostic work can be done gently, one question at a time, and it is still far kinder than a month of guessing where the problem lies. Keep the test papers you brought, too. Comparing them with work from the fourth week gives you the clearest evidence of whether the lessons are doing their job.
items: Board and syllabus code for every subject you want help with.
Tier for each subject: Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher.
Entry series: February/March, May/June or October/November for Cambridge; January or May/June for Edexcel.
Two recent school tests with marks and teacher comments, not only the report card.
Weekly timetable, sector and society name, and whether home visits are possible.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE tutor in Gurgaon cost?
faqs.answer: There is no single fee, because the cost depends on the subject, the tier, the lesson mode, how often lessons run and how close the exam series is. A Grade 10 Extended Maths student preparing for the February/March series with two home lessons a week on Golf Course Road is a very different request from a Grade 9 student taking one online Economics session. Travel can be a factor for home lessons, and online sessions remove it. Ask for the fee to be explained per session and per month before the trial, and check what happens when your child cancels a lesson at short notice.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach both Cambridge IGCSE and Edexcel International GCSE?
faqs.answer: Some tutors teach both, but ask which board they have prepared students for most recently before assuming it. The subject names look alike; the papers do not. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 has a non-calculator paper in each tier from the 2025 exams, while Edexcel 4MA1 has two calculator papers per tier. Cambridge sciences separate multiple choice, theory and a practical paper, whereas Edexcel sciences are untiered and test practical skills inside Paper 1 and Paper 2. A tutor who moves comfortably between boards will raise these differences unprompted. One who treats the two as interchangeable will sooner or later set the wrong past papers.

faqs.question: Where do we find our child's syllabus code, tier and exam series?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's IGCSE or examinations coordinator, who can confirm all three for each subject your child is entered for. A subject teacher may know the tier, but the coordinator is usually the person who handles entries. Do not work it out from a textbook or revision guide, because a book on the shelf is no proof of which code your child will sit, and some Cambridge subjects exist as both an A*-G syllabus and a 9-1 version under a different code. Write the answers down subject by subject and include the list when you send your query to IB Gram. It saves a wasted first lesson.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start tutoring a few months before the February/March series?
faqs.answer: It is not too late, but the goal has to shrink to what those few months can fix. Cambridge offers the February/March series only in India, and because it comes before May/June, a Grade 10 student who starts in the autumn term has a short runway. Spend it on exam technique for the right code and tier, timed past papers and the handful of topics that cost the most marks. Rebuilding two years of content is not realistic in that window. If your child genuinely needs more time, ask the school whether a later series is possible before you book extra lessons.

faqs.question: Does online IGCSE tutoring really work for a 15-year-old?
faqs.answer: It works well for many students and poorly for some, and the difference is usually attention rather than technology. A student who stays on task and sends working promptly can do very well online, and families in Sector 67 on the SPR or Sector 84 in New Gurgaon often gain a much wider choice of tutors. A student who drifts, or who needs someone watching each line of a non-calculator paper, may do better with a home tutor or in a hybrid pattern. Preparing for a practical paper is also harder through a screen. Judge two or three online sessions by the working produced, not by how pleasant the calls felt.

faqs.question: Should we choose a coaching centre instead of a private IGCSE tutor?
faqs.answer: A coaching batch can work, but only when every student in it shares the same syllabus code, tier and exam series. A batch that mixes IGCSE with CBSE Class 10, or seats Core and Extended candidates together, cannot give each student practice on the papers they will actually sit. One-to-one lessons plan around a single child's papers, gaps and school calendar, which matters most in Grade 10. Some families combine the two: a well-matched small group for a subject that is going steadily, and a private tutor for the subject causing trouble. Ask any centre which codes and tiers each batch is built around.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is not working out?
faqs.answer: Ask IB Gram for a different match; it is a normal request, and you do not need to wait until the end of a term. Before you do, have one direct conversation with the tutor about what is going wrong, whether that is lesson structure, punctuality, pace or how feedback reaches you. Sometimes that conversation fixes it. If it does not, give IB Gram specifics. Saying the tutor was not right gives nothing to match on, while saying your child needed more non-calculator Paper 2 practice and mostly got explanations does. The next shortlist can then reflect what went wrong, subject to tutor availability.

faqs.question: Marks have not improved after a month. What should we check?
faqs.answer: Check whether the lessons are aimed at the right exam before blaming the tutor or your child. Confirm that the practice matches your child's syllabus code, tier and practical paper, because good teaching aimed at the wrong papers will not move school marks. Then look at the ordinary causes: missed sessions, homework not attempted between lessons, and school tests covering topics the tutor has not reached yet. Put a first-week attempt beside a recent one on the same topic. If the working is clearer, give it another test cycle. If nothing has changed, ask the tutor for a revised plan, and ask IB Gram for a different match if the second month looks the same.

faqs.question: Will a home tutor come to Sector 108 on Dwarka Expressway on weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: It depends on tutor availability, and in newer sectors the right specialist for your child's code and tier may not live nearby. When you send a query, give your exact sector and society, such as Sobha City or ATS Kocoon, along with the evening slots your child can really use after school and homework. If a suitable tutor can reach you reliably, home tuition is possible. If not, many families settle on a hybrid pattern: online sessions on weekdays and a home session at the weekend, when timing is less tight. That keeps the specialist and cuts the weekday travel.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during IGCSE home tuition?
faqs.answer: Yes, a parent or another trusted adult should be at home for every session, although nobody needs to sit in the room. With a 14- or 15-year-old, that keeps things comfortable for everyone, and it gives you two minutes with the tutor at the end to hear what was covered. Set the lesson at a dining table or a desk in a shared space rather than a bedroom, with good light and room for past papers to lie flat. Keep your child's exam calculator, a clock for timed questions and a folder of marked work on the table, so you and the tutor can both track progress.

faqs.question: Is my child graded A* to G or 9 to 1?
faqs.answer: It depends on the board and the syllabus code, so check the code rather than the subject name. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is graded 9-1. Cambridge IGCSE grades most syllabuses A* to G, but some Cambridge subjects also have a 9-1 version under a different syllabus code, so two students taking what sounds like the same subject may be working to different scales. Tiered Cambridge subjects add a ceiling as well: a Core candidate can be awarded no higher than grade C, while an Extended candidate can reach A*. A tutor should confirm the scale in the first lesson and set targets on it.

faqs.question: Our child plans to take the IB Diploma or A Levels in Class 11. Should the IGCSE tutor prepare for that now?
faqs.answer: Only lightly, because the IGCSE papers at the end of Grade 10 are the exams your child is actually sitting. Families in Gurgaon often choose between the IB Diploma Programme, A Levels, or a move to CBSE or ISC in Class 11, and a good tutor can build useful habits inside ordinary IGCSE work, such as setting out algebra cleanly and writing precise science answers. Teaching next-stage content early usually steals time from past-paper practice for the chosen series. Once the last paper is over, a short bridging plan for the new course makes far more sense.

introSummary: If you searched for an IGCSE tutor near me in Gurgaon, the useful answer depends on your sector, the subjects involved and the evenings your child is actually free. IB Gram asks for those details, then shortlists verified tutors who can reach your area for home lessons, subject to tutor availability. Where no suitable tutor is within easy reach, online or hybrid lessons are usually a better call than a tutor who arrives late and tired. Below you will find every Gurugram corridor from Golf Course Road to Manesar, what home tutoring is realistic in each, whether one nearby tutor can cover Maths and the sciences or you need separate specialists, how to plan around siblings on different programmes, and what to do if you move house halfway through Grade 10.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Finds an IGCSE Tutor Near You in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
A request for an IGCSE tutor near me in Gurgaon starts with an address, not a subject list. When you send a query or book a free consultation, IB Gram asks for your sector or society, the board and syllabus your child sits, the tier in each subject, the school calendar, and the evenings that are genuinely free once the school bus, sport and dinner are accounted for. The society name helps as much as the sector, since gate entry rules and visitor parking vary from one complex to the next.

So a family in Sector 57 on Golf Course Extension Road and a family in Sector 104 on Dwarka Expressway can ask for exactly the same thing, IGCSE Mathematics and Physics twice a week, and receive quite different shortlists. Profiles are checked the same way for both. What changes is who can reach the gate at the agreed hour without cutting another lesson short, and whether that person also teaches the right tier.

The shortlist is drawn from tutors whose profiles are verified and whose subjects, levels and travel areas match what you described, subject to tutor availability. If the nearest suitable tutor for one subject lives on the far side of the city, the shortlist will reflect that, with online lessons suggested for that subject while a closer tutor handles the rest. A demo or trial session can be arranged before you commit. Hold it at home, at the real time slot, so you see how the journey works on an ordinary weekday rather than a quiet Sunday.

If the fit turns out wrong, you can ask for a different match. That applies to distance as much as to teaching. A tutor who keeps arriving late because the drive from Sohna Road ran into office traffic is not a good match for your evenings, however strong the lesson is once it starts.
items: 1. Share your sector or society, board, tiers, subjects and the weekday evenings that are free.
2. IB Gram checks which verified tutors teach those subjects and travel to your area.
3. Subjects with no suitable nearby tutor are flagged, with online or hybrid lessons suggested.
4. A demo or trial session can be arranged at home, at the real slot, before you commit.
5. If distance or teaching style stops working, ask IB Gram for a different match.

contentBlocks.heading: Board, Tier and Series: What a Nearby Tutor Must Know
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE in Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana means one of two qualifications: Cambridge IGCSE, from Cambridge International Education, or the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. Either is usually taught as a two-year course across Grades 9 and 10. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, the International Baccalaureate (IB), Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

The board matters for a near-me search because it narrows the local pool. Cambridge exam series run in February/March, May/June and October/November, and the February/March series is offered only in India. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and May/June. An IGCSE tutor in DLF Phase 4 who has spent recent years preparing students for the Cambridge May/June series is well placed for a Cambridge candidate. A tutor whose recent students all sat the January Edexcel series may still be excellent, but will need to rebuild the revision calendar around your dates. Grading differs as well. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A*-G, and some syllabuses have 9-1 versions under different codes, while Edexcel International GCSE grades 9-1.

Tiers deserve the same care. Many Cambridge subjects have Core and Extended tiers, and Core tops out at grade C while Extended reaches A*. A nearby tutor who is very good at taking a Core student to a secure C is not automatically the right person to push an Extended student towards the top grades, and the reverse holds too. Give IB Gram the tier for each subject, even if the school has not confirmed it, and say which way it might move.

Then look one step ahead. IGCSE is often followed by the IB Diploma Programme (DP), A Levels, or a move to CBSE or ISC in Class 11. None of that should decide who teaches Grades 9 and 10 at your dining table.
items: Cambridge IGCSE series: February/March (offered only in India), May/June and October/November.
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series: January and May/June.
Cambridge grades most syllabuses A*-G; Edexcel International GCSE grades 9-1.
Core tier tops out at grade C, while the Extended tier reaches A*.
Tell the tutor the syllabus code; your school's coordinator can confirm it.

contentBlocks.heading: Should One Nearby Tutor Teach Maths and the Sciences?
contentBlocks.body:
Often yes, especially for Core students and for Extended students who are steady rather than struggling, provided the tutor teaches your exact board and tier in every subject they take on. One nearby tutor for IGCSE Mathematics and the sciences saves travel, keeps one adult watching the whole workload and makes weekday scheduling far simpler. The arrangement breaks down when one subject needs a specialist.

The case for grouping is practical. Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry share habits: rearranging formulae, handling units, reading graphs and setting out working so an examiner can follow it. A nearby IGCSE Maths tutor who is also strong in Physics will notice that a Physics mark was lost to algebra, not to the physics, and fix it at the source. Biology leans harder on precise wording and data interpretation, so check it separately instead of assuming it comes bundled. And one familiar tutor at home twice a week is easier for a 14-year-old to sustain than three different people on three evenings.

The case for separate specialists is just as real. English and Economics rarely sit well with a science tutor, because they rely on structured writing, evaluation and close reading. Additional Maths and Computer Science are the usual sticking points, since the tutor who fits either well may live on the far side of Gurgaon. A family in Sector 84, for example, might find that the right Computer Science specialist is based near DLF Phase 2. In that case the sensible split is a nearby tutor at home for Mathematics and the sciences, with the specialist teaching online on a separate evening.

One simple test helps. Ask a combined tutor to go through a recent school test in each subject during the trial and explain where the marks went. If the explanations are sharp in two subjects and vague in the third, give the third to someone else. Distance should never be the reason a child is taught weakly in a subject that counts.
items: Mathematics with Physics and Chemistry is the most natural grouping for one nearby tutor.
Check Biology separately; its wording and data questions need their own confidence.
English and Economics usually need a separate tutor with writing and evaluation skills.
Additional Maths and Computer Science specialists are harder to find nearby, so online often wins.
Test a combined tutor with one recent school paper in each subject.

contentBlocks.heading: School Calendars That Shape Evening Slots in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Most of the pressure on a home tutor's timetable comes from school, not from the exam board. International schools in Gurgaon tend to run long days, and activities, sport fixtures and late buses push the real start of evening study later than the timetable suggests. Schools such as Scottish High International School, Pathways World School, Lancers International School, GD Goenka World School, DPS International Edge and Excelsior American School appear on this page only as local context. IB Gram is not affiliated with any of them, and nothing here describes what a particular school teaches.

The pressure points are predictable in shape even when the dates differ. Grade 9 usually brings the first school assessments set in IGCSE style. Grade 10 brings mocks ahead of the chosen series, whether February/March, May/June or October/November for Cambridge, or January or May/June for Edexcel. Ask the coordinator for mock dates at the start of the year and pass them to the tutor, because a nearby tutor with a full evening diary needs notice to add a second weekly session.

Siblings make this harder. Picture a household in Nirvana Country with a Grade 10 IGCSE student and an older sister in the IB DP. The IGCSE student needs steady past-paper practice through the spring. The DP student has coursework drafts and internal deadlines set by her school, which can peak in the same weeks. One tutor rarely covers both well, because DP subjects need a different specialist. But two tutors arriving on the same evening, back to back, keep the disruption to one stretch of the week.

Holidays cut both ways. A long school break is the best time for a nearby tutor to add catch-up sessions, and the worst time if either your family or the tutor is travelling. Confirm plans before you count on them.
items: Collect the school's mock dates early; nearby tutors need notice to add sessions.
Late buses and sport fixtures move real study time later than the timetable shows.
IGCSE and IB DP siblings usually need different tutors, booked back to back.
Plan holiday catch-up only after both family and tutor confirm travel plans.

contentBlocks.heading: Nearby Tutor, Farther Specialist or Online: Which Fits?
contentBlocks.body:
Choose a nearby tutor at home when one person teaches the subject well and can reach you reliably. Choose online when the right specialist lives far away. Pay for a farther specialist to travel only when the subject truly needs someone beside the student and nobody closer fits. For many families, a hybrid of a nearby home tutor and an online specialist ends up doing the work.

Here is the trade-off in plain terms. A nearby tutor at home is the most dependable option week to week: short travel, fewer cancellations, an easy extra session before mocks, and an adult sitting beside a 15-year-old who might otherwise drift. The weakness is choice. In Sector 69 on the SPR or Sector 109 on Dwarka Expressway, the closest tutor may be a capable generalist rather than an Additional Maths specialist. A farther specialist at home gives you both expertise and presence, but you pay in reliability. One bad evening on Golf Course Extension Road or around Hero Honda Chowk and the lesson starts late, and a travelling tutor may limit how many evenings they will make the journey. Online gives you the widest choice of specialist with no travel risk, but it needs a student who can stay with a screen and a parent who checks the work gets done.

Hybrid is often the honest answer. A family in Sobha City might keep a nearby tutor at home for Mathematics and Chemistry on Tuesdays and Fridays, and book an online Computer Science specialist from across the city for Wednesdays. Another family, looking for an IGCSE tutor near me in Gurgaon for one subject only, might keep home lessons through most of the year and switch to online in weeks when heavy rain makes some roads unreliable.

What does not work is choosing on distance alone. A tutor two towers away who does not know the Extended tier is no bargain.
items: Nearby tutor at home: most reliable and easy to add sessions, but narrower subject choice.
Farther specialist at home: expert and in person, but traffic puts punctuality at risk.
Online specialist: widest choice and no travel, but needs a focused, self-starting student.
Hybrid: nearby tutor for core subjects, online specialist for Additional Maths or Computer Science.

contentBlocks.heading: What Should You Check Before a Tutor Comes Home?
contentBlocks.body:
Check that the tutor's profile has been verified, that they genuinely teach your board and tier, and that the journey from their previous lesson to your gate is realistic on a weekday. IB Gram shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified, but the travel check is one only your family can finish, because only you know your evenings.

Profile verification tells you who the tutor is and what they teach. The demo or trial session is where you confirm the fit. Ask which board and series their recent students sat, and whether those students took Core or Extended papers. Ask how they would use a past paper from your child's syllabus, and listen for syllabus-specific language rather than general exam advice.

Then ask about the evening itself. Find out where the tutor is coming from and which lesson ends just before yours. A tutor who teaches in Sector 43 at five and comes on to Sector 46 for the next slot has a workable plan; the same tutor promising Sector 90 straight afterwards is guessing. Evening diaries tend to fill from the nearest families outward, so a tutor squeezing you in at the end of a long route is a warning sign. Agree in advance what happens when traffic makes them late, whether the lesson runs over, moves online for that evening or is rescheduled.

Home lessons carry their own practical checks. In gated societies, register the tutor with the security desk or the resident app before the first session, so lesson time is not lost at the gate. Keep a parent or another adult at home, at least for the early weeks, and hold lessons at a dining table or study area rather than behind a closed bedroom door. And agree how the tutor will report progress, since you will not always be in the room.
items: Confirm the board, series and tier the tutor last taught, not just 'IGCSE'.
Ask where the tutor's previous lesson ends and how they travel to you.
Agree a late-arrival rule in advance: run over, switch online, or reschedule.
Pre-register the tutor at your society gate or resident app before lesson one.
Keep an adult at home and lessons in a shared space, at least early on.

contentBlocks.heading: How Near Should Your Home IGCSE Tutor in Gurgaon Be?
contentBlocks.body:
Near enough to arrive on time on an ordinary weekday evening, every week, without rushing out of the previous lesson. In practice that usually means the same corridor or a neighbouring one, not a straight-line distance. Sector 50 and Sector 57 look close on a map, yet evening traffic between Sohna Road and Golf Course Extension Road can stretch that short trip badly.

The slots most families want, from late afternoon into the early evening, are the slots every home tutor is asked for. A student back from school needs food and a break first, and a tutor's opening slot usually goes to a family close to where the tutor starts. So a family in DLF Phase 3 or Sector 28 who can offer two or three possible evenings tends to have more nearby options than a family holding out for one fixed hour. Weekend mornings are easier to fill, but an IGCSE course cannot rest on Saturdays alone once Grade 10 mocks approach.

With two or more children, ask for consecutive slots in the same home on the same evening. One nearby tutor teaching IGCSE Mathematics to an older child, then a younger sibling's Middle Years Programme (MYP) Mathematics straight afterwards, saves a second journey and a second gate entry, provided that tutor knows both programmes.

Moving house mid-course is the scenario families underestimate. Say a family moves from Palam Vihar to Sector 106 on Dwarka Expressway halfway through Grade 10. The old tutor may be excellent and still unable to make the new journey reliably. If the exam series is only months away, continuity usually matters more than proximity, so keep the familiar tutor online until the papers are over. If the move comes early in Grade 9, a nearer home tutor is worth the switch, and IB Gram can shortlist one for the new sector. Either way, ask the outgoing tutor for a short handover note listing topics covered, weak areas and past papers attempted, so the new arrangement does not start from zero.
items: Judge distance by evening traffic between corridors, not by the map.
Offering two or three possible evenings widens the choice of nearby tutors.
Siblings: ask for back-to-back slots in the same home on one evening.
Moving during Grade 10: keep the familiar tutor, online, until the series ends.
Moving during Grade 9: switch to a nearer tutor with a written handover note.

contentBlocks.heading: What Progress Looks Like, and When to Change Tutors
contentBlocks.body:
Progress with a home IGCSE tutor shows in habits before it shows in grades. In the first three or four weeks, look for a student who sets out working without being told, keeps an error log and can say why an answer went wrong. Ask the tutor to show you that error log after a fortnight. By the first school test after lessons begin, fewer marks should be lost to careless slips, even if the overall grade has not moved. Grade movement usually comes later, once past-paper practice has built up.

No tutor can guarantee a grade. A tutor can help a Core student become secure within what Core allows, which tops out at grade C, or give an Extended student the practice that makes an A* possible. The result still depends on the student's work between sessions, the tier entered and the paper on the day. Be wary of anyone who promises otherwise.

Starting late narrows what is possible. A student who begins home tuition a few months before the May/June series can still make useful gains in one or two subjects, but spreading those months across four subjects usually helps none of them enough. And some students do not need a tutor at all. A child who is working steadily, getting useful school feedback and scoring comfortably at their tier may need nothing more than a few doubt-solving sessions before mocks.

When there is no progress after a month, separate the causes before changing anything. Late arrivals and cancellations point to a distance problem, which a nearer tutor or a move online can fix. On-time lessons that feel aimless point to a teaching problem, and the answer is to ask for a different match. Families searching for IGCSE tuition near me in Gurugram sometimes swap a good teacher for a closer, weaker one, and lose weeks they cannot spare.
items: Weeks 1-4: working set out unprompted, an error log started, fewer careless slips.
First school test after lessons begin: fewer marks lost to avoidable errors.
Late arrivals or cancellations signal a distance problem; switch closer or online.
On-time but aimless lessons signal a teaching problem; ask for a different match.
No tutor can guarantee a grade, whichever corridor they travel from.

contentBlocks.heading: Starting Home IGCSE Lessons in Your Gurgaon Sector
contentBlocks.body:
Before you send a query, gather a few things. Note the board, syllabus code and tier for each subject; the school's coordinator can confirm them. Find the last two school tests or reports in the subjects that need help. Write down the weekly timetable, including sport, activities and the days the bus runs late. Check how your society or block registers visitors. And list the evenings that are free for every child who needs a tutor, not only the one you are asking about first.

With that in hand, a search for 'home IGCSE tutor in my sector' becomes a precise brief: a Grade 10 Extended Mathematics and Chemistry student in Sector 62, free on Tuesday and Thursday evenings, possibly needing Additional Maths online. Another might read: an IGCSE home tutor near me in Gurgaon for a Core Biology student in Sector 23 who can only manage weekends. IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, level, school calendar, location and schedule, then shortlists verified tutors who match, subject to tutor availability.

The first session, usually the demo or trial, should not be a lecture. A good tutor will ask the student to attempt a few questions from a recent paper, watch how they work and name the habits costing the most marks. Expect the student to feel slightly stretched, not lost. The tutor should agree the weekly slot and a rule for late arrivals, set a small piece of work for next time, and tell you how they will report progress.

Hold that first session at the hour you actually plan to use. If the tutor reaches Ireo Skyon or Vipul Greens comfortably at that time, you have learned something useful. If not, it is better to know now, while an online or hybrid arrangement is still easy to set up. After any change in school timings, test the new slot the same way before assuming the old arrangement still works.
items: Board, syllabus code and tier for each subject, confirmed by the school's coordinator.
Two recent school tests or reports for each subject that needs help.
Timetable with sport, activities and late-bus days clearly marked.
Society name, tower and the visitor registration process at your gate.
Free evenings for every child in the house who needs a tutor.

faqs.question: Will a home IGCSE tutor come to my sector on weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: Usually, in the central corridors, and less predictably in the newer outer sectors, subject to tutor availability. Tutors already teaching in Sushant Lok, South City 1 or the DLF phases often have a workable evening route into neighbouring sectors. In New Gurgaon, along Dwarka Expressway or out towards IMT Manesar, fewer tutors make the trip after school hours. When you ask for an IGCSE tutor near me in Gurgaon, offer two or three possible evenings and name your society, not just the sector.

faqs.question: Does a tutor who travels farther charge more than a nearby one?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, because travel time is part of what a home tutor gives up, but there is no fixed rule and no single figure worth quoting here. Fees vary with the subject, tier, session length and journey. A tutor crossing corridors in evening traffic may price that time in, or simply offer fewer slots. Online lessons take travel out of the sum. Compare fees like for like, for the same subject, tier and session length, and check whether travel is included.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach my IGCSE child and a sibling in the IB Diploma Programme?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, but two tutors usually serve the household better, because IGCSE and the IB DP ask for different expertise even within one subject. A tutor who genuinely fits both is worth keeping, provided the trial covers each child's own syllabus. If the two lessons overlap, plan the space as well as the time: two tutors talking in one living room rarely works, so one child may be better off taking that evening's lesson online in another room. Share both school calendars when you send the query, since each child's busiest weeks can collide.

faqs.question: What if the right Additional Maths or Computer Science tutor lives across Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: Book that specialist online and keep a nearby tutor at home for the other subjects, instead of settling for a closer tutor who is weaker in Additional Maths or Computer Science. Put the online lesson on an evening with no home lesson, so the student is not facing a screen straight after a long session at the table. Let both tutors see the same recent school tests. If the specialist can travel for an occasional weekend session before mocks, subject to availability, the student still gets some in-person time when it counts.

faqs.question: We are moving to another sector mid-course. Do we have to change tutors?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily; it depends on how close the exam series is and whether the current tutor can reach the new address reliably. A move from Sector 49 on Sohna Road to a society in New Gurgaon can turn an easy trip into a long evening drive. After the move, give the current arrangement two weeks at the real slot. If the journey fails and papers are close, keep the same tutor online. If there is time, ask IB Gram for a shortlist near the new address.

faqs.question: Is an online IGCSE tutor a poor second to someone who lives nearby?
faqs.answer: No, not when the online tutor is the stronger match for the subject, though online suits some students better than others. Parents searching for an IGCSE tutor near me in Gurgaon often treat online as the fallback, yet a self-starting student who sets out working neatly tends to adapt within a few sessions. A student who drifts or hides mistakes usually does better with a tutor at the table. If you are unsure, hold a couple of lessons each way, then compare the work actually completed.

faqs.question: The tutor keeps arriving late because of traffic. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Raise it after the second or third late start, and agree a fix with the tutor before asking for someone else. Office traffic around Cyber City or along Golf Course Road can make an early-evening start unrealistic for a tutor coming from another lesson, so try a later slot, a weekend morning or that evening online. Keep a note of actual start times so the conversation stays factual. If nothing holds for a month, ask IB Gram for a different match, ideally closer to your sector.

faqs.question: There has been no progress after a month of home lessons. What now?
faqs.answer: Count the full-length sessions that actually happened before judging the tutor, then look at the work done between them. School events, late starts and a short holiday can shrink a month to a handful of real lessons. If sessions ran in full and the set work was done, ask the tutor for a written plan for the next four weeks and check it matches the tier your child sits. A Core-level plan will not carry an Extended candidate far. If the plan is vague or the tier is wrong, ask IB Gram for a different match.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who lives in our own society a good idea?
faqs.answer: It can be, provided you judge that tutor on subject fit and professionalism rather than the short walk. A tutor in the next tower rarely cancels for traffic and can often add a session before mocks at short notice. The risks are softer. Lessons can drift into casual timings, cancellations become awkward to raise with a neighbour, and changing tutors later can feel personal. Agree the slot, the cancellation notice and how progress will be reported at the start, exactly as you would with anyone else.

faqs.question: Should we wait for a nearby tutor or start online straight away?
faqs.answer: Start online now if the exam series is close or school marks are slipping, and wait for a nearby tutor only when there is time in hand. Early in Grade 9, a few weeks spent waiting for the right home tutor in your corridor costs little. In Grade 10, with mocks approaching, the same wait can cost topics that never get revised. Some families split the difference: they begin online with a tutor who fits and move to home lessons once a suitable evening opens, subject to tutor availability.
