introSummary: IGCSE tuition in Gurgaon works best as a steady weekly routine across Grades 9 and 10, and for many families that routine is IGCSE home tuition: a verified tutor teaching your child at home, in your own sector or society, on the subjects where marks are genuinely being lost. The plan then adjusts term by term as school mocks and the final exam series come closer. This page covers which subjects need tuition, whether one tutor can carry Maths with the sciences, a two-year calendar in plain prose, progress checks worth your attention, and what to change before mocks. It also compares home tuition with online lessons across Golf Course Extension Road, the DLF phases, New Gurgaon and Old Gurgaon. IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform: it shortlists tutors with verified profiles and arranges a demo or trial before you commit.

contentBlocks.heading: How weekly IGCSE tuition in Gurgaon gets matched
contentBlocks.body:
Weekly tuition that runs across Grades 9 and 10 needs a different kind of match from a last-minute rescue before one paper. The tutor has to fit your child's week for two years, not just be good at a single topic. So the first conversation is less about headline credentials and more about the details that decide whether lessons are still happening, calmly, in the fourteenth month.

IB Gram asks which board your child sits, Cambridge IGCSE from Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, the syllabus in each subject that worries you, the tier, and the exam series the school plans to enter. It also asks about the school calendar, your sector or society, and the afternoons that are genuinely free once school timings, sport and travel are counted. From that, it shortlists tutors whose profiles are verified and who match those needs.

Two details change a shortlist more than parents expect. The first is tier. A student on Extended Mathematics needs a tutor at ease with the harder Paper 2 and Paper 4 questions, while a Core candidate needs someone patient with Paper 1 and Paper 3 who can rebuild confidence without rushing. The second is the slot. A tutor free on Tuesday and Thursday evenings may suit a family in DLF Phase 3 and be no use at all to one in Sector 84 whose son finishes football practice late.

Be candid on that first call. If Maths is comfortable and Chemistry is the real worry, say so, because a shortlist built around the wrong subject wastes the first month, and on a two-year course a lost month in Grade 9 has a way of turning up again in Grade 10. And if the fit feels wrong after a few weeks, ask for a different match rather than persisting out of politeness.
items: 1. Send a query or book a free consultation with grade, school and worrying subjects.
2. IB Gram asks about board, syllabus, tier, series, location and realistic weekly slots.
3. It shortlists tutors with verified profiles who match those subjects, tiers and timings.
4. A demo or trial session is arranged before any weekly schedule is fixed.
5. Lessons run at home, online or hybrid, and a different match can be requested.

contentBlocks.heading: Which exam series and tier is Grade 9 and 10 tuition aiming at?
contentBlocks.body:
Tuition should aim at the specific series and tier your child will sit, and both can usually be pinned down with the school early in the course. IGCSE here means Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, normally a two-year course across Grades 9 and 10, and each board has its own series, grading scale and tiers. Confirm yours with the school coordinator before tuition starts.

Cambridge International Education runs series in February/March, May/June and October/November, and the February/March series is offered only in India. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs series in January and May/June. For a tuition plan this matters more than it sounds. A student entered for February/March has a shorter final stretch than a classmate aiming at May/June, so timed past-paper work has to begin earlier in Grade 10. An Edexcel January entry pulls everything forward again.

Grading differs too. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, and some syllabuses have 9-1 versions under different codes. Edexcel International GCSE grades 9-1. Many Cambridge subjects have Core and Extended tiers: Core tops out at grade C, and Extended reaches A*. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1) is tiered Foundation or Higher, with two calculator papers per tier. So a Cambridge tier is also a ceiling, and a weekly tutor needs to know which ceiling a student is working under before setting targets for the term.

What comes after the IGCSE shapes the tuition as well. Students often move on to the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP), A Levels, or CBSE or ISC in Class 11. A student heading for DP or A Level Mathematics gains from tuition that leaves algebra fluent rather than merely exam-ready. Two years of weekly lessons leave room for that longer view. A crash course before the series does not.
items: Cambridge IGCSE series: February/March (India only), May/June and October/November.
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series: January and May/June.
Cambridge grades most syllabuses A*-G; some have 9-1 versions under separate codes.
Cambridge Core tiers top out at grade C, while Extended tiers reach A*.
Edexcel Mathematics A (4MA1): Foundation or Higher tier, two calculator papers each.

contentBlocks.heading: How many IGCSE subjects need tuition, and can one tutor cover several?
contentBlocks.body:
Fewer than most parents first assume. Weekly tuition belongs in the subjects where school marks, homework time or recurring doubts show a real gap, often one to three of them, not across the whole timetable. One tutor can carry Maths with a science or two, especially in Grade 9, but specialists tend to justify themselves in whichever subject carries the most risk by Grade 10.

A useful test: take the last two school assessments in each subject and ask where the lost marks came from. Content the student did not understand needs tuition. Exam technique can often be fixed in a handful of sessions and then left to the student. Careless slips are a habit problem, and weekly tuition is an expensive way to fix a habit. Watch for gaps that masquerade as several subjects. A girl who struggles to rearrange equations in Physics and to handle ratios in Chemistry may really have one Maths gap, and one tutor can close it.

Maths is the anchor for most plans, and IGCSE Maths tuition in Gurgaon is often what other subjects get bundled around. For Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, from the 2025 exams, Core candidates sit Paper 1 (non-calculator) and Paper 3 (calculator), and Extended candidates sit Paper 2 (non-calculator) and Paper 4 (calculator). That non-calculator paper changes the weekly work: arithmetic, fractions and algebra done by hand need steady practice across both years, not a burst in the last term. On Edexcel 4MA1 both papers in each tier are calculator papers, so the emphasis moves towards method and multi-step problems.

Bundling Maths with Physics and Chemistry under one tutor brings one routine, one set of methods for equations and graphs, and one adult who notices when the student is tired. The trade-off is depth. IGCSE science tuition from a specialist, even fortnightly, can sit alongside a Maths tutor when Biology answers need sharper wording. IGCSE English tuition is usually a separate arrangement, because good equation teaching and good essay feedback rarely come from the same person.
items: Tuition belongs where school marks show content gaps, not where a student is merely anxious.
Cambridge 0580 Core, from 2025 exams: Paper 1 non-calculator, Paper 3 calculator.
Cambridge 0580 Extended, from 2025 exams: Paper 2 non-calculator, Paper 4 calculator.
One tutor for Maths with Physics keeps methods consistent across both subjects.
English and Humanities and Business subjects usually suit a separate, writing-focused tutor.

contentBlocks.heading: Cambridge IGCSE tuition across Gurgaon's four corridors
contentBlocks.body:
On Golf Course Extension Road, families in Sector 56, Sector 57, Sector 58, Sector 59, Sector 60, Sector 62 and Sector 65, along with Sushant Lok 3, Ghata and Gwal Pahari, can usually make weekly home tuition work if the slot is fixed early in term. Gated societies such as M3M Golf Estate, Ireo Grand Arch and Ireo Skyon register visitors, so a tutor coming twice a week should be on the approved list, or the start of every lesson goes to intercom calls. Evening traffic on the extension road can stretch a short trip, which makes a tutor already teaching in a neighbouring sector worth a lot.

In DLF Phase 2, DLF Phase 3 and DLF Phase 4, and around MG Road, Cyber City, Sikanderpur, Chakkarpur, Sector 24, Sector 27 and Sector 28, homes sit close together and home tuition is often practical. DLF Beverly Park, Heritage City, DLF Hamilton Court, DLF Regency Park, DLF Richmond Park and Ambience Caitriona each have their own entry routine. The pressure point is office-hour traffic near Cyber City and MG Road, so an earlier weekday slot is easier to keep than one that starts as offices empty.

New Gurgaon takes in Sector 82, Sector 83, Sector 84, Sector 85, Sector 86, Sector 89 and Sector 90, with Kherki Daula and Pataudi Road, and societies such as Vatika India Next and Godrej Air. The sectors are newer and spread out, so the number of tutors able to reach a home every week depends on level and schedule. Here weekly online lessons are often steadier, with a home session before school mocks if someone nearby is available.

Old Gurgaon and Palam Vihar covers Palam Vihar, Civil Lines, Sadar Bazar, Jacobpura, Rajendra Park, Ashok Vihar, Sector 4, Sector 14, Sector 15, Sector 22 and Sector 23. Gate entry is simpler, but parking near the market lanes needs thought. Across Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana, every arrangement stays subject to tutor availability.
items: Golf Course Extension Road societies: put a twice-weekly tutor on the gate list.
DLF Phases 2 to 4: earlier weekday slots dodge the Cyber City evening build-up.
New Gurgaon, Sectors 82 to 90: weekly online lessons plus occasional home sessions.
Old Gurgaon and Palam Vihar: easier entry, but plan parking near Sadar Bazar.
Kherki Daula and Pataudi Road: confirm tutor travel before fixing a weekday evening.

contentBlocks.heading: School terms, mocks and deadlines for Gurgaon IGCSE students
contentBlocks.body:
Gurgaon has a wide spread of international schools, among them Scottish High International School, Pathways World School, Lancers International School, GD Goenka World School, DPS International Edge and Excelsior American School. Each sets its own term dates, assessment weeks and mock timetable, and a weekly tutor has to plan around the calendar your child's school actually publishes, not a generic one. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel.

Some pressures repeat from school to school. Grade 9 can feel gentle for a term and then speed up once topic tests start to count. Grade 10 mocks are set ahead of the series the school has entered, so their timing depends on whether the entry is February/March, May/June or an Edexcel January series. Ask the coordinator for the mock window in the first month of Grade 10 and put it into the tuition plan the same week.

Then come the collisions nobody plans for. Sports fixtures, the Diwali break, winter holidays, school trips and family weddings land in the same months as revision. A tutor working with your child every week for two years should know these dates and move sessions rather than drop them. If a student is travelling for a fortnight, an online lesson from wherever they are keeps the rhythm without much fuss.

Expectations differ between schools as well. Some share clear targets early; others say little until mocks are marked. When school feedback is thin, the tutor's own checks matter more, but they should add to the school's picture, never replace it. Bring the latest report to the first consultation. And ask the school directly whether a tier entry can still change, rather than relying on what other parents in the class have heard.
items: Ask the coordinator for the Grade 10 mock window in the first month of term.
Mark the Diwali break, winter holidays and sports fixtures on the tuition calendar.
Confirm which series your child is entered for before planning final revision.
Share school reports with the tutor so weekly targets match the school's feedback.

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid: what suits a two-year IGCSE plan?
contentBlocks.body:
Start with home tuition if a reliable tutor can reach your sector or society every week, because over two years a tutor at the table catches slips in handwritten working that are easy to miss on a screen. Online is the stronger call when travel is unpredictable or the right specialist is far away. Hybrid, with Maths at home and other subjects online, sits between the two.

Here is the trade-off stated plainly. IGCSE home tuition gives the closest supervision: a home tutor notices a tired student at the end of a long school day, and a fixed arrival time is hard for a teenager to dodge. The cost is travel, which shrinks the pool of tutors and makes cancellations likelier when roads jam. IGCSE online tuition widens the pool, survives rain and traffic, and makes shorter, more frequent sessions possible. It asks more of the student's self-discipline, and handwritten working is harder to check unless it is photographed and shared. Hybrid keeps supervision where it matters and flexibility elsewhere, at the price of a little more coordination.

The right mode can change over the course. A Grade 9 student in Sector 57 might begin with home classes while study habits form, then move one weekly slot online in Grade 10 when school days run longer. A family in Sector 86 who started online might add home sessions in the weeks before mocks, if a tutor is available nearby. In DLF Phase 4 or Palam Vihar, where a tutor may already teach a few streets away, home lessons can stay the default for IGCSE tuition in Gurgaon from start to finish.

Online is not automatically worse for a 14-year-old, and home is not automatically better. The honest test is whether the homework set in one lesson is done before the next. If it is not, change the mode or the tutor before adding sessions. Pick the arrangement that will still be running smoothly in the second year, not the one that feels most reassuring in the first week.
items: Home tuition: closest check on handwritten working, but fewer tutors and traffic-related cancellations.
Online: wider choice of specialists and no travel, but relies on student self-discipline.
Hybrid: Maths at home and other subjects online, with slightly more scheduling to manage.
Review the mode at the start of Grade 10 and again before school mocks.

contentBlocks.heading: How are home tutors checked before weekly lessons begin?
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram shortlists only tutors whose profiles are verified, and before a home tutor starts visiting every week, you check fit for yourself through the demo or trial session. A verified profile is the starting point, not the whole check. The trial, and the first few weeks, tell you whether this person can teach your child's syllabus and tier, reliably, every week for two years.

For a long arrangement, the questions that matter are practical ones. Which syllabus codes and tiers has the tutor taught in recent series, and has that included the board your child sits, since Cambridge and Edexcel papers are built differently? How will the first half-term be planned, and will you see that plan in writing? What happens when the student arrives without homework done? How will progress be reported to you, and how often? A tutor who answers these clearly on day one is far easier to work with in month eighteen.

Agree the working rules before the weekly schedule settles. Cancellation and make-up arrangements need to cover school exam weeks, the Diwali break and family travel, because over two years every one of those will happen. Ask the tutor to keep a simple record of topics covered and questions set, so that if a different match is ever needed, the next tutor is not starting blind.

For home lessons, use a shared room rather than a bedroom, have an adult at home, and register the tutor at the society gate. For online lessons, agree with the tutor whether sessions are recorded and who keeps the recordings. Then look hard at the homework set after the trial. It should be specific to the syllabus, sized for the week and marked properly the following lesson. Vague worksheets with no marking are a sign to ask for someone else.
items: Ask which syllabus codes and tiers the tutor has taught in recent series.
Request a written plan for the first half-term before weekly lessons settle in.
Agree cancellation and make-up rules covering exam weeks, holidays and travel.
For home lessons, use a shared room and register the tutor at the gate.
Check that trial homework is syllabus-specific and properly marked the next lesson.

contentBlocks.heading: A two-year IGCSE tuition calendar for Gurgaon families
contentBlocks.body:
Here is one workable calendar for weekly IGCSE tuition in Gurugram, written for a student who sits a May/June series at the end of Grade 10. If the school enters the Cambridge February/March series or an Edexcel January series, pull every later stage forward to match. In the first three months of Grade 9, keep tuition to the one or two subjects that need it, once a week each, and treat this stretch as diagnosis. The tutor finds out what the student can do without help, starts an error log, and teaches in step with school rather than racing ahead. From roughly month four to month nine, Grade 9 IGCSE tuition does its quiet work: topics are consolidated as school covers them, short past-paper questions on finished topics appear regularly, and you get a considered update about once a month.

The end of Grade 9 needs a proper review. Compare school results with where the student started, drop tuition in any subject that has settled, and add one only if a real gap has opened. The break between grades is for filling specific holes. It is not the time to teach Grade 10 content early unless the tutor and the school both think it sensible.

In the early months of Grade 10, tuition mixes new content with timed questions on finished topics. If the student sits a non-calculator Maths paper, by-hand accuracy gets a few minutes in every lesson. Then comes the run-up to school mocks, whenever the school sets them. Grade 10 IGCSE tuition shifts from teaching to full papers and markscheme-based feedback, and this is the one stretch where a second weekly session in the weakest subject often earns its place.

After mocks comes the biggest adjustment of the two years. The tutor reads the marked scripts, sorts lost marks into content, technique and time pressure, and rebuilds the remaining weeks around the largest loss. The final weeks before the series are mostly timed past papers, with fewer new explanations and shorter, sharper sessions. After the last paper, tuition stops. A short bridge towards DP or A Levels is a separate decision.
items: Grade 9, first three months: diagnosis, an error log, and tuition in step with school.
Grade 9, final term: review each subject and drop or add tuition on evidence.
Grade 10, early months: timed questions on finished topics alongside new content.
Before school mocks: full papers with markscheme feedback, perhaps an extra weekly session.
After mocks: rebuild the final weeks around the biggest source of lost marks.
February/March or Edexcel January entries: pull every later stage forward to match.

contentBlocks.heading: What should progress look like after a term of tuition?
contentBlocks.body:
After one term of weekly tuition you should see fewer repeated mistakes, homework finished with less help, and steadier school test marks in the tutored subject, even if the grade itself has not jumped. Larger movements in grades usually take longer. If none of these signs appear after a full term, something in the plan, the mode or the match needs to change.

A progress check means something only when it compares like with like. Ask the tutor to set a short, timed set of past-paper questions on topics already taught, every four to six weeks, marked strictly against the markscheme, and to keep the scripts. Then look at why marks were lost, not just how many. A student whose Paper 2 errors move from not knowing how to begin to slipping on the final line is making real progress, even if the total barely changes. Topic tests the tutor writes from scratch are harder to compare over time, so past-paper questions from the correct syllabus are the better yardstick.

Parent updates should be short and specific: what was covered, what the student can now do alone, what is still shaky, and what the next four weeks will target. A message after every lesson is less useful than a considered note once a month, plus a conversation before and after school mocks. If updates only ever say the lessons are going well, ask to see the marked scripts. And if the tutor's checks and the school's marks disagree, raise it with both rather than quietly picking one.

Now the limits. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and IGCSE tuition in Gurgaon or anywhere else cannot make up for a student who does nothing between sessions. Starting in the final months of Grade 10 narrows what is possible to technique and a handful of high-value topics. And sometimes the best result of a term is stopping, because the gap has closed.
items: Every four to six weeks: timed past-paper questions on topics already taught.
Keep marked scripts so each check is judged on comparable questions.
Monthly parent note: topics covered, independent skills, weak areas and next focus.
A conversation before and after school mocks to reset the plan.
When tutor checks and school marks disagree, raise it with both.

contentBlocks.heading: Starting IGCSE tuition in Gurgaon this term
contentBlocks.body:
Preparation for the first consultation is simple. Gather the last two school reports, a few recently marked tests in the subjects you are worried about, the syllabus codes if the school has shared them, and the tier each subject is set at for now. Note the series the school intends to enter, even if it is provisional, and list the weekday slots that are genuinely free once school timings, activities and the journey home are counted.

The first session, usually the demo or trial, is mostly diagnosis. Expect the tutor to spend a few minutes with you on the school calendar and what you want from the two years, then work through a mix of questions with your child: some from topics already taught, one or two slightly ahead, and at least one question in exam format under a time limit. Your child should leave with a clear piece of homework, and you should leave with a short note on what the tutor noticed.

Only then fix the weekly schedule. For most Grade 9 students, one session a week per tutored subject is a sensible start, with extra time added later on evidence rather than worry. Families sometimes ask whether IGCSE tuition classes in Gurgaon, or an IGCSE tuition centre in Gurgaon, would be simpler than one-to-one lessons. That format question has its own page on this site, and the calendar and progress advice here applies to either choice.

If you are reading this in the middle of Grade 10, still start. The plan will be shorter and more selective, built around the papers and topics that cost your child the most marks, and the first session can begin with the mock scripts if the school has returned them. Starting late makes the plan narrower. It does not make it pointless, and a focused few months of IGCSE tuition in Gurgaon can still steady a student before the series.
items: Bring two recent school reports and marked tests in the subjects causing concern.
Note syllabus codes, current tiers and the provisional exam series for each subject.
List genuinely free weekday slots after school timings, activities and travel home.
Expect the first session to diagnose, set homework and send you a short note.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week of IGCSE tuition does a Grade 9 or 10 student need?
faqs.answer: One session a week per tutored subject is enough for most of the two years, with a second weekly session in the weakest subject only during the run-up to school mocks and the final series. More than that tends to crowd out homework and school revision, which is where most practice actually happens. If a student needs three sessions a week in one subject just to keep up, the cause is usually a foundation gap, and it is better to spend a few weeks fixing that directly than to keep adding hours.

faqs.question: Should IGCSE tuition start in Grade 9, or can we wait until Grade 10?
faqs.answer: Start in Grade 9 only in subjects where school work already shows a gap, and review everything else at the end of the first term. A small gap is cheap to close early, for example a student who cannot yet manage algebra without a calculator ahead of a non-calculator Maths paper. But paying for tuition in a subject that is going well can teach a student to wait for help. Starting only in Grade 10 is workable, though the plan becomes narrower and leans more heavily on exam technique.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle Maths, Physics and Chemistry for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, provided the tutor is comfortable with each syllabus and tier your child sits. Bundling works well when the difficulties are mostly calculations, graphs and rearranging equations, because one tutor can fix a method once and use it in all three subjects. It works less well when one science needs precise written answers, or when Extended Maths is heading towards DP or A Level Mathematics and deserves a specialist. Review the arrangement at the end of Grade 9 and split it if one subject starts slipping behind.

faqs.question: How much does weekly IGCSE tuition in Gurgaon cost?
faqs.answer: Fees for IGCSE tuition in Gurgaon depend on the subject, tier, grade, lesson mode and number of weekly sessions, so IB Gram discusses them during the consultation rather than quoting one figure. A second weekly session before mocks changes the monthly total, and home and online arrangements are not always charged the same way. When comparing options, think about the likely cost across two years, not a single month. Then decide which subjects genuinely need weekly help before agreeing to tuition in all of them, because that decision affects the total far more.

faqs.question: The tutor is not working out. Can we change in the middle of the year?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can ask IB Gram for a different match whenever the fit is wrong, including mid-year. Before switching, be clear about what is not working, because that shapes the next shortlist. A tutor who is punctual and pleasant but never sets homework is a different problem from one who knows the content but cannot explain it to your son. Share the latest school report and the outgoing tutor's record of topics, so the new tutor starts from where the student is rather than from page one.

faqs.question: Does online IGCSE tuition really work for a 14- or 15-year-old?
faqs.answer: It can, provided the student arrives prepared and the tutor checks written working in every lesson. The weakness of online weekly lessons is drift: camera off, half-finished homework, a phone just out of view. So set rules from the first week, such as working on paper and sharing a photo of each solution, and keep an adult within earshot for the first month. A hybrid plan, with Maths at home and other subjects online, keeps supervision where handwritten method matters most.

faqs.question: We live in Sector 85 in New Gurgaon. Will a tutor come home on weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: It can be arranged, subject to tutor availability for your child's level and schedule: ask for home tuition first, and keep online as the fallback. New Gurgaon's sectors, along with Kherki Daula and Pataudi Road, are spread out, and fewer home tutors can commit to a weekday evening visit every week for two years. Mention your society, such as Vatika India Next or Godrej Air, during the consultation, so that travel is weighed honestly on the shortlist. If the weekly trip is not workable, a pattern that holds up is online lessons every week, with home sessions added around school mocks where a tutor can manage them.

faqs.question: Our society on Golf Course Extension Road restricts visitors. Does that make home tuition difficult?
faqs.answer: No, it just needs setting up once. In societies such as M3M Golf Estate, Ireo Grand Arch or Ireo Skyon, register the tutor with security as a regular visitor so lessons do not begin with calls from the gate. Share the tower, flat number, parking instructions and a contact number before the demo. If entry rules change during the year, tell the tutor early and switch that week's lesson online instead of cancelling it, so the weekly rhythm holds.

faqs.question: It has been a month and school marks have not moved. Is something wrong?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, because a month is usually too early for school marks to shift, though it is long enough to see smaller signs. Look for homework finished with less help, fewer repeats of the same mistake, and a student who can explain a method back to you. If none of these have appeared, ask the tutor for a short written account of what has been covered and what the next four weeks will target. If the answer is vague, consider asking for a different match.

faqs.question: How should tuition change after school mock results come back?
faqs.answer: Mock results should reshape the final weeks, not simply confirm a worry. Give the tutor the marked scripts, not just the grades, and ask for lost marks to be sorted into content not learnt, exam technique and time pressure. Remaining sessions then target the largest category, using past papers from the board and syllabus your child actually sits. A student who lost most marks by not finishing papers needs timed practice more than new teaching. Speak to the school as well, especially if a tier entry is under review.

faqs.question: What changes if the school enters my child for the February/March series?
faqs.answer: Everything in the tuition plan moves earlier than it would for a May/June entry. The February/March series is a Cambridge series offered only in India, and because it falls before May/June, the stretch between school mocks and the real papers is usually shorter and less forgiving. Timed past-paper work should begin sooner in Grade 10, and holiday breaks before the series may need a lighter schedule rather than a full pause. Confirm the entry, and the school's mock dates, with the coordinator before the tutor rebuilds the calendar.

acceptedAnswer.text: Fees for IGCSE tuition in Gurgaon depend on the subject, tier, grade, lesson mode and number of weekly sessions, so IB Gram discusses them during the consultation rather than quoting one figure. A second weekly session before mocks changes the monthly total, and home and online arrangements are not always charged the same way. When comparing options, think about the likely cost across two years, not a single month. Then decide which subjects genuinely need weekly help before agreeing to tuition in all of them, because that decision affects the total far more.

mainEntity.name: The tutor is not working out. Can we change in the middle of the year?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can ask IB Gram for a different match whenever the fit is wrong, including mid-year. Before switching, be clear about what is not working, because that shapes the next shortlist. A tutor who is punctual and pleasant but never sets homework is a different problem from one who knows the content but cannot explain it to your son. Share the latest school report and the outgoing tutor's record of topics, so the new tutor starts from where the student is rather than from page one.

mainEntity.name: Does online IGCSE tuition really work for a 14- or 15-year-old?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can, provided the student arrives prepared and the tutor checks written working in every lesson. The weakness of online weekly lessons is drift: camera off, half-finished homework, a phone just out of view. So set rules from the first week, such as working on paper and sharing a photo of each solution, and keep an adult within earshot for the first month. A hybrid plan, with Maths at home and other subjects online, keeps supervision where handwritten method matters most.

mainEntity.name: We live in Sector 85 in New Gurgaon. Will a tutor come home on weekday evenings?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can be arranged, subject to tutor availability for your child's level and schedule: ask for home tuition first, and keep online as the fallback. New Gurgaon's sectors, along with Kherki Daula and Pataudi Road, are spread out, and fewer home tutors can commit to a weekday evening visit every week for two years. Mention your society, such as Vatika India Next or Godrej Air, during the consultation, so that travel is weighed honestly on the shortlist. If the weekly trip is not workable, a pattern that holds up is online lessons every week, with home sessions added around school mocks where a tutor can manage them.

mainEntity.name: Our society on Golf Course Extension Road restricts visitors. Does that make home tuition difficult?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, it just needs setting up once. In societies such as M3M Golf Estate, Ireo Grand Arch or Ireo Skyon, register the tutor with security as a regular visitor so lessons do not begin with calls from the gate. Share the tower, flat number, parking instructions and a contact number before the demo. If entry rules change during the year, tell the tutor early and switch that week's lesson online instead of cancelling it, so the weekly rhythm holds.

mainEntity.name: It has been a month and school marks have not moved. Is something wrong?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily, because a month is usually too early for school marks to shift, though it is long enough to see smaller signs. Look for homework finished with less help, fewer repeats of the same mistake, and a student who can explain a method back to you. If none of these have appeared, ask the tutor for a short written account of what has been covered and what the next four weeks will target. If the answer is vague, consider asking for a different match.

mainEntity.name: How should tuition change after school mock results come back?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mock results should reshape the final weeks, not simply confirm a worry. Give the tutor the marked scripts, not just the grades, and ask for lost marks to be sorted into content not learnt, exam technique and time pressure. Remaining sessions then target the largest category, using past papers from the board and syllabus your child actually sits. A student who lost most marks by not finishing papers needs timed practice more than new teaching. Speak to the school as well, especially if a tier entry is under review.

mainEntity.name: What changes if the school enters my child for the February/March series?

acceptedAnswer.text: Everything in the tuition plan moves earlier than it would for a May/June entry. The February/March series is a Cambridge series offered only in India, and because it falls before May/June, the stretch between school mocks and the real papers is usually shorter and less forgiving. Timed past-paper work should begin sooner in Grade 10, and holiday breaks before the series may need a lighter schedule rather than a full pause. Confirm the entry, and the school's mock dates, with the coordinator before the tutor rebuilds the calendar.

contentBlocks.heading: How does IB Gram shortlist an IGCSE Class 9 tutor in Gurgaon?
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram builds a Grade 9 shortlist by pinning down the exact course first: Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, the syllabus codes, the tier your child is likely to sit, the school calendar, your sector and the evenings that are genuinely free. Only tutors whose verified profiles fit that picture are shortlisted, and a demo session can be arranged before you commit.

Grade 9 adds a question that later years rarely need: where did your child study Class 8? A student arriving from a CBSE or ICSE school often has the content but not the habits IGCSE papers reward, so the shortlist leans towards tutors whose profiles show experience with that switch, subject to availability. A student from Cambridge Lower Secondary may need sharper exam technique and an early read on Core or Extended instead, so the same subject can need a different tutor.

Before you send the query, dig out the subject options sheet and whatever Grade 9 work has come back so far, including the test your child would rather nobody saw. The Class 8 report helps too. A poor mark is useful. It shows a tutor whether marks were lost on content, on language or on how the answer was set out, and that changes who should teach your child.

Take a student in Sector 50 who scored well in Class 8 Maths and then lost most of the marks on her first Grade 9 test because the working was missing. Her request is not simply for a Maths tutor. It is for an IGCSE Grade 9 Maths tutor who can rebuild written method without re-teaching topics she already knows, who can reach Sohna Road on a weekday evening or teach online, and who understands the Extended papers she hopes to sit. If the first match does not suit her, the family can ask for a different one; that is part of the process, not a complaint.

2. IB Gram asks about board, syllabus codes, likely tier, Class 8 background and school calendar.

contentBlocks.heading: Grade 9 subject choices and the Class 11 routes they keep open
contentBlocks.body:
In Gurgaon, IGCSE means one of two qualifications: Cambridge IGCSE from Cambridge International Education, or the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. Both are usually taught as a two-year course across Grades 9 and 10, and students often move on to the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP), to A Levels, or to CBSE or ISC in Class 11. Cambridge grades most syllabuses from A* to G, though some have 9-1 versions under different codes, while Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1.

That spread of routes is why the options form, whenever your school hands it out, deserves more than an evening's thought. The subjects chosen for Grade 9 are usually the subjects your child sits at the end of Grade 10. How many subjects a student takes is largely set by the school, so ask the coordinator about the usual load before adding one more to look ambitious; each extra subject adds two years of papers, homework and revision.

Each Class 11 route reads Grade 9 choices differently. A student leaning towards the IB DP should ask the intended DP school which IGCSE subjects and grades it looks at. For A Levels in Mathematics or the sciences, the safer course is to keep those subjects and, where a Cambridge subject is tiered, protect the Extended route while the evidence supports it. And a student who may move to CBSE or ISC in Class 11 should check how that school looks at IGCSE subjects when it allots streams, because a science dropped now can close a stream later.

A familiar dilemma goes like this: a student enjoys Computer Science and Business, finds Chemistry heavy and wants to drop it. If medicine, engineering or any science stream is still a possibility, have that conversation with the school before the form goes in. IGCSE subject choices help most when made with Class 11 in view, not around a favourite teacher or a friend's options.
items: Confirm whether each subject is Cambridge or Edexcel, since grade scales differ.
Keep Mathematics and the sciences if A Levels or a science stream is possible.
Before choosing, ask your intended Class 11 school which IGCSE subjects it considers.
Spend tuition on the weak subject Class 11 needs, not the comfortable favourite.

contentBlocks.heading: Core or Extended IGCSE: who decides, and when?
contentBlocks.body:
In practice the school usually decides Core or Extended, and timing varies from school to school, so ask the coordinator when tiers are finalised and which assessments count. The evidence starts building in Grade 9. What is at stake is the ceiling: in tiered Cambridge subjects, Core tops out at grade C, while Extended reaches A*.

The papers show why the decision matters. In Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, from the 2025 exams, Core candidates sit Paper 1 (non-calculator) and Paper 3 (calculator), and Extended candidates sit Paper 2 (non-calculator) and Paper 4 (calculator). The Cambridge sciences examined from 2023 split in a similar way: Paper 1 multiple choice for Core or Paper 2 for Extended, Paper 3 theory for Core or Paper 4 for Extended, plus a practical component through Paper 5 (practical test) or Paper 6 (alternative to practical), chosen by the school. Multiple choice carries 30%, theory 50% and practical 20%.

Pearson Edexcel works differently. Its International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1) is tiered Foundation or Higher, with two calculator papers in each tier, while its sciences are untiered, with Paper 1 and Paper 2 for the separate sciences and practical skills assessed inside the written papers. So for an Edexcel student, only Maths among these subjects carries a tier decision.

Watch patterns rather than one test score. A borderline student usually handles routine questions but stalls on longer, unfamiliar ones, loses the thread of multi-step algebra or writes vague science answers. That is where Grade 9 tutoring earns its place. But Extended is not automatically right: a student entered without secure foundations can spend Grade 10 losing confidence on questions built for a higher ceiling. Talk to the school early, share what it says with the tutor, and remember that a Core entry caps the grade at C, which may matter if a Class 11 school sets grade expectations for that subject.
items: 0580 from 2025: Core sits Papers 1 and 3; Extended sits Papers 2 and 4.
Cambridge science weighting: multiple choice 30%, theory 50%, practical 20%.
Edexcel 4MA1 has Foundation and Higher tiers; Edexcel sciences are untiered.
For Grade 9 IGCSE English, confirm the exact syllabus code with the school.

contentBlocks.heading: What your Gurgaon sector means for Grade 9 home lessons
contentBlocks.body:
Across Gurugram (Gurgaon), Haryana, Grade 9 families face the same squeeze: after school and homework, the only free window is the early evening, when roads are slowest. The Sohna Road corridor takes in Sector 47, Sector 48, Sector 49 and Sector 50, Nirvana Country, South City 2, Rosewood City, Uppal Southend, Vatika Chowk and Badshahpur. Home lessons work well here when the tutor already lives or teaches nearby, while evening traffic around Vatika Chowk can stretch a short trip for anyone coming from farther away. In gated societies such as Central Park Resorts, Orchid Petals, Vatika City, Malibu Towne, Vipul Greens and The Close, register the tutor's details with security before the first session so lessons do not start late at the gate.

Golf Course Extension Road covers Sector 56, Sector 57, Sector 58, Sector 59, Sector 60, Sector 62 and Sector 65, along with Sushant Lok 3, Ghata and Gwal Pahari. In societies such as M3M Golf Estate, Ireo Grand Arch and Ireo Skyon, home lessons are comfortable once gate entry is sorted. But if your child's afternoons are full of school activities or sport, weekday online sessions with a weekend home lesson may fit better.

Dwarka Expressway families, in Sector 102, Sector 103, Sector 104, Sector 106, Sector 108, Sector 109, Sector 110 and Sector 113, and in societies such as Godrej Summit, Sobha City and ATS Kocoon, face a different trade-off. Depending on tutor availability, the right Grade 9 science or Maths specialist may not live within an easy evening drive, and a long commute for a single lesson rarely survives a full term. Online is often the better weekday call on this corridor, with an in-person session added before school test weeks if a suitable tutor is within reach.

Ask for the slot before you ask for the tutor. A strong match who can only reach Sector 109 at half past eight on a school night is not a match for a tired fourteen-year-old.
items: Sohna Road societies such as Malibu Towne: register the tutor with security first.
Golf Course Extension Road: weekday online for doubts, weekend home session for writing.

contentBlocks.heading: The Grade 9 school year at international schools in Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Gurgaon has a wide spread of international schools, among them Scottish High International School, Pathways World School, Lancers International School, GD Goenka World School, DPS International Edge and Excelsior American School, and each sets its own calendar, programmes and assessment rules. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Nothing here describes what a particular school offers; check the details with your own coordinator.

For IGCSE families, Grade 9 is rarely the quiet warm-up year it is sometimes taken for. The first term brings new subject teachers, a new question style and the first unit tests, often before a student has worked out what the teachers expect. Then come term or mid-year exams, and at some schools an end-of-year exam whose results feed conversations about tiers or subject changes. Ask your school whether that applies, because it changes how seriously the last months of Grade 9 should be treated.

School tests are the most useful Grade 9 evidence a family has, and many stay in a school bag, unread. Keep every returned test and read the teacher's comments with your child. If a Physics test lost marks for missing units, or an English piece lost them for answering a different question from the one set, that tells a tutor exactly where to start. A good tutor follows the school's scheme of work instead of racing ahead, so that tuition supports the next unit test rather than competing with it.

The exam series itself feels distant in Grade 9, but it sets the clock. Cambridge runs series in February/March (offered only in India), May/June and October/November, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs January and May/June series. Once you know which series your child's school uses, you know how many months Grade 9 really has to lay foundations before attention moves to past papers.
items: Get the Grade 9 scheme of work so tutoring follows the school's topic order.
Mark unit tests and end-of-year exams on a family calendar early.
Ask whether Grade 9 end-of-year results feed into tier or subject decisions.
Confirm which exam series the school uses before planning Grade 10 revision.

contentBlocks.heading: Should Grade 9 IGCSE lessons in Gurgaon be at home, online or hybrid?
contentBlocks.body:
For a Grade 9 IGCSE student in Gurgaon, choose by subject and by evening. Home lessons suit Maths and science when a tutor needs to watch working on paper; online suits a focused student whose best-matched tutor lives across the city; hybrid suits families who want close supervision without daily travel on school nights.

An IGCSE Class 9 home tutor sits beside the student and sees the pencil move. That matters in the first year, when habits are still forming: skipped working on a non-calculator question, a unit left off a Physics answer, a graph with an uneven scale. The trade-off is travel. A home tutor has to reach your society at the hour you need, and on a weekday evening along Sohna Road or Golf Course Extension Road that narrows the choice of who can come.

An IGCSE Class 9 online tutor removes the commute and widens the choice, which matters most when the right science or Maths specialist is on the other side of Gurgaon. It works well for a self-directed student, and for short doubt-solving sessions the night before a unit test. It works poorly for a student who drifts off camera or keeps mistakes in a notebook the tutor never sees. Ask for written work to be photographed or shared on screen in every session; without that, online Grade 9 lessons turn into listening rather than practising.

Hybrid is often the practical middle for Grade 9: a home session at the weekend to build written habits, and a shorter online session midweek for practice and doubts. For a Grade 9 IGCSE student, the trade-off is plain: home lessons give the closest supervision but the narrowest choice of tutors and the most scheduling friction; online lessons give the widest choice and no travel but depend on the student's focus; hybrid balances the two but needs a tutor willing to teach both ways, subject to availability.
items: Home: best for watching written working, graphs and diagrams as they happen.
Online: widest tutor choice and no travel, but needs a focused student.
Hybrid: weekend home session plus a shorter online midweek session for doubts.
Modes can change by term as school timings and activities change.

contentBlocks.heading: How are Grade 9 tutors checked, and what should you check yourself?
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram shortlists only tutors whose profiles are verified and match the board, syllabus, tier and schedule you describe. Your own checks still matter, and the demo session is where to make them: see whether the tutor asks for the syllabus code, knows how the Grade 9 course leads into the papers and teaches at your child's level.

Give any IGCSE Class 9 tutor in Gurgaon something real to work with in the demo: a Grade 9 test your child found hard. A good sign is a tutor who reads the lost marks before teaching anything, separates content gaps from presentation gaps and asks which tier the school is leaning towards. A weaker sign is a prepared topic lecture, or talk of Grade 10 exam tricks before anyone has checked the Grade 9 foundations. Watch your child too: a fourteen-year-old who is asking questions by the end of the demo is usually a better sign than a polished explanation.

Ask which syllabus codes the tutor has taught, and how they would handle a student from CBSE who writes correct answers with no working. Find out what update you will get after the first four sessions. Then check one detail that separates current knowledge from old notes: from the 2025 exams, Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 includes a non-calculator paper for both Core and Extended candidates. A Grade 9 tutor who plans only around calculator practice is working from an out-of-date picture.

Check that the tutor who arrives or logs in is the person on the shortlisted profile. For home lessons, keep an adult at home and agree timings and cancellations before the first week. If the fit is wrong, say so early. You can ask IB Gram for a different match, and changing tutors in the first term of Grade 9 does far less damage than changing one a few months before the exams.
items: Bring a real Grade 9 test to the demo and watch how it is diagnosed.
Check the tutor knows 0580's non-calculator Paper 1 and Paper 2 from 2025.
Agree the progress update you will receive after the first four sessions.
For home sessions, keep an adult at home and share gate entry details.

contentBlocks.heading: From CBSE or ICSE Class 8 to IGCSE: the skills Grade 9 papers demand
contentBlocks.body:
Moving from CBSE to IGCSE Class 9, or from ICSE, is usually less about new content than about a new way of earning marks. Some early topics in Maths and science may look familiar. What changes is what a good answer looks like: full working, a response shaped by the exact question word and precise science explanations. Top Class 8 students can find this unsettling for a term.

Four habits deserve attention from the first week. Showing working comes first: Grade 9 teachers expect every step, and a bare answer that turns out wrong leaves nothing to give credit for. Number work without a calculator is next, since both 0580 tiers include a non-calculator paper from the 2025 exams. Then there is reading the question word: describing a trend and explaining it are two different tasks. Last, a student has to reason through an experiment on paper, because practical work carries 20% of the Cambridge science assessment through Paper 5 or Paper 6.

No two switchers struggle in the same place. One student from ICSE may write fluent explanations and still lose Maths marks on presentation; another from CBSE may be quick with calculations and stuck on a three-line science answer. Students who came through Cambridge Lower Secondary may already know the question style, so their adjustment is different: the pace of an examined two-year course, the first brush with tiers and revising for tests that start to count.

Consider a student in South City 2 who wrote excellent one-line answers in Class 8 Science at a CBSE school. His first Grade 9 Biology test came back with half marks on questions he understood, because each answer stopped one step short of an explanation. He did not need the topics re-taught. He needed a few weeks of writing, checking against the question and rewriting. That is the kind of gap an IGCSE Class 9 tutor in Gurgaon should find in the first session, not the fifth.
items: Show full working, even on questions that felt obvious in Class 8.
Practise arithmetic without a calculator every week from the first term.
Write science answers that finish the explanation instead of stopping one step short.
Reason through experiments on paper, not just remember what happened in class.

contentBlocks.heading: Foundations to secure in Grade 9, and signs that progress is real
contentBlocks.body:
Grade 10 has little room to teach the basics again. Whatever order a school follows, later IGCSE Maths and science work leans on a small set of foundations, which are also the fairest test of whether Grade 9 tuition is working.

In Maths, the foundation is algebra that holds up under pressure: expanding and factorising, solving linear equations, rearranging formulae and working with indices. Next comes confident number work with fractions, percentages, ratio and standard form, done by hand, and accurate reading and drawing of graphs. An IGCSE Grade 9 Maths tutor who keeps returning to these is not being slow. A student who cannot rearrange a formula in Grade 9 will meet that weakness again in every later topic that uses one.

An IGCSE Grade 9 science tutor should be building similar foundations: the particle model, atomic structure and balanced equations in Chemistry; cells and the idea of transport in Biology; and in Physics, the habit of writing the equation, substituting values with units and rearranging. Across all three sciences, graph work and the language of experiments, such as variables, fair tests and repeat readings, carry straight into practical work.

Progress should show within a term, not a week. In the first month, look for fewer marks lost on presentation: working shown, units written, the question actually answered. By the end of the first term, your child should be attempting the longer questions instead of leaving them blank. By the end-of-year exams, any Core or Extended conversation should rest on evidence. Some gaps take longer: two years of avoided algebra will not close in one term. No tutor can guarantee a grade or an Extended entry, and one who promises either is a warning sign. If a month of regular sessions changes nothing, review the plan with the tutor first, then ask IB Gram for a different match if the fit is the problem.
items: Algebra: expand, factorise, solve linear equations and rearrange formulae unprompted.
Number: fractions, percentages, ratio and standard form, confidently done by hand.
Sciences: units in every answer, balanced equations and properly labelled graphs.
First month: fewer marks lost on working, units and misread questions.

contentBlocks.heading: How much tuition does a Grade 9 student in Gurgaon actually need?
contentBlocks.body:
Some Grade 9 IGCSE students need no tutor at all, and those who do rarely need one for every subject. A switcher from CBSE or ICSE, a borderline Extended candidate or a student losing marks on technique tends to be well served by one or two focused sessions a week in the weakest subject.

More tuition is not better in Grade 9. A student with separate tutors for Maths, Chemistry and Physics, on top of a full school day and homework, has no time left for the independent practice that actually moves marks. Tuition should not replace homework either; a tutor who ends up doing assignments is covering the gap, not closing it. Start with the subject where the evidence is weakest, review after a term, and add a second only when the first is stable. If school tests are sound and your child is coping, first-year IGCSE support can be as light as a check-in before each test block, or nothing at all.

Once a tutor is chosen, the first regular session should set the frame for the term. The tutor and student go through the school's scheme of work for the coming weeks, start a simple log of repeated mistakes and agree one or two targets, such as full working on every Maths question or units on every Physics answer. The tutor should also ask when the next unit test falls, so the first month builds towards it. You should come away knowing how progress will be reported and when the plan will next be reviewed.

To find an IGCSE Class 9 tutor in Gurgaon, send a query or book a free consultation with IB Gram. Before the call, have the syllabus codes, the tier the school is considering, your sector, your free evenings and the latest school test to hand. Nothing needs to be decided for the whole year on day one.
items: 1. Gather the options sheet, Class 8 report and every returned Grade 9 test.
2. Diagnose in the demo: sort lost marks into content, technique and language.
3. Agree one or two monthly targets, such as full working in Maths.
4. Follow the school's scheme of work, with weekly practice on weak foundations.
5. Review each term against school tests, then continue, refocus or stop tuition.

faqs.question: Is Grade 9 too early to start IGCSE tuition?
faqs.answer: It is not too early if there is a specific gap to close, but it is unnecessary if tuition is only there to feel safe. Grade 9 is the easiest point to fix missing working, weak algebra or vague science answers, because no final paper is riding on them yet. Start Class 9 IGCSE tuition in Gurugram when school tests show a repeated problem, and set a term-end review so lessons do not continue out of habit.

faqs.question: My child is moving from CBSE to IGCSE in Class 9. What should the first term focus on?
faqs.answer: The first term should focus on how IGCSE answers earn marks, not on racing through content. Ask for the Grade 9 scheme of work, keep every returned test and look for the pattern: missing working, answers that ignore the question word, science explanations that stop short. Any tutoring should work on those habits alongside the current school unit. A family in Rosewood City or Sector 57 might add one weekend session for the first term only, then review.

faqs.question: Can we push for Extended if the school recommends Core?
faqs.answer: You can ask the school to explain its recommendation and what evidence would change it, but the school usually makes the final call. Find out which assessments count and when tiers are finalised, then give your child a fair run at producing that evidence in school tests. If it is still missing when tiers are set, a well-prepared Core entry is often a better result than an anxious Extended one, despite the grade C ceiling.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring really work for Grade 9 Maths and science?
faqs.answer: It works for most Grade 9 Maths and science theory, provided the tutor sees the student's written working in every session. The weak point online is checking rather than explaining, because a tutor who only hears answers misses skipped steps and missing units. Hands-on practical skills are harder to build through a screen. For a family in Sector 104 or Sobha City on Dwarka Expressway, online may widen the choice of tutor enough to justify that trade-off, subject to availability.

faqs.question: The home tutor is not working out. Can we change after a few sessions?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can ask IB Gram for a different match whenever the fit is wrong, and in Grade 9 it is better to ask early. Say exactly what is not working, because it shapes the next shortlist: re-teaching topics your child already knows, pitching at Grade 10 too soon, arriving late through evening traffic or simply not connecting with a fourteen-year-old. A change in the first term costs little momentum; waiting until the year-end exams costs far more.

faqs.question: We have had a month of tuition and see no progress. What now?
faqs.answer: Review the plan before blaming the tutor or your child, because a month shows early signs but not full results. Check whether sessions targeted the marks your child was actually losing, whether practice happened between sessions and whether recent school tests covered what the tutor taught. If sessions were generic, ask for them to be rebuilt around returned tests. If they were targeted and practice happened but nothing moved, ask IB Gram for a different match.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor reach Sector 108 or Sector 113 on weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, subject to tutor availability, but a weekday evening slot on Dwarka Expressway can be hard to fill with the right Grade 9 specialist. A tutor based nearby can make it work; one travelling from Sohna Road may struggle to keep it up for a term. One workable arrangement is an online session midweek and a home session at the weekend. For home visits, share the gate process at ATS Kocoon, Godrej Summit or your own society in advance.

faqs.question: Should my child study Grade 10 topics ahead during Grade 9?
faqs.answer: Usually not, because Grade 9 time is better spent securing foundations than previewing harder topics built on them. A student who races ahead with shaky algebra carries the same errors into every new topic, and school tests keep exposing them. Working ahead suits a student whose school tests are consistently strong and who wants a challenge, and even then it should run alongside the school's scheme of work. Full past-paper drilling can wait until Grade 10.

contentBlocks.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel, Core or Extended: fit comes before fame
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE in Gurgaon usually means one of two boards, and the tutor has to be fluent in the one your child sits. Cambridge IGCSE, from Cambridge International Education, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE both usually run as two-year courses across Grades 9 and 10, but they differ in grading, tiers and exam series. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, with some subjects offered in 9-1 versions under different syllabus codes. Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1. A tutor who talks about "getting an A*" to an Edexcel student has already told you something.

Tier is where "best" starts to depend on the student. Many Cambridge subjects have Core and Extended tiers: Core tops out at grade C, while Extended reaches A*. Edexcel's Mathematics A is tiered Foundation or Higher. A student entered for Core needs a tutor who builds secure method and confidence, and who can tell you honestly whether a move to Extended is realistic. A student already on Extended and chasing the top grade needs someone who finds the marks that leak away through imprecise working. Those are different skills, and few tutors are equally strong at both.

Series is the third thing to pin down. Cambridge runs exam series in February/March, a series offered only in India, as well as May/June and October/November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE series run in January and May/June. A tutor preparing a student for the March series works to an earlier deadline than one aiming at May/June, so past-paper revision has to begin sooner. Ask any tutor you are considering which series their recent students sat, and listen for specifics.

Keep Class 11 in view too. IGCSE is often followed by the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP), A Levels, or a move to CBSE or ISC. A student heading for the IB DP needs a tutor who teaches firmly to the IGCSE papers while keeping algebra and written explanation sharp for what comes next.
items: Board: Cambridge IGCSE grades most syllabuses A*-G; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades 9-1.
Tier: Cambridge Core tops out at grade C, while Extended reaches A*.
Edexcel Mathematics A (4MA1): Foundation or Higher tier, two calculator papers per tier.
Cambridge series: February/March (India only), May/June and October/November.
Edexcel International GCSE series: January and May/June.

contentBlocks.heading: Paper-level fluency to test in IGCSE Maths, sciences and English
contentBlocks.body:
Maths is where subject fluency is easiest to test, because the paper structure is specific. For Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, from the 2025 exams, Core candidates sit Paper 1 (non-calculator) and Paper 3 (calculator), while Extended candidates sit Paper 2 (non-calculator) and Paper 4 (calculator). An IGCSE Maths home tutor worth hiring knows this without checking, and has a plan for the non-calculator paper, starting with the written methods many students quietly stopped using years ago. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1) works differently, with two calculator papers per tier at Foundation or Higher.

Sciences need a different test. Many Cambridge subjects have Core and Extended tiers, so an IGCSE science home tutor should confirm the tier and the syllabus code before planning anything. Then watch how they use past papers. A strong tutor chooses questions by topic, marks the student's answer against the mark scheme with the student watching, and shows exactly which word or step earned or lost the mark. A weak one reads model answers aloud. Ask a candidate tutor to mark one answer from your child's last school test in front of you.

English and Additional Mathematics catch families out in opposite ways. With English, the problem is identification: ask the school exactly which English syllabus and code the student is entered for, because a tutor who prepares students well for one English paper may be little help with another. With Additional Mathematics, the problem is assumption. Strength in 0580 Extended does not prove a tutor teaches Additional Mathematics well, so ask separately, and ask them to talk you through a question they taught recently.

One test works across every subject. Hand the tutor a past-paper question your child got wrong and ask what they would do with it in the next half hour. The answer tells you more than a CV.
items: Cambridge 0580 Core: Paper 1 non-calculator and Paper 3 calculator, from the 2025 exams.
Cambridge 0580 Extended: Paper 2 non-calculator and Paper 4 calculator, from the 2025 exams.
Sciences: the tutor confirms tier and syllabus code before choosing any past-paper questions.
Additional Mathematics: ask for recent, specific teaching experience, not general Maths strength.
